title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄序
萬曆己卯天下復當賓士于
鄉江西則巡按御史邵陞寔
監臨之先期戒事有司奉規
畫惟恪馳禮幣聘四方文學
博□□則以樓雲與敎諭趙
□□為試官學正翁大賓
===
敎諭朱孔昭李四維陳公大
樊大通陶□皐訓導余光先
林維翰張思明史著勳為同
考試官提調則右布政使張
大忠左參議吳與言監試則
副使王世懋蕭廩簾內外執
事咸集相與協誠毖劼合提
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄序
萬曆己卯，天下復當賓士于鄉，江西則巡按御史邵陞寔監臨之。先期戒事，有司奉規畫惟恪，馳禮幣聘四方文學博□□，則以樓雲與敎諭趙□□為試官，學正翁大賓、敎諭朱孔昭、李四維、陳公大、樊大通、陶□皐、訓導余光先、林維翰、張思明、史著勳為同考試官。提調則右布政使張大忠、左參議吳與言，監試則副使王世懋、蕭廩。簾內外執事咸集，相與協誠毖劼，合提
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the jimao year of the Wanli era [1579], the empire was once again due to welcome scholars as guests at the provincial level. In Jiangxi, Regional Inspector Shao Sheng 邵陞 served as Supervising Official. Prior to the scheduled date, preparations were ordered, and the authorities carried out the plans with utmost diligence. Messengers were dispatched with ceremonial gifts to invite men of wide learning and literary attainment [?] from all quarters. Thus, Lou Yun 樓雲 [?] and County Director of Studies Zhao [][] 趙□□ were appointed as Examiners; Subprefectural Director of Studies Weng Dabin 翁大賓, County Directors of Studies Zhu Kongzhao 朱孔昭, Li Siwei 李四維, Chen Gongda 陳公大, Fan Datong 樊大通, and Tao []gao 陶□皐, and Assistant Instructors Yu Guangxian 余光先, Lin Weihan 林維翰, Zhang Siming 張思明, and Shi Zhuxun 史著勳 were appointed as Associate Examiners. Serving as Proctors were Right Administration Commissioner Zhang Dazhong 張大忠 and Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Wu Yuyan 吳與言; serving as Surveillance Officials of the Examination were Surveillance Vice Commissioners Wang Shimao 王世懋 and Xiao Lin 蕭廩. The functionaries both inside and outside the curtain all assembled, working together in sincere harmony and cautious diligence, and gathered the…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
學副使江以東所選士三千
有奇鎖院三試之遵
制額拔其雋九十五人幷錄其
文以
獻接雲循例當有序序曰夫江
右夙稱名勝矣自彭蠡旣豬
決然爲東南鉅觀而匡廬之
綿亘岑嶔乃與衡岳岱宗爭
雄而鼎峙地靈人傑自古記
之接雲應聘而來驅車潯陽
下柴桑故里是五柳先生所
居也指顧螺川式九賢祠則
六一居士爲之領袖比頓轡
洪都訪徐孺子廢宅陳蕃之
punctuated: 學副使江以東所選士三千有奇，鎖院三試之。遵制額，拔其雋九十五人，幷錄其文以獻。接雲循例當有序。序曰：夫江右夙稱名勝矣。自彭蠡旣豬，決然爲東南鉅觀，而匡廬之綿亘岑嶔，乃與衡岳、岱宗爭雄而鼎峙。地靈人傑，自古記之。接雲應聘而來，驅車潯陽，下柴桑故里，是五柳先生所居也；指顧螺川，式九賢祠，則六一居士爲之領袖；比頓轡洪都，訪徐孺子廢宅，陳蕃之
translation_en:
… more than three thousand scholars selected by Assistant Surveillance Commissioner for Education Jiang Yidong 江以東, locked the examination compound, and tested them in three sessions. In accordance with the imperially decreed quota, ninety-five of the most outstanding candidates were selected, and their essays have been compiled to be presented to the Throne. Following precedent, I, [Ouyang] Jieyun 接雲, ought to provide a preface.

The preface reads: Jiangxi (Jiangyou 江右) has long been renowned for its famous sights. Ever since Lake Pengli 彭蠡 [Poyang Lake] was diked and contained, it has decidedly stood as a grand spectacle of the southeast; meanwhile, the continuous and towering peaks of Mount Kuanglu 匡廬 [Mount Lu] vie for supremacy with the Southern Marchmount Heng 衡岳 and Mount Tai 岱宗, standing like the three legs of a tripod. That sacred topography brings forth outstanding people has been recorded since antiquity. Coming in response to the invitation to serve, I drove my carriage through Xunyang 潯陽 and went down to the old village of Chaisang 柴桑, which was where Master Five Willows (Wuliu Xiansheng 五柳先生, i.e., Tao Yuanming 陶淵明) once lived. Looking out toward Luochuan 螺川 [Ji'an], I paid respects from my carriage at the Shrine of the Nine Worthies (Jiuxian Ci 九賢祠), among whom the Retired Scholar of Six Ones (Liuyi Jushi 六一居士, i.e., Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修) stands as the leader. When I halted my reins in Hongdu 洪都 [Nanchang], I visited the ruined residence of Xu Ruzi 徐孺子 [Xu Zhi 徐穉], where the couch of Chen Fan 陳蕃…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
榻隱映在懸已復凝睇鵞湖
山中非陸九淵氏故所講業
處乎竊謂數君子者振起一
代播譽汗青燁然爲山川增
重顧或匿踪蓬蓽或堙抑下
僚或肩鉅乗巍矣而設施靡
竟蓋遭時遇主若斯之難也
===
爾諸士戴纚垂纓而譚往昔
無論數君子所值即悉數黃
虞而下稱盛際者詎有如
今日哉我
國家布功令羅才儁黌序通一
經以上者咸得籍進有司一
儋爵效官當於名實則臚仕
punctuated:
榻隱映在懸；已復凝睇鵞湖山中，非陸九淵氏故所講業處乎？竊謂數君子者，振起一代，播譽汗青，燁然爲山川增重。顧或匿踪蓬蓽，或堙抑下僚，或肩鉅乗巍矣而設施靡竟，蓋遭時遇主若斯之難也。
爾諸士戴纚垂纓而譚往昔，無論數君子所值，即悉數黃、虞而下稱盛際者，詎有如今日哉？我國家布功令，羅才儁，黌序通一經以上者，咸得籍進有司；一儋爵效官，當於名實，則臚仕
translation_en:
…couch still seems faintly suspended there. And then, gazing intently into the mountains of Ehu, is that not the place where Lu Jiuyuan 陸九淵 formerly lectured and taught? In my humble view, these several worthies roused an entire age, spread their renown across the pages of history, and brilliantly added weight and glory to the mountains and rivers. Yet some hid their tracks behind gates of bramble and wicker, some were buried and held down in lowly minor posts, and some, though shouldering great responsibilities and occupying exalted positions, were unable to bring their measures to full completion—so difficult is it, indeed, to meet with the right times and encounter an appreciative ruler!

As you scholars, wearing hair-wraps and trailing cap-strings, discourse upon the past, leaving aside what those several worthies encountered, even if you were to count in full all the eras praised as flourishing from the Yellow Emperor and Yu Shun downward, how could any compare with today? Our dynasty promulgates the regulations governing examination and official advancement to gather in men of talent and distinction, so that in the state schools all who master one Classic or more may have their names registered and be advanced to the authorities; once they receive rank and serve in office, if their performance matches their title and reality, then distinguished advancement…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
厚禄若揭而踵其後士振奮
翔騰所由來尚已
皇上
睿聖天授籲俊
右文迺益深陶而厚植之廓登
進之途詳覈實之法幽枼眢
昧者悉耀于光明顧猶
===
宵旰憂勤亹亹以遺賢爲慮此
千載一時也今天下士波湧
林立雷動雲蒸罔弗爭自濯
磨蘄上應
雍煕之會矧兹邦故足文獻甲
于四方者乎諸士往矣懸黎
結綠剖璞而陳鏌鋣干將發
punctuated: 厚禄，若揭而踵其後。士振奮翔騰，所由來尚已。皇上睿聖天授，籲俊右文，迺益深陶而厚植之，廓登進之途，詳覈實之法，幽枼眢昧者，悉耀于光明。顧猶宵旰憂勤，亹亹以遺賢爲慮，此千載一時也。今天下士波湧林立，雷動雲蒸，罔弗爭自濯磨，蘄上應雍煕之會；矧兹邦故足文獻，甲于四方者乎？諸士往矣，懸黎、結綠，剖璞而陳；鏌鋣、干將，發
translation_en: …and generous emoluments follow right at their heels, as if held aloft. That scholars have been roused to soar aloft has thus had a long history. His Majesty, endowed by Heaven with sagely wisdom, summons men of talent and esteems civil culture. Thereupon he has all the more deeply molded and richly nurtured them, broadening the paths of advancement and making detailed the methods for verifying actual achievements, so that even those in obscure corners and dark seclusion all shine forth in the bright light. Yet he still labors in anxious diligence from before dawn until late at night, tirelessly concerned lest worthy men be overlooked—this is an opportunity that comes once in a thousand years. Today the scholars of the realm surge like waves and stand thick as forests, stirring like thunder and rising like clouds; there is none who does not strive to cleanse and polish himself, hoping to respond above to this era of harmonious splendor—how much more so in this region, which has long abounded in cultural refinement and worthy men, ranking first among the four quarters? Go forth, gentlemen! When the Xuanli and Jielü jades are cut from the rough matrix and displayed, and when the Moye and Ganjiang swords have their…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
刃于治則朝市屬目焉爾諸
士思所爲報稱
明時以厭衆望者宜遵何德哉
先民有言不患無位患所以
立自古豪傑勒不朽之稱者
豈直籍名位顯爾鄉先哲可
考而鏡也今諸士業已釋蒯
===
屨駸駸嚮用所遭逢過古人
遠甚第令矢心精白華實相
副居官則重名節任事則抒
忠猷毋持祿以養交毋和光
以諧俗毋飾情以釣譽則庶
幾哉蜚英騰茂流金石之功
軼聲前軌
punctuated: 刃于治，則朝市屬目焉。爾諸士思所爲報稱明時、以厭衆望者，宜遵何德哉？先民有言：「不患無位，患所以立。」自古豪傑勒不朽之稱者，豈直籍名位顯？爾鄉先哲可考而鏡也。今諸士業已釋蒯屨，駸駸嚮用，所遭逢過古人遠甚。第令矢心精白，華實相副，居官則重名節，任事則抒忠猷；毋持祿以養交，毋和光以諧俗，毋飾情以釣譽。則庶幾哉！蜚英騰茂，流金石之功，軼聲前軌，
translation_en: … their blades fresh from the whetstone [reading 硎 for 治], then both the court and the marketplace will fix their eyes upon them. When you gentlemen consider how to repay and match this enlightened age and satisfy the expectations of the multitude, what virtues should you follow? The ancients had a saying: "Do not worry about having no official position; worry about that by which you establish yourself." Since antiquity, when heroic men of talent have engraved an imperishable reputation for themselves, how could it be merely by relying on rank and position for their distinction? The former worthies of your native region can be examined and taken as a mirror. Now you gentlemen have already cast off your rush sandals and are rapidly advancing toward official employment, enjoying an opportunity that far surpasses that of the ancients. If only you swear to keep your hearts pure and spotless, make your outward brilliance match your inner substance, value reputation and integrity when holding office, and unfold loyal counsels when taking up responsibilities; if you do not cling to emoluments to cultivate personal connections, do not dim your own light to conform with vulgar customs, and do not disguise your true feelings to fish for praise—then how close you will be to the ideal! Your renown will soar and your achievements flourish, you will leave behind merits worthy of being inscribed on metal and stone, and your fame will surpass the tracks of your predecessors; …

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖世明昌之運江右山川之勝亦
籍是有光已萬一與時頡頏
弁髦先資又或眩華采竒無
益於殿最俾觀者按籍而訾
之曰惡在其爲江右士也將
奚以謝
明時耶〔接雲〕屬望諸士甚厚誠
===
不敢以此相擬惟諸士自愛
幸焉是役也先巡撫江西右
副都御史今陞總督兩廣兵
部右侍郎劉〔堯誨〕今巡撫兵
部右侍郎兼右僉都御史劉
〔斯潔〕提督南贛軍務右僉都
御史蒙〔詔〕竝宣威澤化洽章
punctuated:
聖世明昌之運、江右山川之勝，亦籍是有光已。萬一與時頡頏，弁髦先資，又或眩華采竒，無益於殿最，俾觀者按籍而訾之曰：「惡在其爲江右士也？」將奚以謝明時耶？〔接雲〕屬望諸士甚厚，誠不敢以此相擬，惟諸士自愛，幸焉。

是役也，先巡撫江西右副都御史、今陞總督兩廣兵部右侍郎劉〔堯誨〕，今巡撫、兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史劉〔斯潔〕，提督南贛軍務、右僉都御史蒙〔詔〕，竝宣威澤，化洽章…
translation_en:
…the bright and flourishing destiny of our sagely age, and the scenic splendor of the mountains and rivers of Jiangxi [Jiangyou], will also derive glory from this. Should it happen by some chance that they vie with the trends of the times and cast aside the pledges with which they first advanced, or else dazzle with flowery brilliance and pursue novelty to no avail in the evaluation of official merits and demerits, causing observers to examine the register and criticize them, saying, "How is it that they are scholars of Jiangxi?"—then wherewith would they answer to this enlightened era? I, [Jieyun], place very high hopes in the scholars; truly I would not dare to compare them to such behavior, and only hope that the scholars will cherish their own integrity.

In this undertaking, the former Grand Coordinator of Jiangxi and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, now promoted to Supreme Commander of Liangguang and Right Vice Minister of War, Liu [Yaohui 劉堯誨]; the present Grand Coordinator, Right Vice Minister of War concurrently serving as Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, Liu [Sijie 劉斯潔]; and the Military Superintendent of Nan'gan and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, Meng [Zhao 蒙詔], have all proclaimed majesty and beneficence, their transforming influence permeating the…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
縫若協賛于外者右叅政佘
〔希周〕左叅議李〔天植〕副使吳
〔從憲〕郭〔孝〕黃〔思近〕劉〔志業〕僉
事周〔思敬〕武〔尚耕〕叅將尹〔湘〕
署都指揮僉事張〔應科〕楊〔一〕
〔經〕以入
賀行者右叅議王〔希元〕僉事劉
===
〔魯〕署都指揮僉事朱〔家將〕以
遷秩行者按察使陶〔幼學〕咸
先後與勞若戶部主事蔡〔乾〕
〔釡〕黃〔體乾〕蔡〔惟亨〕苗〔淳然〕禮
部司務程〔道淵〕主事陳〔述齡〕
工部員外郎鄒〔廸光〕主事張
〔崱〕中書舍人梁〔釴〕行人袁〔國〕
punctuated: 縫。若協賛于外者，右叅政佘〔希周〕，左叅議李〔天植〕，副使吳〔從憲〕、郭〔孝〕、黃〔思近〕、劉〔志業〕，僉事周〔思敬〕、武〔尚耕〕，叅將尹〔湘〕，署都指揮僉事張〔應科〕、楊〔一〕〔經〕；以入賀行者，右叅議王〔希元〕，僉事劉〔魯〕，署都指揮僉事朱〔家將〕；以遷秩行者，按察使陶〔幼學〕，咸先後與勞。若戶部主事蔡〔乾〕〔釡〕、黃〔體乾〕、蔡〔惟亨〕、苗〔淳然〕，禮部司務程〔道淵〕，主事陳〔述齡〕，工部員外郎鄒〔廸光〕，主事張〔崱〕，中書舍人梁〔釴〕，行人袁〔國〕
translation_en: … the Confucian scholars. As for those who assisted from outside: Administration Vice Commissioner of the Right She Xizhou 佘希周; Assistant Administration Commissioner of the Left Li Tianzhi 李天植; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Wu Congxian 吳從憲, Guo Xiao 郭孝, Huang Sijin 黃思近, and Liu Zhiye 劉志業; Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Zhou Sijing 周思敬 and Wu Shanggeng 武尚耕; Assistant Regional Commander Yin Xiang 尹湘; Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Zhang Yingke 張應科 and Yang Yijing 楊一經; those who departed to present congratulations at court: Assistant Administration Commissioner of the Right Wang Xiyuan 王希元, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Liu Lu 劉魯, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Zhu Jiajiang 朱家將; and the one who departed upon promotion: Surveillance Commissioner Tao Youxue 陶幼學—all, earlier or later, shared in the labor of this undertaking. As for secretaries in the Ministry of Revenue Cai Qianfu 蔡乾釡, Huang Tiqian 黃體乾, Cai Weiheng 蔡惟亨, and Miao Chunran 苗淳然; Office Manager in the Ministry of Rites Cheng Daoyuan 程道淵 and Secretary Chen Shuling 陳述齡; Vice Director in the Ministry of Works Zou Diguang 鄒廸光 and Secretary Zhang Ze 張崱; Drafter Liang Yi 梁釴; and Messengers Yuan Guo…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
臣馬應圖劉霖皆以使事至
樂觀盛典于法得備書云
湖廣永州府祁陽縣儒學教
諭林接雲謹序
punctuated:
臣、馬應圖、劉霖皆以使事至，樂觀盛典，于法得備書云。
湖廣永州府祁陽縣儒學教諭林接雲謹序。
translation_en:
… [Yuan Guo]chen, Ma Yingtu 馬應圖, and Liu Lin 劉霖, all arrived on official missions and were delighted to witness this grand ceremony; according to the regulations, their names may be fully recorded.
Respectfully prefaced by Lin Jieyun 林接雲, Instructor of the Confucian School of Qiyang County in Yongzhou Prefecture, Huguang.

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
萬曆七年江西鄉試
監臨官
巡按江西監察御史邵陞〔世忠浙江餘姚縣人戊辰進士〕
提調官
江西等處承宣布政使司右布政使張大忠〔國禎浙江秀水縣人壬戌進士〕
江西等處承宣布政使司左參議吳與言〔志默廣東大埔縣人乙丑進士〕
監試官
江西等處提刑按察司副使王世懋〔敬美直隸太倉州人巳未進士〕
江西等處提刑按察司副使蕭遍〔文明湖廣沔陽衛官籍沔陽州人乙丑進士〕
===
考試官
湖廣永州府祁陽縣儒學教諭林接雲〔喬登廣東陽江縣人甲子貢士〕
直隸蘇州府崑山縣儒學教諭趙成孚〔子惠浙江太平縣人戊午貢士〕
同考試官
山東東昌府濮州儒學學正翁大賓〔思敬浙江餘姚縣人辛酉貢士〕
直隸鎮江府金壇縣儒學教諭朱孔昭〔潛叔福建莆田縣人庚午貢士〕
山東青州府高苑縣儒學教諭李四維〔國張河南唐縣籍陝西慶陽衛人庚午貢士〕
湖廣德安府安陸縣儒學教諭陳公大〔子受福建閩縣人甲子貢士〕
直隸揚州府江都縣儒學教諭樊大通〔良宰湖廣荊州衛人庚午貢士〕
punctuated:
萬曆七年江西鄉試

監臨官

translation_en:
Jiangxi Provincial Examination of the Seventh Year of the Wanli Era (1579)

Supervising Official
Shao Sheng 邵陞 (courtesy name Shizhong 世忠, a native of Yuyao County, Zhejiang, and a metropolitan graduate [jinshi] of the wuchen year [1568]), Regional Inspector of Jiangxi and Investigating Censor.

Proctors
Zhang Dazhong 張大忠 (courtesy name Guozhen 國禎, a native of Xiushui County, Zhejiang, and a metropolitan graduate [jinshi] of the renxu year [1562]), Right Administration Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Administration Commission.
Wu Yuyan 吳與言 (courtesy name Zhimo 志默, a native of Dabu County, Guangdong, and a metropolitan graduate [jinshi] of the yichou year [1565]), Left Assistant Administration Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Administration Commission.

Monitoring Officials
Wang Shimao 王世懋 (courtesy name Jingmei 敬美, a native of Taicang Subprefecture, Southern Metropolitan Region [Zhili], and a metropolitan graduate [jinshi] of the jiwei year [1559]), Surveillance Vice Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Surveillance Commission.
Xiao Bian 蕭遍 (courtesy name Wenming 文明, of an official household in Mianyang Guard, Huguang, a native of Mianyang Subprefecture, and a metropolitan graduate [jinshi] of the yichou year [1565]), Surveillance Vice Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Surveillance Commission.

Examiners
Lin Jieyun 林接雲 (courtesy name Qiaodeng 喬登, a native of Yangjiang County, Guangdong, and a tribute student [gongshi, i.e., provincial graduate] of the jiazi year [1564]), Instructor of the Confucian School of Qiyang County, Yongzhou Prefecture, Huguang.
Zhao Chengfu 趙成孚 (courtesy name Zihui 子惠, a native of Taiping County, Zhejiang, and a tribute student [gongshi] of the wuwu year [1558]), Instructor of the Confucian School of Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Region [Zhili].

Associate Examiners
Weng Dabin 翁大賓 (courtesy name Sijing 思敬, a native of Yuyao County, Zhejiang, and a tribute student [gongshi] of the xinyou year [1561]), Instructor of the Confucian School of Puzhou Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong.
Zhu Kongzhao 朱孔昭 (courtesy name Qianshu 潛叔, a native of Putian County, Fujian, and a tribute student [gongshi] of the gengwu year [1570]), Instructor of the Confucian School of Jintan County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Region [Zhili].
Li Siwei 李四維 (courtesy name Guozhang 國張, registered in Tang County, Henan, a native of Qingyang Guard, Shaanxi, and a tribute student [gongshi] of the gengwu year [1570]), Instructor of the Confucian School of Gaoyuan County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong.

Fan Datong 樊大通 (courtesy name Liangzai 良宰, a native of Jingzhou Guard, Huguang, and a tribute student [gongshi] of the gengwu year [1570]), Instructor of the Confucian School of Jiangdu County, Yangzhou Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Region [Zhili].

Zheng Dundian 鄭惇典 (courtesy name Weichi 維勅, native of Houguan County 侯官縣, Fujian; metropolitan graduate [jinshi] of the renxu year [1562]), Prefect of Yuanzhou Prefecture 袁州府.

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子謂子夏日女爲君子儒無爲小人儒
詩云予懷明德不大聲以色子曰聲色之
於以化民末也詩曰德輶如毛毛猶有
倫上天之載無聲無臭至矣
孟子曰無爲其所不爲無欲其所不欲如
此而已矣
易
===
六四至臨无咎象曰至臨无咎位當也六
五知臨大君之宜吉象曰大君之宜行
中之謂也
象曰雷在天上大壯君子以非禮弗履
卦之德方以知
乾健也坤順也
書
人心惟危道心惟微
昔先正保衡作我先王乃曰予弗克俾厥
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子謂子夏日：「女爲君子儒，無爲小人儒。」

《詩》云：「予懷明德，不大聲以色。」子曰：「聲色之於以化民，末也。」《詩》曰：「德輶如毛。」毛猶有倫。「上天之載，無聲無臭。」至矣！

孟子曰：「無爲其所不爲，無欲其所不欲，如此而已矣。」

易

六四，至臨，无咎。《象》曰：「至臨无咎，位當也。」六五，知臨，大君之宜，吉。《象》曰：「大君之宜，行中之謂也。」

《象》曰：雷在天上，大壯；君子以非禮弗履。

卦之德方以知。

乾，健也；坤，順也。

書

人心惟危，道心惟微。

昔先正保衡，作我先王，乃曰：「予弗克俾厥
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said to Zixia [日 is a variant/misprint for 曰]: "You should be a scholar after the manner of the noble man, and not a scholar after the manner of the petty man." (Analects 6.13)

The Book of Odes says: "I cherish your bright virtue, which makes no great display of sound or appearance." The Master said: "Among the means for transforming the people, sound and appearance are trivial." The Book of Odes says: "Virtue is as light as a hair." Yet a hair still has something to which it may be compared. "The workings of High Heaven have neither sound nor smell." That is perfection! (Doctrine of the Mean 33)

Mencius said: "Do not do what you would not do, and do not desire what you would not desire—that is all." (Mencius 7A.17)

Book of Changes (Yi)

Six in the fourth place: Approaching in the closest way; no blame. The Commentary on the Images says: "'Approaching in the closest way; no blame'—this is because the position is appropriate." Six in the fifth place: Approaching with wisdom, fitting for a great ruler; auspicious. The Commentary on the Images says: "'Fitting for a great ruler' means acting with centrality." (Hexagram 19, Lin)

The Commentary on the Images says: Thunder is above heaven: Great Strength (Dazhuang). Thus the noble man does not tread upon anything that is contrary to ritual propriety. (Hexagram 34, Dazhuang)

The virtue of the hexagrams is square and therefore wise. (Appended Remarks, Part 1, 11)

Qian is vigorous; Kun is compliant. (Discussion of the Trigrams, 7)

Book of Documents (Shu)

The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle. ("Counsels of the Great Yu")

In昔 (antiquity), the former worthy Baoheng [Yi Yin] aroused and guided our former king. He said: "If I cannot make my… [sovereign like Yao and Shun]" ("Charge to Yue," Part 3)

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
后惟堯舜其心愧耻若撻于市一夫不
獲則曰時予之辜
先知稼穡之艱難乃逸則知小人之依
天齊于民俾我一日非終惟終在人
詩
龍盾之合鋈以觼軜
春日遲遲卉木萋萋倉庚喈喈采蘩祁祁
保玆天子生仲山甫仲山甫之德柔嘉維
則令儀令色小心翼翼古訓是式威儀
是力天子是若明命使賦王命仲山甫
式是百辟纘戎祖考王躬是保出納王
命王之喉舌賦政于外四方爰發
無此疆爾界陳常于時夏
春秋
春正月公狩于郎桓公四年
春王正月公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯
許男曹伯侵蔡僖公四年
晉人宋人衛人曹人同盟于清丘宋師
punctuated:
后惟堯舜，其心愧耻，若撻于市。一夫不獲，則曰時予之辜。
先知稼穡之艱難，乃逸，則知小人之依。
天齊于民，俾我一日，非終惟終，在人。
《詩》：
龍盾之合，鋈以觼軜。
春日遲遲，卉木萋萋。倉庚喈喈，采蘩祁祁。
保玆天子，生仲山甫。仲山甫之德，柔嘉維則。令儀令色，小心翼翼。古訓是式，威儀是力。天子是若，明命使賦。王命仲山甫，式是百辟。纘戎祖考，王躬是保。出納王命，王之喉舌。賦政于外，四方爰發。
無此疆爾界，陳常于時夏。
《春秋》：
春，正月，公狩于郎。桓公四年。
春，王正月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡。僖公四年。
晉人、宋人、衛人、曹人同盟于清丘；宋師
translation_en:
… sovereign become like Yao and Shun, his heart felt ashamed, as if he had been flogged in the marketplace. If a single man did not find his place, he would say, ‘It is my fault!’”
“First know the hardships of sowing and reaping, and then take your ease; thus you will know on what the common people depend.”
“Heaven regulates the people, granting us a single day’s opportunity; whether one fails to reach the end or succeeds in reaching the end depends on man.”

Book of Odes (Shi):
“The dragon-figured shields are joined side by side; silvered are the rings for the inner reins.”
“The spring days lengthen gently, the plants and trees grow lush; the orioles sing in harmony, and they gather the white southernwood in crowds.”
“Protecting this Son of Heaven, it gave birth to Zhong Shanfu. As for the virtue of Zhong Shanfu, gentle and admirable, it is a model. With fine deportment and fine countenance, he is cautious and reverent. The ancient teachings are his standard; dignified demeanor is what he strives for. Compliant with the Son of Heaven, he is commissioned to spread abroad the illustrious decrees. The king commanded Zhong Shanfu: ‘Be a model to all the princes, continue the great work of your ancestors, and protect the king’s person. Issue and receive the king’s decrees, as the throat and tongue of the king; spread government abroad so that the four quarters respond on every side.’”
“Without distinction of this boundary or that border, you spread the constant norms throughout this realm of Xia.”

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):
“In spring, in the first month, the Duke hunted in winter at Lang.” (Fourth year of Duke Huan.)
“In spring, in the king’s first month, the Duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao to make an incursion into Cai.” (Fourth year of Duke Xi.)
“Men of Jin, men of Song, men of Wei, and men of Cao made a covenant together at Qingqiu; the army of Song …”

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
伐陳俱宣公十有二年
楚屈完來盟于師僖公四年齊人歸我濟
西田宣公十年夏公會齊侯于夾谷公
至自夾谷齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田俱定
公十年齊人歸讙及闡哀公八年
禮記
晉人謂文子知人文子其中退然如不勝
衣其言呐呐然如不出諸其口所舉於
晉國管庫之士七十有餘家
===
君子如欲化民成俗其必由學乎玉不琢
不成器人不學不知道是故古之王者
建國君民教學爲先
文采節奏聲之飾也
子曰爲上可望而知也爲下可述而志也
則君不疑於其臣而臣不惑於其君矣
尹吉曰惟尹躬及湯咸有壹德
第貳場
論
punctuated:
伐陳。（俱《宣公十有二年》。）
楚屈完來盟于師。（《僖公四年》。）齊人歸我濟西田。（《宣公十年》。）夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田。（俱《定公十年》。）齊人歸讙及闡。（《哀公八年》。）

《禮記》
晉人謂文子知人。文子其中退然如不勝衣，其言呐呐然如不出諸其口，所舉於晉國管庫之士七十有餘家。
君子如欲化民成俗，其必由學乎！玉不琢，不成器；人不學，不知道。是故古之王者，建國君民，教學爲先。
文采節奏，聲之飾也。
子曰：「爲上可望而知也，爲下可述而志也，則君不疑於其臣，而臣不惑於其君矣。《尹吉》曰：『惟尹躬及湯，咸有壹德。』」

第貳場
論
translation_en:
… attacked Chen. (Both from the 12th year of Duke Xuan.)
Qu Wan of Chu came to make a covenant with the army. (4th year of Duke Xi.) The people of Qi restored to us the lands west of the Ji River. (10th year of Duke Xuan.) In summer, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The Duke arrived back from Jiagu. The people of Qi came to restore the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin. (All from the 10th year of Duke Ding.) The people of Qi restored Huan and Chan. (8th year of Duke Ai.)

Record of Rites (Liji)
The people of Jin said that Wenzi knew men. Internally, Wenzi was so retiring that it seemed he could not bear the weight of his clothes, and in his speech so halting that the words seemed unable to come out of his mouth; yet the men in charge of storehouses in the state of Jin whom he recommended for office numbered more than seventy families.
If a gentleman wishes to transform the people and perfect their customs, must he not start from learning! If jade is not carved, it cannot become a vessel; if a man does not learn, he will not know the Way. Therefore, when the kings of antiquity established states and ruled the people, they made instruction and learning their first priority.
Patterned brilliance and rhythmic cadence are the ornaments of sound.
The Master said: "When the ruler above can be known simply by looking at him, and the minister below can have his deeds recounted and recorded, then the ruler does not doubt his minister, and the minister is not perplexed by his ruler. The 'Announcement of Yin' (Yin Ji) says: 'Both Yin personally and Tang possessed pure and single-minded virtue.'"

Second Session
Discourse (Lun)

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
王道至大至正
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢詔諸儒講五經異同於石渠閣詔〔甘〕
〔露三年〕
擬唐以裴度爲司空同平章事誥〔元和十〕
〔年〕
擬
上以
御製聽
===
經筵官講大學衍義詩示輔臣輔臣依韻恭
和
命彙爲一冊名曰翊學詩謝表〔嘉靖六年〕
判語〔五條〕

詔、誥、表〔內科一道〕

translation_en:
"The Kingly Way is supremely great and supremely upright."

Imperial Proclamations (zhao), Mandates (gao), and Memorials (biao) [candidates are examined on one of these]:
Imitation of the Han imperial proclamation summoning Confucian scholars to discuss the discrepancies and agreements among the Five Classics at the Stone Canal Pavilion (Shiqu ge) [3rd year of the Ganlu era, 51 BCE].
Imitation of the Tang mandate appointing Pei Du (裴度) as Minister of Works (sikong) and Jointly Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery (tong pingzhang shi) [10th year of the Yuanhe era, 815 CE].
Imitation of a memorial of thanks on the occasion of the Emperor showing his imperial poem "Listening to the Classics Colloquium Officials Lecture on the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi)" to the Grand Secretaries, who respectfully composed poems in matching rhyme, and His Majesty's command to compile them into a single volume titled Poems in Aid of Learning (Yixue shi) [6th year of the Jiajing era, 1527].

Legal Judgments [five items]:
Recommending and employing officials and subofficial functionaries who have committed offenses.
Mutual surveillance regarding money and grain.
Prohibiting spirit mediums, sorcerers, and heterodox arts.
Harboring prohibited military weapons.
Riding postal relay horses while carrying private goods.

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
第叁塲
第五道
問我
國家稽古定制
朝與
講竝蓋
御大廷則顯比以理萬幾
處燕閒則靜淵以友千古此
聖德神功所以照耀於後先也於古若路寢視
===
朝而未聞有講者豈其制猶未備耶講
之制肇於何載哉便殿經筵宋代始詳
宜不自宋始也洪惟我
高皇帝至聖好學動有諏稽無非
講者自正統初服定爲儀注遂爲典章不易
焉我
皇上御極以來七載于茲
講之視
朝常倍其日邇益練習政典繙閱章奏時引
punctuated:
第叁塲

第五道

問：我國家稽古定制，朝與講竝。蓋御大廷則顯比以理萬幾，處燕閒則靜淵以友千古，此聖德神功所以照耀於後先也。於古若路寢視朝，而未聞有講者，豈其制猶未備耶？講之制肇於何載哉？便殿經筵，宋代始詳，宜不自宋始也。洪惟我高皇帝至聖好學，動有諏稽，無非講者。自正統初服，定爲儀注，遂爲典章，不易焉。我皇上御極以來，七載于茲，講之視朝，常倍其日。邇益練習政典，繙閱章奏，時引
translation_en:
Third Session

Fifth Question

Question: When our dynasty examined antiquity to establish its institutions, holding court audience and holding classical colloquia were placed side by side. Indeed, when presiding over the grand court, [the sovereign] openly unites [with his officials] to manage the myriad affairs of state; when abiding in private leisure, he remains tranquil and profound in order to befriend the ancients across a thousand ages. This is whereby sacred virtue and divine achievement shine brightly across past and future. In antiquity, there were practices such as holding court in the State Chamber (luqin), yet one does not hear of classical colloquia—could it be that the institution was not yet complete? In what era did the institution of classical colloquia originate? Side-hall classical colloquia (jingyan) were first elaborated in detail during the Song dynasty, though surely they did not begin with the Song. Humbly reflecting on our High August Emperor [Hongwu], who was supremely sage and fond of learning, in every action he consulted and investigated—none of it was anything other than exposition and study. From the beginning of the Zhengtong reign (1436–1449), ceremonial protocols were established, and they thereupon became permanent statutes that have not been altered. Since Our Majesty ascended the throne, seven years have passed up to the present, and the days devoted to classical colloquia have regularly been double those of court audiences. Recently, He has increasingly practiced the administrative statutes and perused memorials, frequently summoning…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
輔臣造膝盡言以圖所以登閎三五貽
萬世之治安者煌煌乎
盛德大業諸士能揚厲之歟夫
明主典學務於終始人臣願忠意常無窮也宋
之君稱好學者多矣而當時猶有循故
事爲美談之譏或欲從容降接以盡下
情或謂涉覽書史止學一事或謂治亂
得失不宜偏諱或謂因事立訓以廣談
議此皆近而易行者也可一一舉其說
===
歟宋制臣僚朝辭日具轉對有上殿劄
子卽非
今制所有而宴見陳奏
歷朝有之可乘
聖天子之勵精而請復也若是則萬方之情僞
悉聞
九重之聽覽益遠矣試言以備採擇何如敬
君之大始於責難毋顧望不盡也
問八音與政相通文章與時高下其說尚
punctuated:
輔臣造膝盡言，以圖所以登閎三五、貽萬世之治安者。煌煌乎盛德大業，諸士能揚厲之歟？夫明主典學，務於終始；人臣願忠，意常無窮也。宋之君稱好學者多矣，而當時猶有循故事、爲美談之譏。或欲從容降接以盡下情，或謂涉覽書史止學一事，或謂治亂得失不宜偏諱，或謂因事立訓以廣談議，此皆近而易行者也，可一一舉其說歟？宋制，臣僚朝辭日具轉對，有上殿劄子，卽非今制所有，而宴見陳奏，歷朝有之，可乘聖天子之勵精而請復也？若是，則萬方之情僞悉聞，九重之聽覽益遠矣。試言以備採擇，何如？敬君之大，始於責難，毋顧望不盡也。
問：八音與政相通，文章與時高下，其說尚…
translation_en:
…the Grand Secretaries to approach closely and speak without reserve, in order to plan how to ascend to and surpass the grandeur of the Three Emperors and Five Sovereigns, and bequeath peace and order to ten thousand generations. How glorious are such flourishing virtue and great achievements! Can you scholars extol and set them forth? Now, an enlightened ruler's dedication to learning must be maintained from beginning to end; a minister's desire to be loyal is ever boundless in its intent. Among the rulers of the Song dynasty, many were praised for their love of learning, yet at the time there remained the criticism that they merely followed routine precedent and treated it as a matter for fine talk. Some wished that the ruler would unhurriedly condescend to receive his ministers so as to fully grasp the conditions of those below; some said that browsing through books and histories is but one aspect of learning; some said that the successes and failures of order and disorder should not be partially tabooed; and some said that instructions should be established in response to actual affairs so as to broaden discussion and deliberation. All of these are near at hand and easy to put into practice; can you recount each of these arguments one by one? Under the Song system, on days when officials took leave of the court, rotational audiences (zhuandui) were arranged, and they presented memorials upon ascending the hall (shangdian zhazi). Even if this is not part of the present system, informal audiences for presenting memorials existed under previous reigns of our dynasty—could we take advantage of the Sacred Son of Heaven's diligent dedication to governance to request their restoration? If so, the true and false conditions of the myriad regions would all be heard, and the hearing and vision of the Ninefold Palace would reach ever farther. Try to set forth your views to prepare them for selection—how would that be? The greatest way to respect one's ruler begins with urging difficult achievements upon him; do not hesitate or hold back from speaking in full.

Question: That the eight musical tones correspond with governance, and that literary writing rises and falls with the times, is a view of…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
矣五帝三王之文載在六籍中國之人
世守之亦可以高下論否也自春秋秦
漢以迄於今其文章具在操觚之士日
劌心焉卽其才人人殊而一代之機杼
較若畫一其故何也論者以爲三代之
文至戰國而病涉秦漢復起漢之文至
列國而病唐興復起又有謂韓文不如
漢漢文不如先秦戰國者其遞相沿以
降乎其代有盛衰焉轉移變化之迹其
===
端安在可得詳究之歟古之論文者其
書至不可紀有爲典論者有爲文賦者
又有文章流別論與文心雕龍二書其
詳可得聞歟我
國家以文化致理往學士家論著故已富於
前代邇年以來作者愈工大氐馳騖於
先秦西京以爲復古而日靡於綺麗雕
華則可謂甚盛矣然識者顧以文巧太
過爲世道之憂其亦有見否歟彼將以
punctuated: 矣。五帝、三王之文，載在六籍，中國之人世守之，亦可以高下論否也？自春秋、秦、漢以迄於今，其文章具在，操觚之士日劌心焉。卽其才人人殊，而一代之機杼，較若畫一，其故何也？論者以爲三代之文至戰國而病，涉秦、漢復起；漢之文至列國而病，唐興復起。又有謂韓文不如漢，漢文不如先秦、戰國者。其遞相沿以降乎？其代有盛衰焉？轉移變化之迹，其端安在？可得詳究之歟？古之論文者，其書至不可紀：有爲《典論》者，有爲《文賦》者，又有《文章流別論》與《文心雕龍》二書，其詳可得聞歟？我國家以文化致理，往學士家論著，故已富於前代。邇年以來，作者愈工，大氐馳騖於先秦、西京以爲復古，而日靡於綺麗雕華，則可謂甚盛矣。然識者顧以文巧太過爲世道之憂，其亦有見否歟？彼將以
translation_en: …is of long standing. The writings of the Five Emperors and Three Kings are recorded in the Six Classics, and the people of the Central Kingdom have preserved them from generation to generation; can they too be evaluated in terms of superiority and inferiority? From the Spring and Autumn period, the Qin, and the Han down to the present day, their literary works all remain extant, and scholars who wield the writing tablet apply their minds assiduously to them every day. Even though their talents differ from person to person, the literary loom and pattern of each era is as uniform as if drawn to a single line—what is the reason for this? Critics hold that the literature of the Three Dynasties fell into decline by the Warring States period, and revived upon reaching the Qin and Han; that the literature of the Han fell into decline by the era of the Divided Kingdoms, and revived with the rise of the Tang. Yet there are also those who say that the prose of Han Yu (韓愈) is not as good as that of the Han, and that the prose of the Han is not as good as that of the pre-Qin and Warring States periods. Have they successively declined as they were passed down from one age to the next? Or does each era have its own flourishing and decline? Wherein lie the beginnings of these traces of shift and transformation? Can they be investigated in detail? Among the ancients who discussed literature, their books are too numerous to recount: there was one who composed the Discourse on Literature (Dianlun 典論), one who composed the Rhapsody on Literature (Wenfu 文賦), and there are also the two works, Discourse on the Genres of Literature (Wenzhang liubie lun 文章流別論) and The Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons (Wenxin diaolong 文心雕龍)—may we hear their details? Our Dynasty achieves governance through cultural transformation, and the discourses and writings of past scholars have already been richer than those of former eras. In recent years, writers have grown ever more skillful, generally galloping in pursuit of the pre-Qin and Western Han in the name of restoring antiquity, while daily growing more decadent in ornate beauty and carved splendor—this may indeed be called an extreme flourishing. Yet men of discernment, on the contrary, regard excessive literary artifice as a cause for concern over the state of the world; do they have a valid insight or not? Are they…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
文體之變不可不亟反耶抑亦有出於
文之外者歟夫賁辭觀乎人文以化成
天下孔子卦得之喟然而嘆聖人固無
樂乎文盛也誠欲返之其道奚由諸士
必有心知其意者尚究言之毋以文應
問孔子曰君子不可小知而可大受也古
之成大功立顯名於世者其居常守職
與人不相遠惟當天下之至難才技所
不能為而後其過人者乃見彼遵何道
===
也宋人雅以識量論人如謂士惟識量
不可强及器局欲大識見欲遠之言豈
不亦論篤歟然識量何以辨也甞觀古
人行事有疆臣陳兵入朝而談咲折之
者有回紇傾國入寇而單騎見之者有
失印不問而得於故處者有下馬嵩呼
而軍不敢譁者或當魏軍方至而圍棋
對戲識者即知其辦賊或當車駕渡河
而飲博驩呼人主顧恃以無憂其處天
punctuated:
文體之變不可不亟反耶？抑亦有出於文之外者歟？夫《賁》辭「觀乎人文以化成天下」，孔子卦得之，喟然而嘆，聖人固無樂乎文盛也。誠欲返之，其道奚由？諸士必有心知其意者，尚究言之，毋以文應。

問：孔子曰：「君子不可小知，而可大受也。」古之成大功、立顯名於世者，其居常守職，與人不相遠；惟當天下之至難，才技所不能為，而後其過人者乃見，彼遵何道也？宋人雅以識量論人，如謂「士惟識量不可强」，及「器局欲大，識見欲遠」之言，豈不亦論篤歟？然識量何以辨也？甞觀古人行事，有疆臣陳兵入朝而談咲折之者，有回紇傾國入寇而單騎見之者，有失印不問而得於故處者，有下馬嵩呼而軍不敢譁者。或當魏軍方至而圍棋對戲，識者即知其辦賊；或當車駕渡河而飲博驩呼，人主顧恃以無憂。其處天
translation_en:
… the change in literary style must urgently be reversed? Or is there also something that goes beyond literature itself? Now, the text of the Bi ["Grace"] hexagram says, "Observe the patterns of human culture to transform and perfect the world," yet when Confucius obtained this hexagram in divination, he sighed deeply—for the Sage inherently took no pleasure in the mere flourishing of ornament. If we truly wish to return from this, by what way should it be done? Among you gentlemen there must be those who understand the meaning of this in their hearts; please discuss it thoroughly, and do not respond with mere rhetorical display.

Question: Confucius said, "The gentleman cannot be known by small matters, but can be entrusted with great responsibilities." Those in antiquity who achieved great merit and established illustrious reputations in the world did not differ much from others when routinely fulfilling their duties in ordinary times; it was only when confronting the utmost difficulties in the world—things that mere talent and skill could not accomplish—that their superiority to others became manifest. What Way did they follow? Men of the Song dynasty regularly judged people by their insight and capacity (shiliang), as in the sayings, "In a scholar, only insight and capacity cannot be forced," and "One's vessel and scope should be broad, and one's insight and vision should be far-reaching." Are these not indeed sound discussions? Yet how are insight and capacity to be distinguished? I have examined the deeds of the ancients: there was one who, when a frontier commander arrayed his troops and entered the court, subdued him while chatting and laughing; there was one who, when the Uyghurs mobilized their entire state to invade, went to meet them on a single horse; there was one who, when an official seal was lost, made no inquiry and recovered it in its original place; and there was one who dismounted to shout "Long live the Emperor!" so that the army dared not make an uproar. Another, just as the Wei army arrived, played a game of encirclement chess (weiqi) with an opponent, and men of discernment immediately knew he could handle the enemy; still another, when the imperial carriage was crossing the Yellow River, drank, gambled, and shouted merrily, yet the sovereign relied on him to remain free from worry. In their handling of the world's…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
下之難一何偉歟又有密薦仁傑而反
見擯於外者有數稱寇準而陰見短於
上者詘於所知皆不自明又何汪洋無
際也小有可以驗大近有可以明遠故
有跌寶器於軍中而色不少吝有觸玉
杯於座上而神不為動者事雖眇小固
難能矣此其人皆負一代之望當時號
為有識量者今以數事觀之果稱其名
否歟假令局曲之士當其所處其亦能
===
辦否也然則大受之具信有不可及者
歟夫大音希聲大圭不琢豪儁不羣之
士固不可以才技取也誠慕而效之其
必有本焉諸士將志為大人者幸明著
所由以觀尚友之學
問孔子贊易而稱說道之大蓋自古及今
未有上下不相說而可言極治者然觀
詩書所稱君有凜凜於民上而民有兢
兢於王法者豈上下之間猶有畏心而
punctuated:
下之難，一何偉歟！又有密薦仁傑而反見擯於外者，有數稱寇準而陰見短於上者；詘於所知，皆不自明，又何汪洋無際也！小有可以驗大，近有可以明遠，故有跌寶器於軍中而色不少吝，有觸玉杯於座上而神不為動者；事雖眇小，固難能矣。此其人皆負一代之望，當時號為有識量者，今以數事觀之，果稱其名否歟？假令局曲之士當其所處，其亦能辦否也？然則大受之具，信有不可及者歟！夫大音希聲，大圭不琢，豪儁不羣之士，固不可以才技取也。誠慕而效之，其必有本焉。諸士將志為大人者，幸明著所由，以觀尚友之學。
問：孔子贊《易》而稱說道之大，蓋自古及今，未有上下不相說而可言極治者。然觀《詩》、《書》所稱，君有凜凜於民上，而民有兢兢於王法者，豈上下之間猶有畏心，而
translation_en:
… difficulties of the empire, how magnificent indeed! Moreover, there was one who secretly recommended [Di] Renjie 狄仁傑 and yet was rejected by him in public; and there was one who repeatedly praised Kou Zhun 寇準 and yet was secretly disparaged by him before the sovereign. Wronged by those whom they knew and appreciated, neither sought to clear himself—how boundless and vast like an ocean they were! The small can be used to verify the great, and the near can be used to illuminate the distant. Thus, there was one who had a precious vessel dropped and broken in the army camp without showing the slightest look of regret, and another who had a jade cup knocked over at a banquet without his composure being the least bit disturbed. Though such matters are trivial, they are truly difficult to achieve. All of these men bore the highest reputation of their age and were acclaimed in their time as possessing insight and magnanimity. Viewing them today through these several deeds, did they truly live up to their reputation or not? Suppose men of narrow and cramped minds were placed in their circumstances—would they also be capable of handling them or not? If so, is the capacity for great responsibilities truly something beyond reach? Now, the greatest sound is scarcely heard, and the greatest jade tablet is uncarved; men of heroic and extraordinary stature certainly cannot be judged merely by petty talents and skills. If one genuinely admires and seeks to emulate them, there must be a fundamental root to it. Gentlemen, as you aspire to become great men, please clearly set forth the way by which this is attained, so that we may observe your learning in befriending the ancients.

Question: In praising the Book of Changes (Yi 易), Confucius extolled the greatness of the Way of joy and mutual satisfaction (ydao 說道); indeed, from antiquity to the present, there has never been a case where ruler above and subjects below did not delight in one another and yet it could be called the pinnacle of governance. However, looking at what is celebrated in the Book of Odes (Shi 詩) and the Book of Documents (Shu 書), the ruler stands in trembling awe above the people, and the people remain cautiously fearful before the royal laws. Could it be that because a sense of fear still existed between those above and those below, they …

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
終遠於黃虞之治歟太史公左酷吏而
右游俠推秦之敝而以爲救火揚沸似
矣而游俠扞當世之文網乃津津道之
豈畏當獨在上而不在下歟昔有監謗
而拑民以目者寵鶴而不恤其民者卒
以致流亡之禍宜也至乃亡徒與上爭
衡而諫臣憂爲亂階宿衛士擅殺不問
英雄聞之而起則民不畏上之禍等耳
由斯以言豈爲治者苟取足於相維而
===
不必於古之所謂說歟今天下雖治而
上下之情猶似有不相通者得無畏心
之勝而未躋於說道也諸士有志於論
治其明以告我
問江右舊稱樂土其民沐浴德化且二百
餘年我
皇上御極以來亟下考成之令百司奉職惟謹
治具益張其效至於湖波不揚亦可謂
吏稱其職民樂其生矣顧治久則易隤
punctuated:
終遠於黃虞之治歟？太史公左酷吏而右游俠，推秦之敝，而以爲救火揚沸，似矣；而游俠扞當世之文網，乃津津道之，豈畏當獨在上而不在下歟？昔有監謗而拑民以目者，寵鶴而不恤其民者，卒以致流亡之禍，宜也。至乃亡徒與上爭衡，而諫臣憂爲亂階；宿衛士擅殺不問，英雄聞之而起，則民不畏上之禍等耳。由斯以言，豈爲治者苟取足於相維，而不必於古之所謂說歟？今天下雖治，而上下之情猶似有不相通者，得無畏心之勝，而未躋於說道也？諸士有志於論治，其明以告我。

問：江右舊稱樂土，其民沐浴德化且二百餘年。我皇上御極以來，亟下考成之令，百司奉職惟謹，治具益張，其效至於湖波不揚，亦可謂吏稱其職，民樂其生矣。顧治久則易隤，
translation_en:
… ultimately remains far removed from the governance of the Yellow Emperor and Yu Shun? When the Grand Historian [Sima Qian 司馬遷] disparaged harsh officials and esteemed wandering knights-errant, tracing the abuses of Qin and comparing them to fighting fire by fanning the flames or stopping boiling by stirring the pot, he seemed close to the mark; yet when wandering knights-errant defied the legal net of their age, he spoke of them with relish—could it be that fear and awe ought to reside solely among those above and not among those below? In antiquity, there was one who monitored slander and reduced the people to exchanging silent glances [King Li of Zhou 周厲王], and another who doted on cranes without caring for his people [Duke Yi of Wei 衛懿公]; that they ultimately brought about the calamity of exile and ruin was only fitting. Yet when fugitives and convicts vied for power with their superiors, so that remonstrating officials worried it would become the stepping-stone to rebellion [as Jia Yi 賈誼 warned under Han]; or when palace guards killed without authorization and went unpunished, upon hearing which ambitious heroes rose up [at the end of the Later Han]—then the calamity of the people not fearing those above is just the same! Speaking from this perspective, could it be that those who govern merely content themselves with mutual restraint, without needing what the ancients called joyful accord? Today, although the empire is well-governed, the sentiments of those above and those below still seem not fully communicated; could it be that a mentality of fear prevails, and we have not yet ascended to the Way of joyful accord? You gentlemen who aspire to discourse on governance, pray explain this clearly to me.

Question: Jiangxi (Jiangyou 江右) has long been called a happy land, and its people have been bathed in the transformative influence of virtue for over two hundred years. Since Our Emperor ascended the throne, he has repeatedly issued orders for the evaluation of official performance (kaocheng 考成); the百司 (various officials) attend to their duties with utmost care, the instruments of governance are increasingly extended, and the effect has reached the point where the waves of Poyang Lake do not rise—it may truly be said that officials are equal to their offices and the people rejoice in their livelihoods. Yet when order lasts long, it easily deteriorates; …

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
法久則易瑕識者摘瑕指隙或有桑土
之思諸瑣瑣不暇論試舉其大者與諸
士籌之罷遣客戍益募土兵兵畫得矣
而武備日弛額伍空虛果足稱折衝之
具歟歲穀屢登憲政力崇食筴似矣而
公私告乏閭閻鮮藏果足稱九年之蓄
歟長江大湖層嶺疊嶂形勢足恃也而
使姦人得竊以負嵎將要害之扼猶未
講歟調租計庸汰濫平役業謂良法乃
===
田里多愁歎之聲豈推行之術猶有遺
議歟蓋聞古有作內政以強國者有議
積貯以豫備者有欲固屯守之要者有
欲均賦役之法者其說具在也舉而行
之可以副
今日考成之實否歟抑更有法外之意可探
本而言者歟諸士生于其鄉必有抱先
憂之慮者願悉言之以助我所不逮
punctuated: 法久則易瑕，識者摘瑕指隙，或有桑土之思。諸瑣瑣不暇論，試舉其大者與諸士籌之：罷遣客戍，益募土兵，兵畫得矣，而武備日弛，額伍空虛，果足稱折衝之具歟？歲穀屢登，憲政力崇，食筴似矣，而公私告乏，閭閻鮮藏，果足稱九年之蓄歟？長江大湖，層嶺疊嶂，形勢足恃也，而使姦人得竊以負嵎，將要害之扼猶未講歟？調租計庸，汰濫平役，業謂良法，乃田里多愁歎之聲，豈推行之術猶有遺議歟？蓋聞古有作內政以強國者，有議積貯以豫備者，有欲固屯守之要者，有欲均賦役之法者，其說具在也。舉而行之，可以副今日考成之實否歟？抑更有法外之意，可探本而言者歟？諸士生于其鄉，必有抱先憂之慮者，願悉言之，以助我所不逮。
translation_en:
… and when laws remain in place for a long time, they easily develop flaws. Discerning observers point out these flaws and gaps, perhaps harboring a concern for precautionary measures before the storm ("binding the mulberry roots"). Without time to discuss minor details, let us raise the major issues and deliberate on them with you gentlemen:

Dismissing and sending home non-native garrison troops while recruiting more local militia seems like a sound military plan; yet military preparedness grows laxer by the day and the prescribed ranks are depleted—can this truly be called an adequate instrument for repelling the enemy? Grain harvests have repeatedly been abundant, and provincial governance has vigorously promoted food policies, which seems right; yet both public treasuries and private households report shortages, and the common folk have scant reserves—can this truly be called an adequate store for nine years? The Yangtze River and great lakes, along with layered ridges and overlapping peaks, offer topography sufficient to rely upon; yet if wicked men are able to secretly occupy them and hold out in cornered strongholds, is it because the control of strategic choke points has still not been properly studied? Adjusting land rent and calculating labor services, eliminating abuses and equalizing corvée—these are already called good laws; yet in the countryside there are many sounds of sorrow and sighing—could it be that the methods of implementation still leave room for criticism?

Indeed, we have heard that in antiquity there were those who instituted internal administration to strengthen the state, those who deliberated on accumulating grain reserves for advance preparation, those who sought to consolidate the essentials of military agricultural colonies and defense, and those who wished to equalize the system of taxes and corvée. Their doctrines are all extant. If we take them up and put them into practice, can they fulfill the reality of today's evaluation of official performance (kaocheng), or not? Or is there some meaning beyond the letter of the law that can be spoken of by probing into the fundamental roots? You gentlemen were born in this region and among you there must be those who cherish the foresight to worry before the rest of the world does. I hope you will speak of it in full, to assist me where my own understanding falls short.

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子謂子夏日女爲君子儒無爲小人儒
饒位
同考試官訓導林批發揮儒學之辨體認精微
而格調不凡無一語落蹊徑
同考試官教諭陳批清空雅澹洗刷陳言非胸
中理會素融安能入此妙境
考試官教諭趙批講爲與不爲宛得口氣
===
===
考試官教諭林批說理之文旨趣雋永
聖人語賢者以儒而欲其嚴君子小人之辨焉
夫儒一也而君子小人則必有分矣可不愼哉
昔子夏入聞夫子之道而悅出見紛華美麗而
悅則君子小人之介茫然而未有决也夫子乃
謂之曰天下有名同而實異者儒也是故有君
子儒矣有小人儒矣就君子而言其去小人也
遠甚就君子之所以爲君子而言其去小人也
特在幾希之間最易淆也人莫不知君子之爲
punctuated:
第壹場
四書

「子謂子夏日：『女爲君子儒！無爲小人儒！』」
饒位

同考試官、訓導林批：發揮儒學之辨，體認精微，而格調不凡，無一語落蹊徑。
同考試官、教諭陳批：清空雅澹，洗刷陳言，非胸中理會素融，安能入此妙境？
考試官、教諭趙批：講「爲」與「不爲」，宛得口氣。
考試官、教諭林批：說理之文，旨趣雋永。

聖人語賢者以儒，而欲其嚴君子小人之辨焉。夫儒一也，而君子小人則必有分矣，可不愼哉？昔子夏入聞夫子之道而悅，出見紛華美麗而悅，則君子小人之介，茫然而未有决也。夫子乃謂之曰：「天下有名同而實異者，儒也。是故有君子儒矣，有小人儒矣。就君子而言，其去小人也遠甚；就君子之所以爲君子而言，其去小人也特在幾希之間，最易淆也。人莫不知君子之爲
translation_en:
First Session
The Four Books

"The Master said to Zixia, 'You must be a noble man's scholar! Do not be a petty man's scholar!'"
By Rao Wei 饒位

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Lin 林 comments: He develops the distinction within Confucian learning with a subtle and profound personal comprehension, and his style is extraordinary, with not a single phrase falling into well-worn ruts.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Chen 陳 comments: Clear, airy, elegant, and serene, washing away stale clichés. Unless the understanding in his breast had long been thoroughly integrated, how could he enter such a marvelous realm?
Examiner and Instructor Zhao 趙 comments: In explaining "to be" and "not to be," he captures the exact tone of voice.
Examiner and Instructor Lin 林 comments: A composition that explicates principle with rich and lasting meaning.

The Sage spoke to the worthy about being a scholar, wishing him to be strict in distinguishing between the noble man and the petty man. Now, the term "scholar" is one, yet between the noble man and the petty man there is necessarily a division; how could one not be cautious? In the past, when Zixia went in and heard the Way of the Master, he was pleased; when he went out and saw profuse splendor and fine beauty, he was also pleased. Thus, at the boundary between the noble man and the petty man, he was muddled and had not yet reached a firm resolution. The Master therefore said to him: "In the world, that which shares the same name while differing in reality is the 'scholar.' For this reason, there is the noble man's scholar, and there is the petty man's scholar. Speaking of the noble man as a whole, his distance from the petty man is vast indeed; yet speaking of that whereby the noble man is a noble man, his distance from the petty man lies merely in the slightest fraction, which is most easily confused. There is no one who does not know that the noble man is…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
是而稍有不察遂未免以小人而混于君子矣
女惟於儒之中審其孰爲君子而爲焉致知而
務期於心得力行而務期於心體蓋無論跡之
所在視君子何如而求諸隱微有一爲己之念
者即君子也其爲之而已矣此女之不可不勉
者也就小人而言其去君子也遠甚就小人之
所以爲小人而言其去君子也特在幾希之間
最難辨也人莫不知小人之爲非而稍有不察
遂未免以君子而混于小人矣女惟於儒之中
===
審其孰爲小人而勿爲焉致知而非以炫俗力
行而非以干名蓋無論跡之所在視小人何如
而反諸幽獨有一爲人之念者即小人也其勿
爲而已矣此女之不可不戒者也吁儒果何常
之有哉爲君子則君子矣爲小人則小人矣名
實之際尚其愼之雖然今之爲儒者又異矣夫
君子小人之辨寬於跡而嚴於心以爲跡可假
也今之爲儒者孰不以君子自命究其爲或不
齒於小人有起而詰之輒曰吾求心之無媿而
punctuated: 是，而稍有不察，遂未免以小人而混于君子矣。女惟於儒之中，審其孰爲君子而爲焉。致知而務期於心得，力行而務期於心體，蓋無論跡之所在視君子何如，而求諸隱微，有一爲己之念者，即君子也，其爲之而已矣，此女之不可不勉者也。就小人而言，其去君子也遠甚；就小人之所以爲小人而言，其去君子也特在幾希之間，最難辨也。人莫不知小人之爲非，而稍有不察，遂未免以君子而混于小人矣。女惟於儒之中，審其孰爲小人而勿爲焉。致知而非以炫俗，力行而非以干名，蓋無論跡之所在視小人何如，而反諸幽獨，有一爲人之念者，即小人也，其勿爲而已矣，此女之不可不戒者也。吁！儒果何常之有哉？爲君子則君子矣，爲小人則小人矣，名實之際，尚其愼之！雖然，今之爲儒者又異矣。夫君子小人之辨，寬於跡而嚴於心，以爲跡可假也。今之爲儒者，孰不以君子自命？究其爲，或不齒於小人。有起而詰之，輒曰：「吾求心之無媿而
translation_en: … right, yet with the slightest lack of discernment, one inevitably ends up confounding the petty man with the gentleman. Among scholars (ru 儒), you must carefully examine what constitutes a gentleman and practice that. In extending knowledge, strive for genuine realization in the mind; in earnest practice, strive for genuine embodiment in the mind. Regardless of how your outward traces compare to those of a gentleman, if you seek within the subtle and hidden recesses of the mind and find even a single thought that is for the sake of self-cultivation, that is the gentleman. Simply practice this and nothing else—this is what you must not fail to strive after. Speaking of the petty man himself, he is vastly distant from the gentleman; yet speaking of that by which a petty man becomes a petty man, his divergence from the gentleman lies only in the slightest hair's breadth and is hardest to distinguish. No one fails to know that the petty man is wrong, yet with the slightest lack of discernment, one inevitably ends up confounding the gentleman with the petty man. Among scholars, you must carefully examine what constitutes a petty man and refrain from practicing that. Extend knowledge not to dazzle the vulgar, and practice earnestly not to seek fame. Regardless of how your outward traces compare to those of a petty man, if you reflect in solitary seclusion and find even a single thought that is for the sake of showing off to others, that is the petty man. Simply refrain from practicing this and nothing else—this is what you must not fail to guard against. Alas! What constant nature does being a scholar truly have? If one acts as a gentleman, one is a gentleman; if one acts as a petty man, one is a petty man. Between name and reality, one must indeed be cautious! Even so, those who act as scholars today are different yet again. The distinction between the gentleman and the petty man is lenient toward outward traces and strict toward the mind, on the grounds that outward traces can be feigned. Among those who act as scholars today, who does not style himself a gentleman? Yet if we examine their actions to the end, some would be despised even by petty men. When someone rises to question them, they invariably say, "I seek only that my mind be free of shame, and…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
已矣何者心可匿也噫跡不可匿也而可假心
不可假也而可匿吾不知儒之所終也
詩云予懷明德不大聲以色子曰聲色之
於以化民末也詩曰德輶如毛毛猶有
倫上天之載無聲無臭至矣
王守勝
同考試官訓導史批作此題者類襲浮語是篇
簡潔清新點綴明徹足為多士式矣
同考試官訓導張批體會傳註直寫心源闡發
===
至矣之義尤為超脫
考試官教諭趙批詞意精到
考試官教諭林批能發人所未發
論不顯之德者必要諸天而後至焉夫無聲無
臭天之所以為不顯也知天則知德矣皇矣蒸
民之詩何足以語此中庸推言下學之極功也
若曰君子由尚絅之心造篤恭之盛其為德至
矣將何以擬諸形容哉予懷明德不大聲以色
吾得諸皇矣之詩矣然而由孔子言之猶以為
punctuated:
已矣。何者？心可匿也。噫！跡不可匿也，而可假；心不可假也，而可匿。吾不知儒之所終也。

詩云：「予懷明德，不大聲以色。」子曰：「聲色之於以化民，末也。」詩云：「德輶如毛。」毛猶有倫。「上天之載，無聲無臭。」至矣！
王守勝
同考試官訓導史批：作此題者，類襲浮語。是篇簡潔清新，點綴明徹，足為多士式矣。
同考試官訓導張批：體會傳註，直寫心源，闡發「至矣」之義，尤為超脫。

論不顯之德者，必要諸天而後至焉。夫無聲無臭，天之所以為不顯也，知天則知德矣。《皇矣》、《蒸民》之詩，何足以語此？《中庸》推言下學之極功也，若曰：君子由尚絅之心，造篤恭之盛，其為德至矣，將何以擬諸形容哉？「予懷明德，不大聲以色」，吾得諸《皇矣》之詩矣；然而由孔子言之，猶以為
translation_en:
… all!” Why is this? Because the mind can be concealed. Alas! Outward traces cannot be concealed, yet they can be feigned; the mind cannot be feigned, yet it can be concealed. I do not know where those who call themselves Confucians will end up!

The Book of Odes (Shijing) says: “I cherish your bright virtue, which makes no great display of sound or appearance.” The Master said: “Among the means of transforming the people, sound and appearance are trivial.” The Book of Odes says: “Virtue is as light as a hair.” Yet a hair still has something to which it may be compared. “The workings of High Heaven have neither sound nor smell.” That is perfection!

Wang Shousheng 王守勝

Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Shi comments: Those who write on this topic generally repeat superficial clichés. This essay is concise, fresh, and lucidly embellished—fully worthy to serve as a model for the many scholars.
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Zhang comments: He comprehends the commentary and notes and writes directly from the fountainhead of the mind; his elucidation of the meaning of “That is perfection!” is especially transcendent.
Examiner, Instructor Zhao comments: The diction and conception are precise and thorough.
Examiner, Instructor Lin comments: Able to bring forth what others have left unexpressed.

Those who discuss unmanifested virtue must ultimately trace it to Heaven before reaching perfection. Now, having neither sound nor smell is whereby Heaven remains unmanifested; when one knows Heaven, one knows virtue. How could the odes “Huang yi” and “Zheng min” suffice to speak of this? In the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), when extending its account to the ultimate achievement of lower-level learning, it is as if to say: When the noble man proceeds from the mind of wearing an unlined garment over brocade to reach the fullness of steadfast reverence, his virtue has reached perfection—how then shall one liken and describe it? “I cherish your bright virtue, which makes no great display of sound or appearance”—this I have found in the ode “Huang yi”; yet from Confucius’s words, it is still regarded as…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
末焉德輶如毛吾得諸蒸民之詩矣然而以毛
擬之猶有倫焉夫囿于末者耳目見聞可得而
及也囿于倫者意言象數可得而及也是皆顯
之乎言德也其必如文王之詩所稱上天之載
無聲無臭乎蓋謂之聲臭則已忘乎其爲形固
不顯也謂之無聲無臭則并忘乎其爲氣尤不
顯之至也以之言天而天之精蘊見矣以之言
德而德之精蘊見矣聲色不大謂其囿於末而
未至也語至於是則非惟無末之可舉抑且無
===
本之可窺所以發揮乎篤恭之懿者爲甚悉德
輶如毛謂其囿於倫而未至也語至于於是則非
惟無似之可倫抑且無實之可指所以闡揚乎
篤恭之秘者爲甚精吁其斯以爲至乎而不顯
之妙可以觀矣要而論之何莫非自尚絅之一
念充之耶雖然亦不俟乎充之也人之心蓋如
此也是故無聲無臭其本體也日不見日不言
日不動其功夫也上智即本體爲功夫下學即
功夫爲本體無二也而說者以爲必自有而後
punctuated: 末焉。「德輶如毛」，吾得諸《蒸民》之詩矣；然而以毛擬之，猶有倫焉。夫囿于末者，耳目見聞可得而及也；囿于倫者，意言象數可得而及也。是皆顯之乎言德也。其必如《文王》之詩所稱「上天之載，無聲無臭」乎！蓋謂之聲臭，則已忘乎其爲形，固不顯也；謂之無聲無臭，則并忘乎其爲氣，尤不顯之至也。以之言天，而天之精蘊見矣；以之言德，而德之精蘊見矣。「聲色不大」，謂其囿於末而未至也；語至於是，則非惟無末之可舉，抑且無本之可窺，所以發揮乎篤恭之懿者爲甚悉。「德輶如毛」，謂其囿於倫而未至也；語至于於是，則非惟無似之可倫，抑且無實之可指，所以闡揚乎篤恭之秘者爲甚精。吁！其斯以爲至乎！而不顯之妙可以觀矣。要而論之，何莫非自尚絅之一念充之耶？雖然，亦不俟乎充之也，人之心蓋如此也。是故無聲無臭，其本體也；曰不見、曰不言、曰不動，其功夫也。上智即本體爲功夫，下學即功夫爲本體，無二也。而說者以爲必自有而後
translation_en: …merely superficial. "Virtue is as light as a hair"—this we find in the ode "Zhengmin" [The Multitude of the People]; yet to compare it to a hair is still to subject it to analogy. Now, what is confined to the superficial can still be reached by sight and hearing; what is confined to analogy can still be reached by thought, words, images, and numbers. All of this is to speak of virtue in terms of the manifest! Must it not rather be as the ode "Wen Wang" [King Wen] declares: "The workings of High Heaven have neither sound nor smell"? For to speak of sound and smell is already to forget physical form, which is indeed unmanifest; to speak of having neither sound nor smell is to forget even vital breath (qi), which is the utmost extreme of the unmanifest. When used to speak of Heaven, the subtle essence of Heaven is revealed; when used to speak of virtue, the subtle essence of virtue is revealed. That "sound and appearance are not great" was said to remain confined to the superficial and to fall short of the ultimate; when the discussion reaches this point, not only is there nothing superficial that can be cited, there is not even a root that can be glimpsed—thus bringing out the excellence of steadfast reverence with the utmost thoroughness. That "virtue is as light as a hair" was said to remain confined to analogy and to fall short of the ultimate; when the discussion reaches this point, not only is there no likeness to which it can be compared, there is not even a concrete reality that can be pointed to—thus elucidating the mystery of steadfast reverence with the utmost subtlety. Ah! This is indeed the ultimate! And herein the marvel of the unmanifest may be beheld. In sum, how is any of this not the full extension of that single thought of wearing an unlined garment over brocade? And yet, it does not even wait upon being extended, for the human mind is inherently thus. Therefore, having neither sound nor smell is its original substance (benti); what is called not being seen, not speaking, and not moving is its practical effort (gongfu). For those of the highest wisdom, the original substance is itself the practical effort; for those who learn from below, the practical effort is itself the original substance—they are not two. Yet some commentators hold that one must proceed from being before…

可進於無此以枯槁當吾無而疑其入於老氏
之寂滅也違無聲無臭之旨遠矣不可以不辨
孟子曰無爲其所不爲無欲其所不欲如
此而已矣
方鳴盛

尤爽剴緊切讀之快心

何等直截
===
考試官教諭趙批盡刷浮靡直窮本旨
考試官教諭林批說理精透
大賢論義盡之於不爲不欲之心矣夫不爲不
欲之心義也人能無失其心而義不盡於此哉
孟子示人之意若曰夫義何常一日而泯於人
心也義不可爲則人亦覺其不可爲義不可欲
則人亦覺其不可欲是是非非昭然在也自物
誘乗於外而不爲者始未免冒焉而爲之矣誠
思曰人一心也昔何以不爲今何以冒焉而爲之
punctuated:
可進於無，此以枯槁當吾無，而疑其入於老氏之寂滅也。違無聲無臭之旨遠矣，不可以不辨。

孟子曰：「無爲其所不爲，無欲其所不欲，如此而已矣。」

方鳴盛
