同考試官學正翁批：論義盡於不爲不欲之心，何等直截。
考試官教諭趙批：盡刷浮靡，直窮本旨。
考試官教諭林批：說理精透。

大賢論義，盡之於不爲不欲之心矣。夫不爲不欲之心，義也。人能無失其心，而義不盡於此哉？孟子示人之意若曰：夫義何常一日而泯於人心也？義不可爲，則人亦覺其不可爲；義不可欲，則人亦覺其不可欲。是是非非，昭然在也。自物誘乗於外，而不爲者始未免冒焉而爲之矣。誠思曰：人一心也，昔何以不爲，今何以冒焉而爲之…
translation_en:
…can advance to non-being. This mistakes withered lifelessness for our concept of non-being, and suspects it of falling into the quietistic extinction of Laozi. This departs far from the purport of "without sound or odor," and one cannot fail to distinguish them.

Mencius said: "Do not do what one would not do, and do not desire what one would not desire; it is simply like this and nothing more."

By Fang Mingsheng 方鳴盛

Associate Examiner and Instructor Fan 樊 comments: The conception is refined and profound, and the phrasing is vigorous and strong. The conclusion is especially brisk, incisive, and tightly focused; reading it gladdens the heart.
Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Weng 翁 comments: Discussing rightness as fully exhausted in the mind that refuses to do and refuses to desire—how direct and straightforward!
Examiner and Instructor Zhao 趙 comments: Completely sweeping away florid superficiality, it directly exhausts the fundamental purport.
Examiner and Instructor Lin 林 comments: The exposition of principle is refined and penetrating.

When the Great Worthy discusses rightness, he exhausts it in the mind that refuses to do and refuses to desire. Now, the mind that refuses to do and refuses to desire is rightness. If a person can avoid losing this mind, is rightness not fully exhausted right here? What Mencius meant to show people is as if to say: How has rightness ever for a single day been extinguished in the human mind? When in rightness something ought not to be done, people naturally sense that it ought not to be done; when in rightness something ought not to be desired, people naturally sense that it ought not to be desired. Right and wrong are brightly manifest within. It is only when the enticements of external things take advantage from without that what one originally would not do begins, unavoidably, to be done recklessly. If one genuinely reflects, saying: "A person has but one mind; why did I refuse to do this in the past, and why do I recklessly do it now…?"

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
也就爲之之時反求吾不爲之心而勿之爲焉
自已私乘於內而不欲者始未免苟焉而欲之
矣誠思曰人一心也昔何以不欲今何以苟焉
而欲之也就欲之之時反求吾不欲之心而勿
之欲焉是知不爲者義也無爲其所不爲者所
以充義也不欲者義也無欲其所不欲者所以
精義也天下之事有屬於是者莫不待義以決
其是而要之舍吾心之眞是別無所謂是天下
之事有屬於非者莫不待義以決其非而要之
===
舍吾心之眞非別無所謂非故曰如此而已矣
彼不求諸心而襲取於形跡之間吾恐得一事
止得一事之義也得一物止得一物之義也所
遺不旣多哉君子尚無自失其心可也先正之
言曰學者當求日減勿求日增夫人心至虛萬
有不染而强以一切納諸其中豈不悖乎故無
爲無欲日減之道也孔子告顏氏以四勿而子
思之論下學也推及於無聲無臭夫惟有無爲
無欲之心然後可以語無聲無臭之學君子其
punctuated: 也？就爲之之時，反求吾不爲之心，而勿之爲焉。自已私乘於內，而不欲者始未免苟焉而欲之矣。誠思曰：人一心也，昔何以不欲，今何以苟焉而欲之也？就欲之之時，反求吾不欲之心，而勿之欲焉。是知不爲者，義也；無爲其所不爲者，所以充義也。不欲者，義也；無欲其所不欲者，所以精義也。天下之事有屬於是者，莫不待義以決其是；而要之，舍吾心之眞是，別無所謂是。天下之事有屬於非者，莫不待義以決其非；而要之，舍吾心之眞非，別無所謂非。故曰「如此而已矣」。彼不求諸心，而襲取於形跡之間，吾恐得一事止得一事之義也，得一物止得一物之義也，所遺不旣多哉？君子尚無自失其心可也。先正之言曰：「學者當求日減，勿求日增。」夫人心至虛，萬有不染，而强以一切納諸其中，豈不悖乎？故無爲無欲，日減之道也。孔子告顏氏以「四勿」，而子思之論下學也，推及於「無聲無臭」。夫惟有無爲無欲之心，然後可以語無聲無臭之學，君子其
translation_en: …? At the very moment of doing it, one should turn back and seek the mind that does not do, and refrain from doing it. Once selfish desires take advantage from within, one begins to carelessly desire what one previously did not desire. If one genuinely reflects: "Man has but one mind; why did I not desire it in the past, and why do I carelessly desire it now?"—then at the very moment of desiring it, one should turn back and seek the mind that does not desire, and refrain from desiring it. Thus we know that not doing is righteousness, and not doing what one would not do is the way to fulfill righteousness; not desiring is righteousness, and not desiring what one would not desire is the way to refine righteousness. Among the affairs of the world that pertain to right, none do not depend on righteousness to determine their rightness; yet in essence, apart from the true rightness of my own mind, there is nothing else that can be called right. Among the affairs of the world that pertain to wrong, none do not depend on righteousness to determine their wrongness; yet in essence, apart from the true wrongness of my own mind, there is nothing else that can be called wrong. Therefore it is said, "It is simply like this, and nothing more." As for those who do not seek it in the mind, but instead appropriate it superficially from outward traces, I fear that in grasping one affair they only grasp the righteousness of that one affair, and in grasping one thing they only grasp the righteousness of that one thing—is not what they leave out already a great deal? The gentleman should simply not lose his own mind. A former worthy said, "The student should seek daily diminution, not daily addition." Now, the human mind is supremely empty, untainted by the myriad things; to forcibly cram everything into it—is this not perverse? Therefore, non-action and non-desire are the way of daily diminution. Confucius instructed Yan Yuan with the "Four Prohibitions," and when Zisi discussed elementary learning, he extended it all the way to being "without sound or scent." Only when one possesses a mind without action and without desire can one speak of the learning that is without sound or scent; may the gentleman…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
自得之
易
六四至臨无咎象曰至臨无咎位當也六
五知臨大君之宜吉象曰大君之宜行
中之謂也
方鳴盛
同考試官教諭樊批體裁莊整詞意簡嚴易義
之最佳者
同考試官學正翁批語約而該思婉而切君相
用賢之義闡發甚明
考試官教諭趙批瑩潔不浮
考試官教諭林批布置有法
===
臨爻之君相任賢而皆本于德焉夫任賢所以
輔治而德則其本也臨爻之君相以之二聖交
著其善也宜哉且夫治廣于用人而賢用于純
心君相之臨天下未有能違之者也何也以人
事君相道之所由光也六四處得其位下應初
九則加禮于巖穴之賢者不徒接遇之虛文而
punctuated:
自得之。
《易》
「六四：至臨，无咎。《象》曰：『至臨，无咎』，位當也。六五：知臨，大君之宜，吉。《象》曰：『大君之宜』，行中之謂也。」
方鳴盛
同考試官、教諭樊批：「體裁莊整，詞意簡嚴，《易》義之最佳者。」
同考試官、學正翁批：「語約而該，思婉而切，君相用賢之義闡發甚明。」
考試官、教諭趙批：「瑩潔不浮。」
考試官、教諭林批：「布置有法。」
臨爻之君相任賢，而皆本于德焉。夫任賢所以輔治，而德則其本也。臨爻之君相以之，二聖交著其善也，宜哉！且夫治廣于用人，而賢用于純心，君相之臨天下，未有能違之者也。何也？以人事君，相道之所由光也。六四處得其位，下應初九，則加禮于巖穴之賢者，不徒接遇之虛文，而
translation_en:
… attain it within himself.

Book of Changes (Yi)

"Six in the fourth place: Most earnest approach; no blame. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: 'Most earnest approach; no blame'—this is because the position is appropriate. Six in the fifth place: Wise approach; what is fitting for a great ruler; good fortune. The Commentary on the Images says: 'What is fitting for a great ruler'—this refers to practicing the mean."

Fang Mingsheng 方鳴盛

Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies (jiaoyu) Fan comments: "The structure is dignified and orderly, the diction and meaning concise and rigorous—the finest among the essays on the Book of Changes."

Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies (xuezheng) Weng comments: "The language is brief yet comprehensive, the thought subtle yet pertinent; the meaning of how ruler and chief minister employ the worthy is elucidated with great clarity."

Examiner and County Director of Studies Zhao comments: "Lustrous and pure, without superficiality."

Examiner and County Director of Studies Lin comments: "Methodically arranged."

The ruler and the chief minister in the lines of the hexagram Approach (Lin) entrust responsibility to the worthy, and both base this upon virtue. Now, entrusting responsibility to the worthy is the means to assist governance, while virtue is its foundation. Since the ruler and the chief minister in the lines of Approach act by this principle, it is fitting indeed that the two sages both set forth their excellence! Moreover, governance is broadened through the employment of men, and the worthy are employed through a pure heart; when ruler and chief minister approach all under Heaven, none has ever been able to depart from this. Why is that? Serving the ruler by means of men is whereby the way of the chief minister shines forth. Six in the fourth place occupies its proper position and responds below to Nine in the first place; thus, in bestowing courtesy upon the worthies from mountain caves, it does not consist merely in the empty formalities of reception, but …

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
出于延訪之實意此無負于相而蔽賢之過寡
也故周公繫之以至臨而占則无咎焉乃夫子
以位當申之夫亦以天下之士類非無德者所
能虛拘而以正感正固豪傑之聞風而景附也
通是道者所謂相而已矣用人則裕君道之所
爲智也六五柔中虛已下應九二則圖維于廟
廊之上者不以無不知爲明而以急親賢爲務
此克宜于君而得賢之化弘也故周公繫之以
知臨大君之宜而占則吉焉乃夫子以行中申
===
之夫亦以天下之治類非自賢者所能倖成而
以中行願固明君之恭已而成功也通是道者
所謂君而已矣是知相之得士自有相入而無
間者在疇咨晉接之先而君之致治亦自有相
得而益章者在憂勤宵旰之外周公舉其要而
夫子探其本臨道蔑以加矣抑論君人者如天
運于上而光明下濟臣如地之承天無成而代
有終故君不自役其智而寄之臣臣不自有其
功而歸之君周公作周孚先定鼎郟鄏厥功懋
punctuated: 出于延訪之實意，此無負于相，而蔽賢之過寡也。故周公繫之以「至臨」，而占則「无咎」焉。乃夫子以「位當」申之，夫亦以天下之士類非無德者所能虛拘，而以正感正，固豪傑之聞風而景附也。通是道者，所謂相而已矣。用人則裕，君道之所爲智也。六五柔中虛已，下應九二，則圖維于廟廊之上者，不以無不知爲明，而以急親賢爲務，此克宜于君，而得賢之化弘也。故周公繫之以「知臨，大君之宜」，而占則「吉」焉。乃夫子以「行中」申之，夫亦以天下之治類非自賢者所能倖成，而以中行願，固明君之恭已而成功也。通是道者，所謂君而已矣。是知相之得士，自有相入而無間者在疇咨晉接之先；而君之致治，亦自有相得而益章者在憂勤宵旰之外。周公舉其要，而夫子探其本，臨道蔑以加矣。抑論君人者，如天運于上而光明下濟；臣如地之承天，無成而代有終。故君不自役其智而寄之臣，臣不自有其功而歸之君。周公作周孚先，定鼎郟鄏，厥功懋
translation_en:
… stems from a genuine intention to seek out and consult them. In this way one does not fail the office of chief minister, and the fault of obscuring the worthy is rare. Therefore the Duke of Zhou appended to it the words "approaching in the highest degree," and its prognostication is "no blame." The Master [Confucius] then elaborated on this with "the position is appropriate," for indeed the scholars of the world cannot be bound by empty formalities by someone lacking in virtue; rather, when rectitude moves rectitude, heroes and outstanding men naturally hear of his wind and attach themselves to him like shadows. One who masters this principle is truly what is called a chief minister.

To be generous in employing others is what constitutes wisdom in the Way of a ruler. The Six in the Fifth place, being yielding, central, and self-effacing, responds below to the Nine in the Second place. Thus, in planning and deliberating high in the imperial court, he does not regard omniscience as discernment, but makes haste to cleave to the worthy his urgent duty. In this way he fulfills what is fitting for a ruler, and the transforming influence of obtaining the worthy is vast. Therefore the Duke of Zhou appended to it the words "approaching with wisdom, fitting for a great ruler," and its prognostication is "auspicious." The Master then elaborated on this with "acting with centrality," for indeed the governance of the world can never be achieved by mere luck by one who considers himself wise; rather, to fulfill one's aspirations through central conduct is how an enlightened ruler reverently composes himself and achieves success. One who masters this principle is truly what is called a ruler.

From this we know that in a chief minister's winning of scholars, there is naturally a mutual resonance without gap even before inquiring of them and receiving them in audience; and in a ruler's bringing about order, there is likewise a mutual rapport that shines forth ever more brightly beyond his anxious toil from before dawn until late at night. The Duke of Zhou set forth its essentials, and the Master probed its root; nothing further could be added to the Way of Approach (Lin).

Furthermore, if we discuss the one who rules over men, he is like Heaven revolving above, its bright light reaching down to bring aid; the minister is like Earth supporting Heaven, claiming no completion for itself but bringing things to an end on Heaven's behalf. Therefore, the ruler does not exhaust his own wisdom, but entrusts it to his ministers; the minister does not claim his own merit, but attributes it to his ruler. The Duke of Zhou inspired trust first in establishing Zhou and settled the tripods at Jiaru; his merit was great …

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
矣君子曰亦臣子之分所當爲曾不以爲周公
之功而成王之功也噫周公繫爻四僅无咎而
吉則歸之五也此公之所以爲遜也
乾健也坤順也
胡登明
同考試官教諭樊批講健順字義另箸色相此
作清新宛曲起繳處意味更深
同考試官學正翁批不襲塵筌沖然大雅錄此
以式多士足挽陋習矣
===
考試官教諭趙批善發題旨
考試官教諭林批詞不繁而意足
卦有陰陽之純者而性情因以異焉夫乾坤者
陰陽之純也一健一順而性情辨於其間矣說
卦之意蓋如此若謂易之所示者陰陽而陰陽
之所寓者理即陰陽以求其理而易卦之性情
可識矣何言乎易有八卦而始於乾坤乾之三
畫皆奇聖人有見於陽之純而象之者也天下
言健者必歸之陽而乾既爲陽之純矣是故无
punctuated:
矣。君子曰：「亦臣子之分所當爲。」曾不以爲周公之功，而成王之功也。噫！周公繫爻，四僅「无咎」，而「吉」則歸之五也，此公之所以爲遜也。

「乾，健也；坤，順也。」
胡登明
同考試官教諭樊批：講「健」、「順」字義，另箸色相。此作清新宛曲，起繳處意味更深。
同考試官學正翁批：不襲塵筌，沖然大雅。錄此以式多士，足挽陋習矣。
考試官教諭趙批：善發題旨。
考試官教諭林批：詞不繁而意足。

卦有陰陽之純者，而性情因以異焉。夫乾、坤者，陰陽之純也，一健一順，而性情辨於其間矣。《說卦》之意，蓋如此。若謂《易》之所示者陰陽，而陰陽之所寓者理，即陰陽以求其理，而《易》卦之性情可識矣。何言乎？《易》有八卦，而始於乾、坤。乾之三畫皆奇，聖人有見於陽之純而象之者也。天下言健者必歸之陽，而乾既爲陽之純矣，是故无
translation_en:
… indeed! Yet the gentleman says, "This is merely what is proper to the duty of a subject and son." Never was it regarded as the achievement of the Duke of Zhou, but rather as the achievement of King Cheng. Alas! When the Duke of Zhou appended the line statements, he assigned the fourth line merely "no blame," while attributing "good fortune" to the fifth line. This was how the Duke showed his humility.

"Qian is vigor; Kun is compliance."
Hu Dengming 
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Fan comments: Usually, those who expound on the meaning of the words "vigor" and "compliance" apply another layer of superficial embellishment. This piece is fresh and subtly winding, and the meaning at its opening and closing is even more profound.
Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Weng comments: It does not follow the dusty traps of convention, being harmoniously serene and of great elegance. Recording this to serve as a model for the many scholars is sufficient to reverse vulgar habits.
Examiner and County Director of Studies Zhao comments: Skillfully brings out the essence of the theme.
Examiner and County Director of Studies Lin comments: The words are not prolix, yet the meaning is complete.

Among the trigrams, there are those whose yin and yang are pure, and their natures and dispositions differ accordingly. Now, Qian and Kun are the pure ones of yin and yang; with the one being vigorous and the other compliant, their natures and dispositions are distinguished therein. The meaning of the Discussion of the Trigrams (Shuogua) is likely thus. It is as if to say: what the Changes (Yi) reveals is yin and yang, and what yin and yang lodge within themselves is principle. If one approaches yin and yang to seek their principle, then the natures and dispositions of the trigrams of the Changes can be understood. Why say this? The Changes has eight trigrams, and they begin with Qian and Kun. The three lines of Qian are all undivided; this is because the sage perceived the purity of yang and gave it emblematic form. In the world, those who speak of vigor must attribute it to yang, and Qian is already pure yang. Therefore, without…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
所屈撓无所止息而發强奮迅之理有浩然其
獨運者迺其純陽之性情則然耳雖乾元用九
若有不專于健者存而要之健者其常也彼諸
卦非无以陽名者然皆陽之雜而非純也則亦
安得以如乾之健哉坤之三畫皆偶聖人有見
于陰之純而象之者也天下言順者必歸之陰
而坤旣爲陰之純矣是故因而不作受而不宰
而柔順安貞之理有退然若無爲者迺其純陰
之性情則然耳雖坤元用六若有不專于順者
===
存而要之順者其常也彼諸卦非无以陰名者
然皆陰之雜而非純也則亦安得以如坤之順
哉于是知乾坤非迹也健順非精也迹之示者
使天下有所可窺而精之寓者使天下有所不
可測易卦之妙固如此嗟乎性无不善而情因
以流聖人能性其情故健也柔克順也剛克二
者各協其能以交濟也次之則任其情之偏而
猶各得其性之所近甚者則以情鑿性其究也
爲强梁爲恇懦而卒以敞噫剛柔相濟之理詩
punctuated: 所屈撓、无所止息，而發强奮迅之理，有浩然其獨運者，迺其純陽之性情則然耳。雖乾元用九，若有不專于健者存，而要之健者其常也。彼諸卦非无以陽名者，然皆陽之雜而非純也，則亦安得以如乾之健哉？坤之三畫皆偶，聖人有見于陰之純而象之者也。天下言順者必歸之陰，而坤旣爲陰之純矣。是故因而不作、受而不宰，而柔順安貞之理，有退然若無爲者，迺其純陰之性情則然耳。雖坤元用六，若有不專于順者存，而要之順者其常也。彼諸卦非无以陰名者，然皆陰之雜而非純也，則亦安得以如坤之順哉？于是知乾坤非迹也，健順非精也。迹之示者，使天下有所可窺；而精之寓者，使天下有所不可測。易卦之妙固如此。嗟乎！性无不善，而情因以流。聖人能性其情，故健也柔克，順也剛克，二者各協其能以交濟也。次之則任其情之偏，而猶各得其性之所近。甚者則以情鑿性，其究也，爲强梁，爲恇懦，而卒以敞。噫！剛柔相濟之理，詩
translation_en: …yielding and nothing halting; and the principle of vigorous exertion and swift rousing, operating vastly on its own, is simply the result of its purely yang nature and disposition. Even though in the primal Qian's use of Nines (Qian yuan yong jiu) there seems to be something present that is not exclusively devoted to strength, in the final analysis strength is its constant norm. As for the other hexagrams, it is not that none are named after yang, yet they are all admixtures of yang rather than pure; how then could they attain a strength like that of Qian? The three lines of Kun are all divided (even); the sages perceived the purity of yin and modeled this after it. In the world, those who speak of compliance necessarily attribute it to yin, and Kun is already the purity of yin. Therefore, it follows without initiating and receives without dominating; and the principle of gentle compliance and tranquil correctness, retiring as though doing nothing, is simply the result of its purely yin nature and disposition. Even though in the primal Kun's use of Sixes (Kun yuan yong liu) there seems to be something present that is not exclusively devoted to compliance, in the final analysis compliance is its constant norm. As for the other hexagrams, it is not that none are named after yin, yet they are all admixtures of yin rather than pure; how then could they attain a compliance like that of Kun? From this we know that Qian and Kun are not mere outward traces, nor are strength and compliance mere inner essences. What is shown by the traces allows the world something that can be glimpsed, while what is lodged in the essence gives the world something that cannot be fathomed. The subtlety of the hexagrams of the Changes is indeed like this. Alas! Nature is never less than good, and the dispositions flow forth from it. The sages are able to govern their dispositions through their nature; therefore, where there is strength they prevail by gentleness, and where there is compliance they prevail by firmness, the two each harmonizing their capacities to mutually complement one another. Those next to them indulge the partiality of their dispositions, yet each still attains what is close to his nature. In extreme cases, people chisel away at their nature through their dispositions; in the end, they become violently overbearing or timidly cowardly, and ultimately fall into ruin [? 敞 for 敗]. Alas! The principle of firmness and gentleness complementing one another, the Odes (Shi)…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
言之詳矣則道性情者信莫辨乎詩也
書
人心惟危道心惟微
王守勝
同考試官訓導史批危微字義摹寫最難是作
不冗不浮逸氣見于言外
同考試官訓導張批直抒直見意旨躍然中有
自得之語予蓋究心于理學者
考試官敎諭趙批文多古調
===
考試官敎諭林批俊雅不羣
聖君論人心道心而著其幾之可畏焉夫人心
欲其安也而危矣道心欲其著也而微矣其幾
如此可不畏哉大舜特指而言之以示禹也若
曰自昔聖人之以天下相傳非其位之謂也心
之謂也汝將有天下之責其亦求端于心乎今
夫人一心也心一道也顧自其發于形氣也謂
之人心是心也引而之于公也難引而之于私
也易有所動于內則不待在外者入而乗之而
punctuated:
言之詳矣，則道性情者，信莫辨乎《詩》也。

《書》：人心惟危，道心惟微。
王守勝
同考試官訓導史批：危微字義，摹寫最難。是作不冗不浮，逸氣見于言外。
同考試官訓導張批：直抒直見，意旨躍然。中有自得之語，予蓋究心于理學者。
考試官敎諭趙批：文多古調。
考試官敎諭林批：俊雅不羣。

聖君論人心、道心，而著其幾之可畏焉。夫人心欲其安也，而危矣；道心欲其著也，而微矣。其幾如此，可不畏哉？大舜特指而言之，以示禹也，若曰：自昔聖人之以天下相傳，非其位之謂也，心之謂也。汝將有天下之責，其亦求端于心乎？今夫人一心也，心一道也。顧自其發于形氣也，謂之人心。是心也，引而之于公也難，引而之于私也易。有所動于內，則不待在外者入而乗之，而
translation_en:
… speaks of it in detail; thus for articulating human nature and feelings, truly nothing is more discerning than the Classic of Poetry (Shi).

Classic of Documents (Shu): "The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle."
Wang Shousheng
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Shi: The meanings of the words "precarious" and "subtle" are most difficult to depict. This essay is neither prolix nor superficial, and a transcendent spirit appears beyond the words.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhang: Directly expressed and directly perceived, the meaning leaps out vividly. Within it are phrases of genuine personal insight; I take him to be [or: he is likely, reading 予 as 字?] one who has devoted his mind to the learning of principle (lixue).
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zhao: The prose has much of the ancient tone.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Lin: Refined, elegant, and extraordinary.

The sage ruler discusses the human mind and the mind of the Way, and makes manifest how fearsome their subtle incipient tendencies are. Now, as for the human mind, one desires it to be secure, yet it is precarious; as for the mind of the Way, one desires it to be manifest, yet it is subtle. Since their incipient tendencies are like this, how can one not stand in awe? Great Shun specifically pointed to them and spoke of this in order to instruct Yu, as if to say: Since antiquity, when the sages transmitted All Under Heaven to one another, it was not a matter of the throne, but a matter of the mind. You are about to bear the responsibility for All Under Heaven—will you not also seek the beginning in the mind? Now, man has one mind, and the mind has one Way. Yet insofar as it issues from physical form and vital energy (xingqi), it is called the human mind. This mind is difficult to lead toward impartiality, and easy to lead toward selfishness. When something is stirred within, it does not wait for external things to enter and take advantage of it, before…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
知誘之隙已啓有所動于外則不待在内者出
而乗之而攻取之勢已成蓋去之不可存之不
可逆之不可順之不可人心抑何危哉自其發
于理義也謂之道心是心也引而之于明也難
引而之于昧也易時當未放則杳然伏于方寸
之内而莫能窺其始時當既放則茫然游于千
里之外而莫能究其終蓋將以爲無又忽焉而
呈于有將以爲有又忽焉而隱于無道心抑何
微哉要之人心危矣而不以道御之則危益危
===
道心微矣而復以人汩之則微益微此精一執
中之學不容以不講也禹其懋哉嘗考堯之授
舜惟曰執中而已舜又益之以人心道心之說
何居曰非益之也人心之說指夫中之已涉于
欲者言也道心之說指夫中之未涉于欲者言
也已涉于欲則當有禁未涉于欲則當有養無
非所以保護此中也非益之也雖然繹其旨非
益之也跡其言則益之也蓋聖人之防天下也
固日以詳哉吁可以觀世變矣
punctuated:
知誘之隙已啓；有所動于外，則不待在内者出而乗之，而攻取之勢已成。蓋去之不可，存之不可，逆之不可，順之不可，人心抑何危哉！自其發于理義也，謂之道心。是心也，引而之于明也難，引而之于昧也易。時當未放，則杳然伏于方寸之内，而莫能窺其始；時當既放，則茫然游于千里之外，而莫能究其終。蓋將以爲無，又忽焉而呈于有；將以爲有，又忽焉而隱于無。道心抑何微哉！要之，人心危矣，而不以道御之，則危益危；道心微矣，而復以人汩之，則微益微。此精一執中之學不容以不講也。禹其懋哉！

嘗考堯之授舜，惟曰「執中」而已；舜又益之以「人心」、「道心」之說，何居？曰：非益之也。人心之說，指夫中之已涉于欲者言也；道心之說，指夫中之未涉于欲者言也。已涉于欲則當有禁，未涉于欲則當有養，無非所以保護此中也，非益之也。雖然，繹其旨，非益之也；跡其言，則益之也。蓋聖人之防天下也，固日以詳哉！吁！可以觀世變矣。
translation_en:
… the opening for perceptual enticements has already been breached; and when something is stirred on the outside, before what is inside even goes forth to take advantage of it, the momentum for seizure and conquest has already taken shape. Indeed, one cannot eradicate it, nor preserve it, nor oppose it, nor indulge it—how precarious indeed is the human mind!

Proceeding from principle and righteousness, it is called the mind of the Way. This mind is difficult to lead toward clarity and easy to draw into obscurity. When it has not yet been let loose, it lies darkly hidden within the square inch of the breast, and none can peer into its beginning; once it has been let loose, it wanders vast and boundless a thousand li away, and none can fathom its end. Indeed, just when one takes it to be non-existent, it suddenly manifests itself in existence; and just when one takes it to be existent, it suddenly conceals itself in non-existence. How subtle indeed is the mind of the Way!

In sum, the human mind is precarious, and if one does not govern it with the Way, its precariousness becomes ever more precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle, and if one further submerges it with the human, its subtlety becomes ever more subtle. This is why the learning of discriminating refinement, undividedness, and holding fast the Mean cannot go uncultivated. May Yu exert himself in this!

If we examine how Yao transmitted the empire to Shun, he said only "Hold fast the Mean" and nothing more. Why then did Shun add to it the doctrine of the "human mind" and the "mind of the Way"? I say: he did not add to it. The doctrine of the human mind refers to that aspect of the Mean which has already become entangled in desires; the doctrine of the mind of the Way refers to that aspect of the Mean which has not yet become entangled in desires. What has already become entangled in desires ought to be restrained, and what has not yet become entangled in desires ought to be nourished—all of which is simply the means to protect and preserve this Mean; it is not an addition to it. Even so, if we unravel his underlying meaning, he did not add to it; yet if we trace his actual words, he did add to it. For the precautions that the sages took for the world naturally grew more detailed day by day! Alas, from this one may observe the transformations of the age!

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
昔先正保衡作我先王乃曰予弗克俾厥
后惟堯舜其心愧耻若撻于市一夫不
獲則曰時予之辜
郭廷輔
同考試官訓導史批詞氣悠揚思致縝密大臣
任天下之重闡發無餘蘊矣
同考試官訓導張批格調高古意趣圓融爾雅
之文不當作經生語者
考試官教諭趙批冲淡中有逸趣
===
考試官教諭林批詞意俱精神
元聖之輔商王也其自任爲至重焉夫以君之
不堯舜爲已耻以一夫之不獲爲已辜元聖之
自任亦重矣則其所效于湯者豈苟焉而已哉
高宗以之期傅說也若謂人臣之在國家所以
上毗君德下毗民生而事業炳然于天下者何
也彼其初固嘗志之也我聞先正保衡矣昔先
正保衡之作我先王也際一德咸有之交慕二
代君民之美仰而思及乎君非必反道敗德遂
punctuated:
昔先正保衡，作我先王，乃曰：「予弗克俾厥后惟堯、舜，其心愧耻，若撻于市。」一夫不獲，則曰：「時予之辜！」
郭廷輔
同考試官訓導史批：詞氣悠揚，思致縝密，大臣任天下之重，闡發無餘蘊矣。
同考試官訓導張批：格調高古，意趣圓融，爾雅之文，不當作經生語者。
考試官教諭趙批：冲淡中有逸趣。
考試官教諭林批：詞意俱精神。
元聖之輔商王也，其自任爲至重焉。夫以君之不堯、舜爲已耻，以一夫之不獲爲已辜，元聖之自任亦重矣！則其所效于湯者，豈苟焉而已哉？高宗以之期傅說也，若謂人臣之在國家，所以上毗君德，下毗民生，而事業炳然于天下者，何也？彼其初固嘗志之也。我聞先正保衡矣。昔先正保衡之作我先王也，際一德咸有之交，慕二代君民之美。仰而思及乎君，非必反道敗德、遂…
translation_en:
"Formerly, the worthy elder Baocheng [Yi Yin 伊尹] raised up our former king. He said, 'If I cannot make my sovereign like Yao and Shun, my heart feels ashamed, as if beaten in the marketplace.' If a single commoner did not find his place, he said, 'This is my fault!'"
Guo Tingfu 郭廷輔
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Shi comments: The tone of the diction is flowing and melodious, and the train of thought is meticulous. The great minister's taking on the heavy responsibility of the world is expounded until no hidden meaning remains.
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhang comments: The style is lofty and ancient, and the conception is well-rounded and harmonious. It is a refined and elegant piece of writing, not something to be regarded as the mere words of a student of the classics.
Examiner and Instructor Zhao comments: Within its serene simplicity, there is an transcendent charm.
Examiner and Instructor Lin comments: Both the diction and the meaning are full of vigor.
When the Great Sage [Yi Yin] assisted the King of Shang, the burden he took upon himself was heavy to the utmost. Now, to take it as one's own shame if the ruler is not like Yao or Shun, and to take it as one's own fault if a single commoner does not find his place—how heavy indeed was the burden the Great Sage took upon himself! How, then, could what he devoted to Tang have been merely perfunctory? Gaozong [Wu Ding 武丁] used this to set his expectations for Fu Yue 傅說, as if to say: When a minister serves in the state, why is it that he is able to aid the ruler's virtue above, aid the people's livelihood below, and make his achievements shine brightly throughout the world? It is because from the very beginning he had set his ambition upon it. I have heard of the former worthy Baocheng. Formerly, when the former worthy Baocheng raised up our former king, meeting in a fellowship where both possessed pure and single virtue, he admired the beauty of the rulers and people of the two previous reigns [Yao and Shun]. Looking up and thinking of his ruler, it was not that the ruler had to violate the Way, ruin virtue, and sink into…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
于匪彞然後援之爲巳耻也即堯舜之聖天下
莫不望而震焉而彼且曰堯舜亦君也致君之
責我實身之而弗克使之爲堯舜天下有以舜
之事堯者律我我何辭也天下有以稷契臯夔
之事舜者律我我何辭也赧赧然有若撻于市
者矣保衡之存心于君也如此俯而思處乎民
非必四海九州胥于陷溺然後引之爲巳辜也
即一夫之微天下莫不眇而忽焉而彼且曰一
夫亦民也澤民之責我實身之而不能無一夫
===
之不獲是誰爲先知而使後知之至此也是誰
爲先覺而使後覺之至此也戚戚然有若推而
納諸溝中者矣保衡之存心于民也如此惟其
存心于君所以能作我先王爲堯舜也惟其存
心于民所以能作我先王之天下爲唐虞也爾
盍比美于保衡乎抑不特保衡然也湯亦有之
日新之銘慄慄之懼蓋奮然以堯舜自待而視
天下爲巳責也於是保衡之志得行而商業成
矣夫保衡不嘗五仕夏哉而夏德竟何如也故
punctuated: 于匪彞，然後援之爲巳耻也。即堯、舜之聖，天下莫不望而震焉，而彼且曰：「堯、舜亦君也。致君之責，我實身之，而弗克使之爲堯、舜；天下有以舜之事堯者律我，我何辭也？天下有以稷、契、臯、夔之事舜者律我，我何辭也？」赧赧然有若撻于市者矣。保衡之存心于君也如此。俯而思處乎民，非必四海九州胥于陷溺，然後引之爲巳辜也。即一夫之微，天下莫不眇而忽焉，而彼且曰：「一夫亦民也。澤民之責，我實身之，而不能無一夫之不獲；是誰爲先知，而使後知之至此也？是誰爲先覺，而使後覺之至此也？」戚戚然有若推而納諸溝中者矣。保衡之存心于民也如此。惟其存心于君，所以能作我先王爲堯、舜也；惟其存心于民，所以能作我先王之天下爲唐、虞也。爾盍比美于保衡乎？抑不特保衡然也，湯亦有之。日新之銘，慄慄之懼，蓋奮然以堯、舜自待，而視天下爲巳責也。於是保衡之志得行，而商業成矣。夫保衡不嘗五仕夏哉？而夏德竟何如也？故
translation_en: …into lawlessness before he would claim it as his own disgrace. Even given the sageliness of Yao and Shun—which everyone in the world looked up to in awe—he would still say: "Yao and Shun were also rulers. The responsibility of elevating the ruler rests squarely upon my own person; if I cannot cause him to become like Yao and Shun, and should the world judge me by the way Shun served Yao, what excuse could I offer? Should the world judge me by the way Hou Ji, Xie, Gao Yao, and Kui served Shun, what excuse could I offer?" Blushing with shame, he felt as though he were being flogged in the marketplace. Such was the heart that Baoheng [Yi Yin] maintained toward his ruler. Looking down and reflecting on how he dealt with the people, it was not only when the Four Seas and the Nine Provinces had all sunk into ruin that he would take it upon himself as his own fault. Even in the case of a single humble man—whom everyone in the world would regard as trivial and overlook—he would still say: "A single man is also one of the people. The responsibility of bringing benefits to the people rests squarely upon my own person; if I cannot prevent even a single man from failing to find his place, then who is it that is the first to know, yet lets those who are later to know come to such a pass? Who is it that is the first to awaken, yet lets those who are later to awaken come to such a pass?" Grieved and distressed, he felt as though he himself had pushed him into a ditch. Such was the heart that Baoheng maintained toward the people. Because he maintained such a heart toward his ruler, he was able to raise up our former king to become like Yao and Shun; because he maintained such a heart toward the people, he was able to raise up our former king's realm to become like Tang and Yu [Yao's and Shun's reigns]. Why do you not match the excellence of Baoheng? Yet it was not only Baoheng who was thus; Tang also possessed this spirit. With his inscription on daily renewal and his tremblingreverence, he roused himself to hold himself to the standard of Yao and Shun, and regarded the world as his own responsibility. Thereupon Baoheng's aspirations were carried into practice, and the enterprise of the Shang was accomplished. Now, did Baoheng not five times go to serve the Xia? Yet what became of the virtue of Xia in the end? Therefore…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
天下之本在君
詩
保茲天子生仲山甫仲山甫之德柔嘉維
則令儀令色小心翼翼古訓是式威儀
是力天子是若明命使賦王命仲山甫
式是百辟纘戎祖考王躬是保出納王
命王之喉舌賦政于外四方爰發
饒位
同考試官教諭陳批天為君而生賢佐此作兼
===
發其旨且典雅明暢子其深于詩者乎
同考試官教諭李批體裁整飭意趣悠長颯颯
乎復古之音可以雄視諸作
考試官教諭趙批純正典雅
考試官教諭林批詞達而文
大臣之生甚重故德職全也夫德職咸備大臣
之所以保天子也知此則仲山甫之生豈非天
哉作詩者意豈不曰天開一代中興之治有所
以主之者必有所次輔之者斯二者皆天也今
punctuated:
天下之本在君。

詩
「保茲天子，生仲山甫。仲山甫之德，柔嘉維則。令儀令色，小心翼翼。古訓是式，威儀是力。天子是若，明命使賦。王命仲山甫，式是百辟。纘戎祖考，王躬是保。出納王命，王之喉舌。賦政于外，四方爰發。」
饒位
同考試官教諭陳批：天為君而生賢佐，此作兼發其旨，且典雅明暢，子其深于《詩》者乎！
同考試官教諭李批：體裁整飭，意趣悠長，颯颯乎復古之音，可以雄視諸作。
考試官教諭趙批：純正典雅。
考試官教諭林批：詞達而文。

大臣之生甚重，故德職全也。夫德職咸備，大臣之所以保天子也。知此，則仲山甫之生，豈非天哉！作詩者意，豈不曰：天開一代中興之治，有所以主之者，必有所次輔之者，斯二者皆天也。今
translation_en:
… the root of all under Heaven lies in the ruler.

Book of Odes (Shi)
"To protect this Son of Heaven, / [Heaven] gave birth to Zhong Shanfu. / The virtue of Zhong Shanfu / Is gentle and admirable, according with the norm. / Of good deportment and good countenance, / Cautious and reverent, / He takes the ancient precepts as his model, / And strives for dignified demeanor. / Compliant with the Son of Heaven, / He causes the bright decrees to be promulgated. / The King charged Zhong Shanfu: / 'Be a model to all thehundred lords; / Continue the work of your great ancestors, / And protect the King's own person. / Issue and receive the King's decrees, / As the throat and tongue of the King; / Promulgate governance abroad, / So that in the four quarters it is set in motion.'"
Rao Wei 饒位
Associate Examiner and Instructor Chen's comment: Heaven gives birth to worthy assistants for the sake of the ruler. This essay fully brings out both aspects of this meaning, and is moreover classic, elegant, clear, and fluent—surely you are one deeply versed in the Odes!
Associate Examiner and Instructor Li's comment: The structure is well-ordered and disciplined, the meaning and spirit long-lingering. With the resonant sound of revived antiquity, it towers above all the other compositions.
Examiner and Instructor Zhao's comment: Pure, upright, classic, and elegant.
Examiner and Instructor Lin's comment: The words achieve their meaning and are refined.

The birth of a great minister is of the utmost weight, and therefore his virtue and his office are both complete. Now, to be fully endowed in both virtue and office is whereby a great minister protects the Son of Heaven. Understanding this, was not the birth of Zhong Shanfu truly the work of Heaven? Did the author of the ode not mean to say: When Heaven inaugurates an era of dynastic restoration and good governance, there is one by whom it is presided over, and there must next [reading 次 as 以] be one by whom he is assisted; both of these are from Heaven. Now…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
觀有明德者天子也而天旣監之故保天子者
天心也而仲山甫實生焉文武成康之德我天
子將肆揚于今日而生之以輔其德也文武成
康之業我天子將重光于今日而生之以佐其
業也如是而山甫之生也豈天生烝民然哉故
得一善皆可爲天子使而山甫之德全德也柔
嘉維則中和之至備矣儀色善而欽翼嚴表裏
何純乎古訓式而威儀力知行何懋乎上可以
順天子下可以敷明命則一身而萬善全矣保
===
我天子而一人之令德其有賴哉凡一職莫非
自天子命而山甫之命特命也式是百辟屛翰
之托重矣纘祖考而保王躬倚之爲腹心焉掌
出納而主王命寄之爲喉舌焉上而宣王之德
下而發民之應則一身而百職舉矣保我天子
而一代之鴻業其有賴哉信乎山甫之生爲保
天子生也異于烝民宜矣抑於是而知天人之
際也有唐虞必有五臣有成周必有十亂王者
名世若相待然非天而何但生賢者天任賢者
punctuated: 觀有明德者，天子也，而天旣監之；故保天子者，天心也，而仲山甫實生焉。文、武、成、康之德，我天子將肆揚于今日，而生之以輔其德也；文、武、成、康之業，我天子將重光于今日，而生之以佐其業也。如是而山甫之生也，豈「天生烝民」然哉！故得一善皆可爲天子使，而山甫之德，全德也。柔嘉維則，中和之至備矣。儀色善而欽翼嚴，表裏何純乎！古訓式而威儀力，知行何懋乎！上可以順天子，下可以敷明命，則一身而萬善全矣。保我天子，而一人之令德其有賴哉！凡一職莫非自天子命，而山甫之命，特命也。式是百辟，屛翰之托重矣。纘祖考而保王躬，倚之爲腹心焉；掌出納而主王命，寄之爲喉舌焉。上而宣王之德，下而發民之應，則一身而百職舉矣。保我天子，而一代之鴻業其有賴哉！信乎山甫之生，爲保天子生也，異于烝民宜矣。抑於是而知天人之際也。有唐、虞必有五臣，有成周必有十亂，王者、名世若相待然，非天而何？但生賢者天，任賢者……
translation_en:
…observing the one who possesses illustrious virtue, it is the Son of Heaven, and Heaven has already watched over him; therefore, protecting the Son of Heaven is the mind of Heaven, and Zhong Shanfu 仲山甫 was truly born for this purpose. The virtue of Kings Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang, our Son of Heaven is about to widely display today, and Heaven gave birth to him to assist that virtue; the enterprise of Kings Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang, our Son of Heaven is about to restore to glory today, and Heaven gave birth to him to aid that enterprise. This being the case with Shanfu's birth, how could it be merely like "Heaven giving birth to the multitude of people"?

Therefore, anyone who attains a single goodness can be employed by the Son of Heaven, yet Shanfu's virtue is complete virtue. Gentle and admirable, abiding by the rule, he possesses the utmost of equilibrium and harmony. His deportment and countenance are good and his reverent caution is strict—how pure are his exterior and interior! He takes the ancient precepts as his model and exerts himself in dignified demeanor—how diligent are his knowledge and action! Above, he can be compliant with the Son of Heaven; below, he can spread abroad the illustrious decrees; thus in a single person myriad goodnesses are complete. In protecting our Son of Heaven, does not the fine virtue of the One Man depend on him!

Every single office is without exception commanded by the Son of Heaven, yet Shanfu's mandate is a special mandate. Acting as a model to all the lords, the trust placed in him as a screen and bulwark is weighty indeed. Continuing the service to the ancestors and protecting the royal person, the King relies on him as his heart and belly; managing the issuing and receiving of decrees and presiding over the royal commands, the King entrusts him to be his throat and tongue. Above, he proclaims the King's virtue, and below, he brings forth the people's response; thus in a single person a hundred duties are fulfilled. In protecting our Son of Heaven, does not the great enterprise of the age depend on him!

Truly, Shanfu's birth was for the sake of protecting the Son of Heaven; that he differs from the multitude of the people is only fitting. Moreover, from this we may understand the interaction between Heaven and man. Where there were Tang 唐 [Yao] and Yu 虞 [Shun], there were necessarily the five ministers; where there was victorious Zhou, there were necessarily the ten able governors. A true king and a famous worthy of the age seem to await one another—if this is not Heaven, what is it? Yet while the one that gives birth to worthies is Heaven, the one who employs worthies…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
吾讀詩見山甫之德又見山甫之職而後知宣
王之中興有由也然我周之盛自文武成康而
下有君有臣以共成一堂之遇者僅見乎此則
上下之交豈亦有數而不可多得哉
無此疆爾界陳常于時夏
范以淑
同考試官訓導林批不事彫刻而文藻蔚然時
義之準繩也宜錄以式
同考試官教諭陶批題本平易作者類多衍詞
===
子于明順中更有剪裁可謂善說詩者
考試官教諭趙批清鬯

道之行由之其德亦大哉思文祀稷而歌之曰
人知唐虞之際我后稷登天下而粒食之不知
其胥天下而文明之也曷言乎常道之在人心
本未甞一日亡者但烝民未粒之先一時夏也
烝民既粒之後又一時夏矣稼穡教而凡此疆

無此疆爾界，陳常于時夏。

When I read the Book of Odes (Shijing), I see both the virtue of Shanfu and the duties of Shanfu, and only then do I understand the reason behind the restoration under King Xuan. Yet in the flourishing of our Zhou dynasty, from Kings Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang onward, the convergence of a ruler and a minister coming together in harmonious accord within one hall is seen only here. Could it be that such communion between sovereign and subject is also governed by fate and rarely attained?

"Without distinction of this boundary or that border, spreading the constant norms throughout these central states."

Fan Yishu 范以淑

Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Lin comments: Without resorting to artificial carving, its literary grace flourishes naturally. It is a standard for contemporary explication and ought to be recorded as a model.

From the breadth of the constant norms, one verifies the greatness of the Way of nourishment. For it was Ji (Houji 后稷) who nourished the people, and the practice of the constant norms stemmed from this—how great indeed was his virtue! The ode "Accomplished" (Siwen 思文), sung in sacrifice to Ji, says in effect: People know that during the era of Tang and Yu, our Lord Millet (Houji) raised all under heaven to eat grain, yet they do not know that he thereby brought all under heaven into civilized order. title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
爾界無往非率育之區樹藝成而無此疆爾界
隨在皆陳常之地道莫大于君臣也至是始得
陳之而衆著于尊尊之義焉凡屬于人合者亦
猶是已道莫大于父子也至是始得陳之而衆
著于親親之義焉凡屬于天合者亦猶是已以
五典則有慎徽者矣而所以康食之者誰與使
人心之常道有所賴而大明于斯世則當時時
雍之化謂稷貽之可也以五教則有敬敷者矣
而所以允殖之者誰與使常道之在人有所藉
===
而四達于中國則萬古禮教之俗謂稷留之可
也蓋上天牖民之意非獨緩于惠民之時故后
稷養民之時即以成夫教民之化天之生稷稷
之承天有如此者尊以配天詎曰不宜大抵天
命聖人各司其事如禹不能兼稷稷不能兼契
推之臯陶伯益皆然要之列聖者事相成而功
相等也故禹身有天下而稷契臯陶伯益則其
後世迭有天下乃知天心固右之矣周人南郊
之祭其以天事天乎逮觀周禮三農九穀之務
punctuated: 爾界，無往非率育之區；樹藝成，而無此疆爾界，隨在皆陳常之地。道莫大于君臣也，至是始得陳之，而衆著于尊尊之義焉；凡屬于人合者，亦猶是已。道莫大于父子也，至是始得陳之，而衆著于親親之義焉；凡屬于天合者，亦猶是已。以五典，則有慎徽者矣，而所以康食之者誰與？使人心之常道有所賴而大明于斯世，則當時時雍之化，謂稷貽之可也。以五教，則有敬敷者矣，而所以允殖之者誰與？使常道之在人有所藉而四達于中國，則萬古禮教之俗，謂稷留之可也。蓋上天牖民之意，非獨緩于惠民之時；故后稷養民之時，即以成夫教民之化。天之生稷，稷之承天，有如此者，尊以配天，詎曰不宜？大抵天命聖人，各司其事，如禹不能兼稷，稷不能兼契，推之臯陶、伯益皆然；要之，列聖者，事相成而功相等也。故禹身有天下，而稷、契、臯陶、伯益則其後世迭有天下，乃知天心固右之矣。周人南郊之祭，其以天事天乎！逮觀《周禮》三農、九穀之務，
translation_en: …your bounds, there was nowhere that was not a region where all were nourished; once the planting and cultivation were accomplished, without distinction between this boundary and your bounds, everywhere became a place where the constant norms were spread. No Way is greater than that between ruler and minister; only at this point could it be set forth, so that the multitude clearly understood the principle of honoring the honorable—and all relationships formed by human association were likewise. No Way is greater than that between father and son; only at this point could it be set forth, so that the multitude clearly understood the principle of loving one's kin—and all relationships formed by Heaven's bond were likewise. As for the Five Constant Norms, there was indeed one who carefully beautified them, yet who was it that provided the people with peace and food? In enabling the constant norms of the human mind to have something to rely upon and shine forth brightly in this world, the harmonious transformation of that age may well be said to have been bequeathed by Ji (Houji 后稷). As for the Five Teachings, there was indeed one who reverently propagated them, yet who was it that truly enabled the people to multiply and prosper? In enabling the constant norms residing in humanity to have a foundation and reach in all directions throughout the Central States, the customs of ritual and moral instruction for ten thousand generations may well be said to have been left behind by Ji. Indeed, High Heaven's intention to enlighten the people was not relaxed even at the time when it was simply bestowing material sustenance upon them; therefore, at the very time when Houji nourished the people, he thereby brought to completion the transformative work of instructing them. Such was Heaven's giving birth to Ji, and such was Ji's succession to Heaven's will; to honor him as a correlate of Heaven—how could that be called inappropriate? On the whole, Heaven commanded the sages each to take charge of his own task: thus Yu 禹 could not concurrently fulfill the role of Ji, nor could Ji concurrently fulfill the role of Xie 契, and by extension the same was true of Gao Yao 臯陶 and Boyi 伯益. In sum, those several sages complemented one another in their undertakings and were equal in their merits. Therefore, while Yu possessed the realm in his own person, the descendants of Ji, Xie, Gao Yao, and Boyi successively possessed the realm in later ages; from this we know that the mind of Heaven assuredly favored and assisted them. In the Zhou people's sacrifice in the southern suburb, were they not serving Heaven by means of Heaven itself! And when we come to observe the tasks concerning the three classes of farmers and the nine grains in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), …

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
與夫七月之陳則又起而嘆曰此天與稷所以
亨也
春秋
春正月公狩于郎〔桓公四年〕
袁時徹
同考試官訓導余批〔有斷制有風骨鏗然金石〕
〔當于古調中求之〕
考試官教諭趙批〔詞意謹嚴筆力蒼老〕
考試官教諭林批〔得本傳謹微之旨〕
===
經於講武非地者而謹之以全王德焉此見不
地之狩雖微而戾于王德則大矣春秋能無謹
乎嘗攷列國田狩之地各有常所若原圃若具
囿未有以易之者魯之去大野而于郎非所矣
然此亦淺失也惡足以病公噫此以細娛爲無
傷而不去也不曰明王愼德以民物得所爲極
致乎吾想其遷迹于郎也豈不以車徒之不遠
則不足以窮弋獵而明得意吾有四境而吾狩
之庸何擇不思從禽之心勝則場圃無完物淫
punctuated:
與夫《七月》之陳，則又起而嘆曰：此天與稷所以亨也。

《春秋》
春正月，公狩于郎。〔桓公四年〕
袁時徹
同考試官訓導余批：〔有斷制，有風骨，鏗然金石，當于古調中求之。〕
考試官教諭趙批：〔詞意謹嚴，筆力蒼老。〕

經於講武非地者而謹之，以全王德焉。此見不地之狩雖微，而戾于王德則大矣，《春秋》能無謹乎？嘗攷列國田狩之地，各有常所，若原圃、若具囿，未有以易之者。魯之去大野而于郎，非所矣。然此亦淺失也，惡足以病公？噫！此以細娛爲無傷而不去也，不曰明王愼德，以民物得所爲極致乎？吾想其遷迹于郎也，豈不以車徒之不遠，則不足以窮弋獵而明得意？吾有四境而吾狩之，庸何擇？不思從禽之心勝，則場圃無完物；淫…
translation_en:
… and the exposition in "Seventh Month" (Qiyue), one cannot help but rise and sigh: "This is why Heaven and Hou Ji enjoy the sacrificial offerings!"

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"In spring, in the王 first month, the Duke hunted in the winter hunt at Lang." [Fourth year of Duke Huan]
By Yuan Shiche 袁時徹
Comment by Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Yu 余: [It possesses decisive judgment and vigorous character, ringing like metal and stone; one must seek its like among the ancient melodies.]
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Zhao 趙: [The diction and conception are rigorous and strict; the brushwork is seasoned and forceful.]
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Lin 林: [It grasps the fundamental commentary's principle of exercising caution over subtle beginnings.]

In a case where military exercises were conducted in an improper place, the Classic recorded it with caution in order to preserve kingly virtue in its entirety. This shows that although hunting in an improper place is a minor matter, its violation of kingly virtue is great indeed—how could the Spring and Autumn Annals not be cautious about it?

I have examined the hunting grounds of the various states and found that each had its regular location—such as Yuanpu in Zheng or Juyou in Qi—which was never altered. For Lu to abandon Daye and go to Lang was to hunt in an improper place. Yet this too seems a superficial fault; how is it enough to reproach the Duke? Alas! To say so is to regard a minor amusement as harmless and refuse to give it up. Is it not said that an enlightened king carefully cultivates his virtue, taking as his ultimate goal that the people and all living things find their proper place?

When I imagine his shifting his tracks to Lang, was it not because he felt that if his chariots and footmen did not go far afield, it would not suffice to exhaust the pleasures of shooting and hunting and display his self-satisfaction, thinking, "I possess all within my four borders and I hunt in them—what need is there to choose?" title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
逞之念滋則道里無寧居有不俟還軫而蓄厲
萌興怨讟並作也國其謂我何嗚呼此直淺失
而已哉王者以民吾同胞即生之而猶若有傷
物吾同與即用之而猶非得已桓迺冒於原獸
而忘其國恤以之訓民則不威以之取物則不
順將焉用之率是而行則凡以一人肆于民上
而棄天地之性者弗可止也已故春秋不以為
微而特書以謹之欲有國者存此心以仁民則
百姓和而四境謐存此心以愛物則鳥獸若而
===
草木蕃每謹于微而王德全矣抑無淫于田自
古記之郎之狩甚矣咸丘之焚又甚矣東魯必
無幸乎雖然親親而仁民仁民而愛物逆德如
桓而可求多哉特假桓以訓天下後世云爾而
後世猶有馳騁弋獵如長楊上林之役者吾不
知于王德何如
楚屈完來盟于師〔僖公四年〕齊人歸我濟
西田〔宣公十年〕夏公會齊侯于夾谷公
至自夾谷齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田〔俱定公〕
punctuated:
逞之念滋，則道里無寧居；有不俟還軫而蓄厲萌興，怨讟並作也。國其謂我何？嗚呼！此直淺失而已哉？王者以民吾同胞，即生之而猶若有傷；物吾同與，即用之而猶非得已。桓迺冒於原獸而忘其國恤，以之訓民則不威，以之取物則不順，將焉用之？率是而行，則凡以一人肆于民上而棄天地之性者，弗可止也已。故《春秋》不以為微而特書以謹之，欲有國者存此心以仁民，則百姓和而四境謐；存此心以愛物，則鳥獸若而草木蕃，每謹于微而王德全矣。抑「無淫于田」，自古記之。郎之狩甚矣，咸丘之焚又甚矣，東魯必無幸乎！雖然，親親而仁民，仁民而愛物；逆德如桓，而可求多哉？特假桓以訓天下後世云爾。而後世猶有馳騁弋獵如長楊、上林之役者，吾不知于王德何如？
「楚屈完來盟于師」〔僖公四年〕、「齊人歸我濟西田」〔宣公十年〕、「夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田」〔俱定公〕
translation_en:
…of wanton indulgence grows, then along the roads there will be no peaceful dwellings; even before the carriages turn back, pent-up distress [?] will sprout up and bitter complaints will arise together. What then would the state say of me? Alas! Is this merely a superficial fault? A true king regards the people as his own flesh and blood, so that even as he gives them life, he still feels as though they might be harmed; he regards creatures as his fellow beings, so that even when he makes use of them, he does so only out of necessity. Yet Duke Huan recklessly pursued the beasts of the plains and forgot the cares of his state. Used to instruct the people, such conduct lacks majesty; used to take creatures, it lacks compliance—of what use then could it be? If one acts along this course, then whenever a single man indulges himself above the people and casts aside the nature of Heaven and Earth, there will be no stopping him. Therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) did not treat this as trivial, but specially recorded it to serve as a caution: desiring that those who possess states preserve this mind to be benevolent to the people, so that the hundred surnames are harmonious and the four borders tranquil; and preserve this mind to love creatures, so that birds and beasts are docile and grasses and trees flourish—being ever cautious in small matters so that kingly virtue is complete. Moreover, "Do not indulge to excess in hunting" has been recorded since antiquity. The winter hunt at Lang was already excessive, and the burning of Xianqiu was even more excessive—surely Eastern Lu could have no good fortune! Even so, one is affectionate to kin and thereby benevolent to the people, benevolent to the people and thereby loving toward creatures; with someone of perverse virtue like Duke Huan, how could one demand so much of him? The sage merely used Duke Huan to instruct the world and future generations, that is all. Yet in later ages there were still those who galloped about shooting and hunting, as in the excursions to Changyang and Shanglin—I do not know how those compare with kingly virtue!

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
公十年齊人歸讙及闡哀公八年
王松孫
同考試官訓導余批書法錯綜作者難于融會
是篇結構精密而詞調更覺鏗鏘
考試官教諭趙批聖人化强之績提點明透
考試官教諭林批意周語勁
春秋殊辭以紀化强之效而不嫌於序績焉此
聖人之化齊去常情遠矣卽以序人者而自序
何嫌哉昔魯之三田隨夾谷而舉之齊也說者
===
曰謝過也夫齊之親魯不寧唯是前有濟西後
有讙闡皆僅以歸書而玆獨以來歸爲文同於
屈完之來盟者何邪噫此夫子化强之績也蓋
卑屈事人者以言請之而不足禮義責人者以
心服之而有餘故楚之方漢猶昔也齊桓一聲
王貢之闕而同好是承夫亦屈於義也以彼霸
者猶然而況于王乎當時鼓譟之齊不減於楚
而式微之魯何敢望齊非夫子當之幾殆矣廼
攝相從君秉禮責敵裔俘却焉兵車拒焉野饗
punctuated:
公十年。齊人歸讙及闡。哀公八年。
王松孫
同考試官訓導余批：書法錯綜，作者難于融會。是篇結構精密，而詞調更覺鏗鏘。
考試官教諭趙批：聖人化强之績，提點明透。
考試官教諭林批：意周語勁。
《春秋》殊辭以紀化强之效，而不嫌於序績焉。此聖人之化齊，去常情遠矣，卽以序人者而自序，何嫌哉！昔魯之三田，隨夾谷而舉之齊也，說者曰「謝過也」。夫齊之親魯，不寧唯是，前有濟西，後有讙、闡，皆僅以「歸」書；而玆獨以「來歸」爲文，同於屈完之「來盟」者，何邪？噫，此夫子化强之績也。蓋卑屈事人者，以言請之而不足；禮義責人者，以心服之而有餘。故楚之方、漢猶昔也，齊桓一聲王貢之闕，而同好是承，夫亦屈於義也。以彼霸者猶然，而況于王乎！當時鼓譟之齊，不減於楚；而式微之魯，何敢望齊？非夫子當之，幾殆矣。廼攝相從君，秉禮責敵：裔俘却焉，兵車拒焉，野饗
translation_en:
…the tenth year of [Duke Ding]. "The men of Qi restored Huan and Chan." Eighth year of Duke Ai.

Wang Songsun 王松孫

Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Yu 余 comments: The historiographical phrasing is intricate, making it difficult for writers to synthesize. This essay is tightly structured, and its tone and cadence feel all the more resonant.
Examiner Instructor Zhao 趙 comments: The sage's achievement in transforming the strong is highlighted with clarity and penetration.
Examiner Instructor Lin 林 comments: The thought is comprehensive and the language vigorous.

The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) uses distinct phrasing to record the efficacy of transforming the strong, without shying away from recounting [Confucius's own] achievement. In this, the sage's transformation of Qi was far removed from ordinary sentiment; even if he used the phrasing applied to others to recount his own deeds, what cause was there for hesitation! In the past, when Lu's three fields of land were recovered from Qi following the meeting at Jiagu, commentators said, "It was to apologize for their transgression." Now, Qi's conciliatory gestures toward Lu were not limited to this occasion alone: earlier there were the fields west of the Ji River, and later there were Huan and Chan, yet all of those were recorded simply with the word "restored" (gui 歸). Why is it that here alone the text reads "came to restore" (lai gui 來歸), matching the phrasing of Qu Wan 屈完 "coming to covenant" (lai meng 來盟)? Ah! This was the Master's achievement in transforming the strong. For those who serve others with humble subservience find that even begging with words is not enough, whereas those who reprove others with ritual and righteousness find that winning their hearts leaves a surplus. Thus楚's hold over the Fangcheng mountains and the Han River was just as it had been in the past, yet as soon as Duke Huan of Qi 齊桓公 denounced their failure to pay royal tribute, they acceded to a pact of mutual amity—for they too submitted to righteousness. If it was thus even with that hegemon, how much more so with the Way of a true king! At that time, Qi with its clamoring drums was no less formidable than Chu, while declining Lu could hardly dare to compare itself with Qi; had the Master not faced them, it would have been nearly fatal. Thereupon, acting as chief minister in attendance on his lord, he upheld ritual to reprove the adversary: the frontier captives [performers] were driven back, the war chariots were rebuffed, and the setting up of the rustic banquet…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
之設罷焉夫禮至則不爭齊固非終入夷狄之
俗者能不逡巡而謝過以質哉兩君合好而壇
墠之外有奉輿圖而至者非强也我無遷善改
過之迹而感者以天彼匪親愛惠遺之私而應
者亦以天姑亡論其功化之淺深何如而變齊
帖楚其績均焉耳矣故夾谷之下而書齊人來
歸鄆讙龜陰田異於他歸而無嫌於與齊同序
者一以天自處之心乎嗚呼歸田者齊而歸女
樂者亦齊何始焉嚮化之誠後相背之戾也平
===
仲其不在事與尼谿之封躬自沮之無亦限於
命邪雖然有管子則桓霸有晏子景不失令名
然則嬰亦仲之流亞哉
禮記
君子如欲化民成俗其必由學乎玉不琢
不成器人不學不知道是故古之王者
建國君民教學爲先
涂嘉會
同考試官敎諭朱批敎學乃化成先務古今所
punctuated:
之設罷焉。夫禮至則不爭，齊固非終入夷狄之俗者，能不逡巡而謝過以質哉？兩君合好，而壇墠之外有奉輿圖而至者，非强也。我無遷善改過之迹，而感者以天；彼匪親愛惠遺之私，而應者亦以天。姑亡論其功化之淺深何如，而變齊帖楚，其績均焉耳矣。故夾谷之下，而書「齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田」，異於他歸，而無嫌於與齊同序者，一以天自處之心乎！嗚呼！歸田者齊，而歸女樂者亦齊，何始焉嚮化之誠，後相背之戾也？平仲其不在事與？尼谿之封，躬自沮之，無亦限於命邪？雖然，有管子則桓霸，有晏子，景不失令名，然則嬰亦仲之流亞哉！
禮記
「君子如欲化民成俗，其必由學乎！玉不琢，不成器；人不學，不知道。是故古之王者，建國君民，教學爲先。」
涂嘉會
同考試官敎諭朱批：敎學乃化成先務，古今所
translation_en:
…of the open-air banquet was canceled. Now, when ritual propriety reaches its utmost, there is no contention. Since Qi was certainly not a state permanently sunk in the customs of the barbarians, how could it not hesitate, draw back, and apologize for its faults with pledges of good faith? When the two rulers joined in amity, outside the altar grounds there were those who arrived presenting territory and maps—this was not coerced. On our side there was no outward trace of demanding that they move toward the good or reform their errors, for what moved them was Heaven; on their side it was not out of private partiality or friendly gift-giving, for what responded in them was also Heaven. Leaving aside for the moment the question of how shallow or deep the transformative achievement was, in transforming Qi and subduing Chu, the merits were quite equal. Therefore, beneath the entry on the meeting at Jiagu, the Spring and Autumn Annals records: "The men of Qi came to restore the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin." That this differs from other restorations of land, and sees no objection in placing this on a par with Qi's earlier conduct, is entirely due to a mind that conducts itself according to Heaven! Alas! It was Qi that restored the lands, yet it was also Qi that later sent the female musicians. Why was there such sincere turning toward moral transformation at first, and such perverse betrayal afterward? Was Pingzhong [Yan Ying 晏嬰] no longer in office? Yet he had personally blocked the enfeoffment of Confucius at Nixi—was this not after all a limitation imposed by destiny? Even so, with Guanzi [Guan Zhong 管仲], Duke Huan became hegemon, and with Yanzi, Duke Jing did not lose his good name; thus Ying was indeed of the same caliber as Zhong!

Record of Rites (Liji)
"If a ruler wishes to transform the people and perfect their customs, must he not start from education! If jade is not carved, it cannot become a vessel; if a man does not learn, he will not know the Way. Therefore, when the kings of antiquity established states and ruled the people, they made instruction and learning their first priority."

Tu Jiahui 涂嘉會
Associate Examiner Instructor Zhu comments: Instruction and learning are the foremost task in transforming the people and perfecting customs, which in ancient and modern times…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
重也是作發揮透徹末復歸本君身旨哉
考試官教諭趙批措詞嚴整運意周匝
考試官教諭林批題旨融貫
論君子願治有其要而徵諸古之王者焉蓋道
者所繇以適治也學而後知道則化民成俗信
必由之矣宜王者以為先務歟且學術者事功
之本也教化者風俗之原也君子而安於𢥠聞
動眾已也則固可不必於學者如不屑於小康
之陋而慨慕夫帝王之盛欲於民而化之如古
之於變者焉於俗而成之如古之時雍者焉是
遵何術哉其必以大學者賢士之所關也而賢
士者所與共成天下之治也羣英才而樂育之
使皆知明德以立其體羅俊乂而甄陶之使皆
知新民以裕其用則養之有全功用之有實效
民化俗成必由此出矣不觀古王者先務之急
哉蓋人必知道而後可適於治猶玉必成器而
後可適於用也玉之不琢不成器矣人而不學
其能知道乎故王者建萬國以親諸侯而獨急
punctuated:
重也。是作發揮透徹，末復歸本君身，旨哉！
考試官教諭趙批：措詞嚴整，運意周匝。
考試官教諭林批：題旨融貫。
論君子願治有其要，而徵諸古之王者焉。蓋道者，所繇以適治也；學而後知道，則化民成俗，信必由之矣。宜王者以為先務歟！且學術者，事功之本也；教化者，風俗之原也。君子而安於𢥠聞動眾已也，則固可不必於學者；如不屑於小康之陋，而慨慕夫帝王之盛，欲於民而化之，如古之於變者焉，於俗而成之，如古之時雍者焉，是遵何術哉？其必以大學者，賢士之所關也；而賢士者，所與共成天下之治也。羣英才而樂育之，使皆知明德以立其體；羅俊乂而甄陶之，使皆知新民以裕其用。則養之有全功，用之有實效，民化俗成，必由此出矣。不觀古王者先務之急哉？蓋人必知道而後可適於治，猶玉必成器而後可適於用也。玉之不琢，不成器矣；人而不學，其能知道乎？故王者建萬國以親諸侯，而獨急
translation_en:
… valued. This essay develops the theme thoroughly, and at the end returns to the root in the ruler's own person—how meaningful!

Examiner and Instructor Zhao comments: The phrasing is rigorous and well-ordered; the train of thought is comprehensive.

Examiner and Instructor Lin comments: The import of the topic is thoroughly integrated.

This discusses how the noble man who desires good governance possesses its essential point, and verifies it by appeal to the kings of antiquity. Now the Way is that whereby one attains good governance; since one knows the Way only after learning, transforming the people and perfecting customs must truly proceed from this. How fitting that the true king takes it as his first priority! Moreover, scholarship is the root of practical achievement, and moral instruction is the source of customs. If the noble man is content merely with frightening ears and stirring up the multitude [? 𢥠聞動眾], then he certainly need not concern himself with learning. But if he disdains the narrowness of Lesser Tranquility (xiaokang) and ardently admires the flourishing of the Five Emperors and Three Kings—wishing, with respect to the people, to transform them as in the "Oh, they were transformed!" of antiquity, and with respect to customs, to perfect them as in the "harmonious times" of antiquity—then what method should he follow? He must surely recognize that the Great Learning (or imperial academy) is the vital concern of worthy scholars, and that worthy scholars are those with whom one jointly accomplishes the governance of the world. If one gathers brilliant talents and delights in nurturing them, causing them all to know how to illustrate illustrious virtue so as to establish their substance, and nets outstanding men to mold and fashion them, causing them all to know how to renew the people so as to enrich their practical application, then their cultivation will achieve complete success, their employment will yield real efficacy, and the transformation of the people and perfection of customs will necessarily issue from this. Does one not behold the urgency of the first priority of the kings of antiquity? For a man must know the Way before he is fit for governance, just as jade must be fashioned into a vessel before it is fit for use. If jade is not carved, it does not become a vessel; if a man does not learn, how can he know the Way? Therefore, when the true king establishes the myriad states to hold the feudal lords close, he is uniquely urgent…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
於造士之方樹君公以擾兆民而首重夫儲材
之地自王公以及庶人莫不有教是以教爲先
也自國都以至鄉黨莫不有學是以學爲先也
當時黎民由之而厚習俗由之而美則以人皆
知道故孚化爲易耳有志於化成者舍學其何
以哉信乎君道以師道而備治化以教化而彰
君子而誠欲之莫若師王者矣抑觀唐虞之際
禹治水稷稼穡民方知有生之樂而司徒之命
乃諄諄焉則教學之不容一日緩由堯舜而已
===
然矣然史臣賛之一則曰克明峻德一則曰重
華協於帝而後變黎民風四方傳曰堯舜帥天
下以仁而民從之知此則化成之要在教學而
教學之本在君身明君以務學爲急信哉
子曰爲上可望而知也爲下可述而志也
則君不疑於其臣而臣不惑於其君矣
尹吉曰惟尹躬及湯咸有壹德
劉啓元
同考試官教諭朱批通篇無一冗語君臣相得
punctuated:
於造士之方；樹君公以擾兆民，而首重夫儲材之地。自王公以及庶人，莫不有教，是以教爲先也；自國都以至鄉黨，莫不有學，是以學爲先也。當時黎民由之而厚，習俗由之而美，則以人皆知道，故孚化爲易耳。有志於化成者，舍學其何以哉？信乎！君道以師道而備，治化以教化而彰，君子而誠欲之，莫若師王者矣。抑觀唐虞之際，禹治水，稷稼穡，民方知有生之樂，而司徒之命乃諄諄焉，則教學之不容一日緩，由堯舜而已然矣。然史臣賛之，一則曰「克明峻德」，一則曰「重華協於帝」，而後變黎民、風四方。《傳》曰：「堯舜帥天下以仁，而民從之。」知此則化成之要在教學，而教學之本在君身。明君以務學爲急，信哉！

子曰：「爲上可望而知也，爲下可述而志也，則君不疑於其臣，而臣不惑於其君矣。」尹吉曰：「惟尹躬及湯，咸有壹德。」
劉啓元
同考試官教諭朱批：通篇無一冗語，君臣相得
translation_en:
… regarding the methods of cultivating scholars; he establishes rulers and dukes to pacify the millions of people, yet places foremost importance on the places for storing talent. From kings and dukes down to the common people, there is no one without instruction, which is to put instruction first; from the capital down to the rural districts and villages, there is no place without schools, which is to put learning first. At that time, the common people thereby became generous, and customs thereby became admirable; this was simply because everyone knew the Way, making it easy to inspire and transform them. For one who aspires to complete transformation through moral teaching, without schools, by what means could it be achieved? Truly, the Way of the ruler is made complete through the Way of the teacher, and transformative governance is made manifest through educational transformation. If the noble man genuinely desires this, there is nothing better than taking the ancient kings as his teacher. Moreover, looking at the era of Tang and Yu [Yao and Shun], when Yu controlled the waters and Ji taught sowing and reaping, the people were only just beginning to know the joy of living, yet the charge to the Minister of Education (situ) was given with earnestness and repetition. Thus, that teaching and learning cannot be delayed for a single day was already so from the time of Yao and Shun. Yet when the historian praised them, of the one he said, "He was able to make illustrious his lofty virtue," and of the other he said, "Hissplendor doubled that of the Emperor," and only afterward were the black-haired people transformed and the four quarters influenced. The Commentary (Zhuan) says: "Yao and Shun led the world with benevolence, and the people followed them." Understanding this, one sees that the essential point of completing moral transformation lies in teaching and learning, and the root of teaching and learning lies in the ruler's own person. That an enlightened ruler takes devotion to learning as his urgent priority—how true indeed!

"The Master said: 'When the one above can be looked at and known, and the one below can be recounted and remembered, then the ruler does not doubt his minister, and the minister is not perplexed by his ruler.' Yin Ji [Yi Yin] said: 'It was that I, Yin, and Tang both possessed pure and single-minded virtue.'"
By Liu Qiyuan 劉啓元.
Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Zhu comments: Throughout the entire piece there is not a single superfluous word; the mutual trust between ruler and minister…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
之意自是明盡且結知重尹此必深于事君大義者
考試官教諭趙批筆力遒勁思致瑩潔
考試官教諭林批詞意冠冕
論君臣以誠而相得必引書以證之也蓋君臣
相得而後功業弘也誠則無疑惑矣即書之所
稱一德者何以加焉見於緇衣者若曰君臣之
相須亦甚殷矣得明君而事之臣之願也得良
臣而任之君之欲也然明良何由以交哉亦曰
誠而已矣彼爲君者以上而臨下毎患於難知
===
也而君之待臣者一於誠則自下而望之外之
所以寵遇我者即其中之所以倚毗我矣不可
望而知乎爲臣者以下而奉上毎嫌於無述也
而臣之事君者一於誠則自上而述之今之所
以照當世者即其後之所以垂休光矣不可述
而志乎惟上之可知故臣不徒見君之貌而見
其心雖堂陛之尊有不能隔者而圖報之益堅
矣又何疑於其臣耶惟下之可志故君不徒信
臣之名而信其實雖讒邪之口有不能入者而
punctuated:
之意，自是明盡，且結知重尹，此必深于事君大義者。
考試官教諭趙批：筆力遒勁，思致瑩潔。
考試官教諭林批：詞意冠冕。
論君臣以誠而相得，必引《書》以證之也。蓋君臣相得，而後功業弘也，誠則無疑惑矣。即《書》之所稱「一德」者，何以加焉？見於《緇衣》者若曰：君臣之相須，亦甚殷矣。得明君而事之，臣之願也；得良臣而任之，君之欲也。然明良何由以交哉？亦曰誠而已矣。彼爲君者，以上而臨下，毎患於難知也。而君之待臣者一於誠，則自下而望之，外之所以寵遇我者，即其中之所以倚毗我矣，不可望而知乎？爲臣者，以下而奉上，毎嫌於無述也。而臣之事君者一於誠，則自上而述之，今之所以照當世者，即其後之所以垂休光矣，不可述而志乎？惟上之可知，故臣不徒見君之貌，而見其心。雖堂陛之尊有不能隔者，而圖報之益堅矣，又何疑於其臣耶？惟下之可志，故君不徒信臣之名，而信其實。雖讒邪之口有不能入者，而
translation_en:
… [the meaning of mutual accord between ruler and minister] is naturally clear and exhaustive, and in its conclusion it knows how to give weight to Yi Yin; this must be someone deeply versed in the great duty of serving one's ruler.
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Zhao comments: The brushwork is vigorous and strong; the train of thought is lustrous and pure.
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Lin comments: The diction and meaning are dignified and exalted.
In discussing how ruler and minister achieve mutual accord through sincerity, one must cite the Book of Documents (Shu) to verify it. Indeed, only when ruler and minister are in mutual accord can their achievements and enterprises be made grand; when there is sincerity, there is neither suspicion nor perplexity. Even what the Book of Documents calls "pure and single virtue" (yide)—how could anything surpass this? What appears in the "Black Robes" ("Ziyi") chapter [of the Record of Rites] is as if to say: The mutual need between ruler and minister is indeed most ardent. To obtain an enlightened ruler and serve him is the wish of the minister; to obtain a worthy minister and entrust him with responsibility is the desire of the ruler. Yet by what means do an enlightened ruler and a worthy minister enter into fellowship? It is simply called sincerity, and nothing more. Now, he who is the ruler presides over those below from above, and there is always the worry that he is difficult to know. Yet if the ruler's treatment of his ministers is wholly unified in sincerity, then when they look up to him from below, the outward favor and reception he bestows upon them is none other than the inward reliance and trust he places in them—can he not be known simply by being looked upon? He who is a minister serves his superior from below, and there is always the suspicion that his deeds cannot be recounted. Yet if the minister's service to his ruler is wholly unified in sincerity, then when his conduct is recounted from above, that by which he illuminates the present age today is none other than that by which he will hand down glorious luster to posterity—can his deeds not be recounted and recorded? Because the superior can be known, the minister sees not merely the ruler's countenance, but sees his heart; even the exaltedness of the hall and throne steps cannot create a barrier between them, and [the minister's] resolve to repay him grows ever firmer—how then could the ruler have any suspicion toward his minister? Because the subordinate's conduct can be recorded, the ruler trusts not merely the minister's reputation, but trusts his reality; even the mouths of slanderers and the wicked cannot find entry, and…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
委任之愈專矣又何惑於其君耶載觀之尹吉
曰惟尹躬及湯咸有壹德夫湯齊聖之君也尹
王者之佐也其始也湯三聘尹而不以爲屈尹
五就湯而不以爲要其旣也湯舉天下而畀之
尹尹舉其身以爲天下果能壹德以有成也君
子曰湯可知也尹可志也壹德者誠故不貳也
三復尹吉之言而可以識萬世君臣之義矣雖
然在君者不可過求在臣者所當自盡伊尹之
事成湯也易而其事太甲也雖然左右贊襄卒
===
能成君德而中興焉何哉蓋天民先覺其心純
乎天也心純乎天則天下萬世皆能諒之故當
其時主不疑臣不忌赫然中興之業迄今頌之
不衰也噫玆固人臣事君之準也
第貳塲
論
王道至大至正
饒位
同考試官敎諭陳批王道正大作者類多竝言
punctuated:
委任之愈專矣，又何惑於其君耶？載觀之《尹吉》曰：「惟尹躬及湯，咸有壹德。」夫湯，齊聖之君也；尹，王者之佐也。其始也，湯三聘尹而不以爲屈，尹五就湯而不以爲要；其旣也，湯舉天下而畀之尹，尹舉其身以爲天下，果能壹德以有成也。君子曰：湯可知也，尹可志也。壹德者，誠故不貳也。三復《尹吉》之言，而可以識萬世君臣之義矣。雖然，在君者不可過求，在臣者所當自盡。伊尹之事成湯也易，而其事太甲也雖〔難〕。然左右贊襄，卒能成君德而中興焉，何哉？蓋天民先覺，其心純乎天也。心純乎天，則天下萬世皆能諒之。故當其時，主不疑，臣不忌，赫然中興之業，迄今頌之不衰也。噫！玆固人臣事君之準也。

第貳塲
論
王道至大至正
饒位
同考試官敎諭陳批：王道正大，作者類多竝言，
translation_en:
… his delegation of authority becomes ever more exclusive; how then could he be misled regarding his ruler? Look further at the "Words of Yin" (Yin ji), which says: "Both Yin himself and Tang possessed pure and constant virtue." Now Tang was a ruler of consummate sagacity, and Yi Yin was the assistant to a true king. At the outset, Tang thrice invited Yin with gifts without considering it a humiliation, and Yin five times went to Tang without considering it self-seeking; afterward, Tang entrusted the whole realm to Yin, and Yin dedicated his whole person to the realm, so that in the end they were able to achieve success through pure and constant virtue. The gentleman says: Tang could be known, and Yin could be recorded. To have pure and constant virtue is to be sincere and therefore undivided. By repeatedly pondering the words of the "Words of Yin," one can understand the righteous principle between ruler and minister for ten thousand generations. Even so, what rests with the ruler cannot be demanded to excess, whereas what rests with the minister is what he ought to exhaust in himself. Yi Yin's service to Cheng Tang was easy, whereas his service to Tai Jia was [difficult? transcription reads 雖 "although" for 難 "difficult"]. Yet by assisting and supporting him at his side, he was ultimately able to bring the ruler's virtue to completion and achieve a dynastic restoration—why was this? It was because, as one among Heaven's people who was first to awaken, his mind was purely aligned with Heaven. When one's mind is purely aligned with Heaven, the whole world and ten thousand generations can understand and trust his intentions. Therefore, in his time, the sovereign did not harbor suspicion and fellow ministers did not feel jealousy, and his illustrious enterprise of restoration has been praised without fail down to the present day. Ah! This is truly the standard for how a minister serves his ruler.

Second Session
Discourse
"The Kingly Way is Most Great and Most Correct"
Rao Wei
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Chen: Concerning the correctness and greatness of the Kingly Way, most writers discuss the two together; …

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
此篇俱極理要歸本君心而筆勢縱橫妙思溢發必超然玄覽士也
同考試官教諭李批反覆數千言無一塵句而
筆力高古意味深長至析王伯之辨愈入精微矣
考試官教諭趙批章法句法逼近兩京
考試官教諭林批議論波瀾迥出時調
王者之道天道也純心以運治是其道之所以
同乎天也何者天下之治非可以一切法度整
齊而約束之王者不顓任法而必有拊摩涵育
天下之具以濟法於不窮故其道卓然與天比
===
隆焉斯道也張設於治則恢廓而不可禦而宰
制於心則純一而不可雜心也者道之𢇁係而
治之樞紐也不能正其心則所為皆苟道也而
徒恃其法曰吾有以治天下豈不難哉宋儒胡
氏曰天道至大至正王道至大至正蓋大者其
治之成也正者其心之運也心與治相表裏而
王道可幾而睹歟今天天窿然覆物以形而穆
然周之以神舉萬彙而亭育陶冶使皆生成於
元造之中其道之大如此然豈物物焉噓拂而
punctuated:
此篇俱極理要，歸本君心；而筆勢縱橫，妙思溢發，必超然玄覽士也。
同考試官教諭李批：反覆數千言，無一塵句，而筆力高古，意味深長。至析王伯之辨，愈入精微矣。
考試官教諭趙批：章法句法，逼近兩京。
考試官教諭林批：議論波瀾，迥出時調。
王者之道，天道也。純心以運治，是其道之所以同乎天也。何者？天下之治，非可以一切法度整齊而約束之。王者不顓任法，而必有拊摩涵育天下之具，以濟法於不窮，故其道卓然與天比隆焉。斯道也，張設於治則恢廓而不可禦，而宰制於心則純一而不可雜。心也者，道之𢇁係而治之樞紐也。不能正其心，則所為皆苟道也；而徒恃其法曰「吾有以治天下」，豈不難哉！宋儒胡氏曰：「天道至大至正，王道至大至正。」蓋大者，其治之成也；正者，其心之運也。心與治相表裏，而王道可幾而睹歟！今天天窿然覆物以形，而穆然周之以神，舉萬彙而亭育陶冶，使皆生成於元造之中，其道之大如此。然豈物物焉噓拂而
translation_en:
… In this essay, both concepts reach the utmost essence of principle and trace their root back to the ruler's mind. Moreover, the momentum of the brush sweeps freely and marvelous thoughts overflow—he must be a scholar of transcendent and profound vision.

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Li: Going back and forth over several thousand words, there is not a single mundane sentence, while the vigor of the brush is lofty and ancient, and its resonance deep and lasting. When it comes to analyzing the distinction between the true king and the hegemon, it enters ever further into subtlety.

Comment by Examiner Instructor Zhao: The structure of the composition and the phrasing of the sentences closely approach the style of the Two Capitals [Western and Eastern Han].

Comment by Examiner Instructor Lin: The surging waves of his argumentation stand far above contemporary conventions.

The Way of the true king is the Way of Heaven. Conducting governance with a pure mind is whereby his Way is identical to that of Heaven. Why is this so? The governance of all under Heaven cannot be made uniform and restrained merely by sweeping laws and regulations. The true king does not rely exclusively on law, but must possess the means to soothe, cherish, and nurture the world so as to supplement the law endlessly; therefore, his Way stands eminently equal in grandeur to Heaven. When this Way is spread forth in governance, it is vast and irresistible; when it is mastered within the mind, it is pure, unified, and unadulterated. The mind is that to which the Way is bound and the pivot of governance. If one cannot rectify one's mind, then whatever one does follows a makeshift way; and if one relies solely on laws, saying, "I have the means to govern all under Heaven," is that not difficult indeed! The Song Confucian Master Hu [Hu Anguo 胡安國] said: "The Way of Heaven is supremely great and supremely upright; the Way of the true king is supremely great and supremely upright." For its greatness is the completion of his governance, and its uprightness is the operation of his mind. When mind and governance form the inner and outer aspects of one another, can the Way of the true king not nearly be witnessed? Now Heaven arches high above, covering all things with its form, and silently encompasses them with its spirit. It takes up the myriad categories of beings, nurturing and molding them so that all are generated and brought to completion within primordial creation—such is the greatness of its Way. Yet how could it breathe upon and brush each and every thing individually, and…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
彫刻之哉功有所不宰誠有所不貳曰鼓物而
無容心者天道之正也故曰大者正也正大而
天地之情可見矣天地包萬物以竝生而普之
以無心王者聯萬民以竝治而出之以無私書
之論皇極也無有偏黨無有反側無有作好作
惡而總之曰王道正直至於會極歸極舉天下
而囿於蕩平之域則大順之治成矣斯非王道
由正而大之明驗歟且王道曷爲而始也天生
民而樹之君豈其使一人巍然寄於民上而無
===
所注厝者哉蓋嘗覽三代之興陳經立紀以爲
民極者何其綢繆而纖悉也天下之勢渙而無
以統也而侯衞藩屛置焉天下之分黷而無以
辨也而官師位序列焉天下之人羣居而無以
齊也而符璽量衡設焉無以養也而井牧貢賦
定焉無以敎也而庠序絃誦備焉無以衞也而
卒伍蒐閲具焉人皆曰是王者治天下之法也
而非道也殊不知王者爲治不盡恃乎紀綱法
度之詳而必有禮以節之樂以和之仁以漸之
punctuated: 彫刻之哉？功有所不宰，誠有所不貳，曰：「鼓物而無容心」者，天道之正也。故曰：「大者，正也；正大而天地之情可見矣。」天地包萬物以竝生，而普之以無心；王者聯萬民以竝治，而出之以無私。《書》之論皇極也，「無有偏黨，無有反側，無有作好作惡」，而總之曰「王道正直」；至於「會極歸極」，舉天下而囿於蕩平之域，則大順之治成矣。斯非王道由正而大之明驗歟？且王道曷爲而始也？天生民而樹之君，豈其使一人巍然寄於民上而無所注厝者哉？蓋嘗覽三代之興，陳經立紀以爲民極者，何其綢繆而纖悉也！天下之勢渙而無以統也，而侯衞藩屛置焉；天下之分黷而無以辨也，而官師位序列焉；天下之人羣居而無以齊也，而符璽量衡設焉；無以養也，而井牧貢賦定焉；無以敎也，而庠序絃誦備焉；無以衞也，而卒伍蒐閲具焉。人皆曰：「是王者治天下之法也，而非道也。」殊不知王者爲治，不盡恃乎紀綱法度之詳，而必有禮以節之、樂以和之、仁以漸之、
translation_en:
… carve and engrave them? Its achievements are not consciously presided over, and its sincerity admits no duplicity; what is called "stimulating things without harboring deliberate intent" is the rectitude of the Way of Heaven. Therefore it is said: "Greatness means rectitude; through rectitude and greatness the true disposition of Heaven and Earth can be seen." Heaven and Earth encompass the myriad things so that they live together, extending to them universally without deliberate mind; the true king unites the myriad people so that they are governed together, acting toward them without selfishness. When the Book of Documents (Shu) discusses the August Ultimate, it speaks of having "no partiality or factionalism, no perversity or deflection, no indulgence in personal likes or dislikes," summing it up by saying, "The Kingly Way is straight and upright"; and when it reaches the point of "converging upon the Ultimate and returning to the Ultimate," encompassing the whole world within a realm of broad impartiality, then the governance of great harmony is achieved. Is this not clear proof that the Kingly Way attains greatness through rectitude?

Moreover, why did the Kingly Way begin? When Heaven gave birth to the people and established a ruler for them, how could it have meant to place one man loftily above the people without anything for him to institute and arrange? Indeed, when we survey the rise of the Three Dynasties, how thorough and meticulous they were in setting forth cardinal principles and establishing regulations to serve as the standard for the people! Because the power of the world was scattered and lacked unity, the feudatories, guard zones, and protective screens were established; because the status distinctions in the world were muddled and lacked differentiation, the ranks and orders of officials and instructors were arrayed; because the people of the world lived in crowds and lacked uniformity, tallies, seals, measures, and weights were instituted; because they lacked means of nourishment, the well-field pastures, tribute, and taxes were fixed; because they lacked means of education, community schools and the recitation of texts to stringed instruments were provided; because they lacked means of defense, military squads, seasonal hunts, and troop reviews were prepared. Everyone says, "These are the laws by which a true king governs the world, and not the Way." Little do they realize that in governing, a true king does not rely entirely upon the detailed elaboration of institutional frameworks and legal measures, but must have ritual to regulate them, music to harmonize them, benevolence to imbue them, …

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
義以摩之其導民也循循乎懇惻而忠厚紆餘
而易簡使天下揉伏馴擾帖然由吾之法以成
敦龐純固之盛此王道之卓越乎萬世也所謂
至大而至正者也故道在朝廷非必日省而月
中也然而休采之臣摶心揖志以象其指者有
同式矣道在邦國非必家至而戶曉也然而樂
利之甿矯手頓足以詠其澤者有同戴矣道在
天下又非必馳騖乎兼容而併包也然而六服
承德四夷來賓執萬玉累九譯以效順者有同
===
===
嚮矣王道之行也朞一世而尊之如天地仰之
如日月親之如父母歸之如流水淳化旁霑洋
溢乎方內外旣其久也雅頌管絃之聲歷數千
歲而勿絕豈不誠至大矣哉而所以權輿之者
固在心也王者之心主之以誠慤行之以公溥
而要歸於至正天理盎然充滿具足無有虧欠
無有假借無有歆羨制立而無私造作功著而
無私炫飾法用而無私控揣惠周而無私施予
機智巧偽洗濯消融靡絲毫留於胸臆故武不
punctuated: 義以摩之。其導民也，循循乎懇惻而忠厚，紆餘而易簡，使天下揉伏馴擾，帖然由吾之法，以成敦龐純固之盛。此王道之卓越乎萬世也，所謂至大而至正者也。故道在朝廷，非必日省而月中也，然而休采之臣，摶心揖志以象其指者，有同式矣；道在邦國，非必家至而戶曉也，然而樂利之甿，矯手頓足以詠其澤者，有同戴矣；道在天下，又非必馳騖乎兼容而併包也，然而六服承德，四夷來賓，執萬玉、累九譯以效順者，有同嚮矣。王道之行也，朞一世而尊之如天地，仰之如日月，親之如父母，歸之如流水。淳化旁霑，洋溢乎方內外，旣其久也，雅頌管絃之聲，歷數千歲而勿絕，豈不誠至大矣哉！而所以權輿之者，固在心也。王者之心，主之以誠慤，行之以公溥，而要歸於至正。天理盎然，充滿具足，無有虧欠，無有假借，無有歆羨。制立而無私造作，功著而無私炫飾，法用而無私控揣，惠周而無私施予。機智巧偽，洗濯消融，靡絲毫留於胸臆。故武不
translation_en: …and rightness to polish them. In guiding the people, he proceeds step by step with earnest sympathy and loyal generosity, in a manner unhurried yet easy and simple, causing all under Heaven to be pliant and tamed, docilely following our laws so as to achieve a flourishing age of thick simplicity and pure solidity. This is why the Kingly Way excels across ten thousand generations, and is what is called supremely great and supremely upright. Therefore, when the Way is at court, one need not inspect daily and examine monthly; yet the illustrious officials who unite their hearts and join their wills to emulate his intent all share the same model. When the Way is in the regional states, one need not visit every family and inform every household; yet the commoners who rejoice in its benefits, raising their hands and stamping their feet to sing of its grace, all share the same reverence. When the Way is in all under Heaven, one again need not rush about striving to encompass and absorb everything; yet the six domains receive his virtue and the four barbarian quarters come as guests, holding ten thousand jades and communicating through ninefold translations to offer allegiance, all sharing the same allegiance. When the Kingly Way is practiced, within a generation people honor him like Heaven and Earth, look up to him like the sun and moon, love him like parents, and turn to him like flowing water. Pure transformation moistens far and wide, brimming over both within and beyond the realm; and after a long time, the sounds of the Odes and Hymns on pipes and strings continue for several thousand years without ceasing. Is this not truly supremely great! Yet that from which it originates lies indeed in the mind. The mind of the true king is governed by sincere honesty, practiced with impartial breadth, and ultimately returns to supreme uprightness. Heavenly principle abounds within it, full and complete, without deficiency, without pretense, and without covetousness. Institutions are established without selfish contrivance; achievements are made manifest without selfish ostentation; laws are applied without selfish manipulation; and favors are distributed universally without selfish bestowal. Calculative cleverness and crafty deceit are washed away and melted off, leaving not a single thread in his breast. Thus his footsteps do not…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
踰閶闔而聲氣之孚捷於影響言不及表著而
德信之感堅於金石此所謂心之至正而王道
繇以出焉者也故王者之心洞達純白如鑑之
明如衡之平斤斤焉規之矩之準之繩之而無
少差跌者其正也是所以爲致大之基也王者
之治恢閎廣博如水之源溢爲萬派木之根蔚
爲千尋而漸漬之末流播散之餘種猶勃乎不
可禦遏者其大也是所以爲積正之效也故必
有純王之心而後有純王之道有純王之道而
===
後有純王之治參相成者也且夫王者之爲天
下威命靈爽非不運也而有不假威而震者焉
禁誡憲令非不宣也而有不藉令而喻者焉物
采文章非不華也而有不倚文而辨者焉何則
其心正也心正則精神念慮日旁皇周浹於海
寓化理所運自可拱巳而不勞王道之隆至於
以天下爲一家中國爲一人者非意之也後之
人君其心未必能正而矻矻焉疲思竭知以炫
逐乎外由是恣睢驅迫之威行焉而窮束縛籠
punctuated: 踰閶闔，而聲氣之孚捷於影響；言不及表著，而德信之感堅於金石。此所謂心之至正，而王道繇以出焉者也。故王者之心，洞達純白，如鑑之明，如衡之平，斤斤焉規之矩之，準之繩之，而無少差跌者，其正也，是所以爲致大之基也；王者之治，恢閎廣博，如水之源溢爲萬派，木之根蔚爲千尋，而漸漬之末流、播散之餘種，猶勃乎不可禦遏者，其大也，是所以爲積正之效也。故必有純王之心，而後有純王之道；有純王之道，而後有純王之治，參相成者也。且夫王者之爲天下，威命靈爽非不運也，而有不假威而震者焉；禁誡憲令非不宣也，而有不藉令而喻者焉；物采文章非不華也，而有不倚文而辨者焉。何則？其心正也。心正則精神念慮日旁皇周浹於海寓，化理所運，自可拱巳而不勞。王道之隆，至於以天下爲一家、中國爲一人者，非意之也。後之人君，其心未必能正，而矻矻焉疲思竭知以炫逐乎外。由是恣睢驅迫之威行焉而窮，束縛籠
translation_en:
… step beyond the palace gates, yet the trust inspired by his reputation and ethos responds more swiftly than shadow or echo; his words do not reach beyond the court stands, yet the moral influence of his virtue and good faith is firmer than metal and stone. This is what is meant by the supreme rectitude of the mind, from which the Kingly Way issues forth.

Therefore, the mind of a true king is thoroughly clear and purely white, as bright as a mirror and as level as a balance; meticulously measuring with compass and square, leveling and aligning with water-level and plumb-line without the slightest error or slip—this is its rectitude, and it is what serves as the foundation for achieving greatness. The governance of a true king is vast and comprehensive, like a fountainhead of water overflowing into ten thousand streams, or the root of a tree flourishing to a height of a thousand fathoms, while even the farthest reaches of its soaking currents and the scattered remnants of its seeds still surge forth irrepressibly—this is its greatness, and it is what serves as the effect of accumulated rectitude. Thus, only when there is the mind of a pure king can there be the Way of a pure king; and only when there is the Way of a pure king can there be the governance of a pure king—the three mutually bring one another to completion.

Moreover, in a true king's governing of the world, it is not that his august commands and numinous majesty do not operate, yet there is that which inspires awe without relying on severity; it is not that his prohibitions, warnings, and statutory ordinances are not promulgated, yet there is that which brings understanding without depending on decrees; it is not that his ritual emblems and institutional forms are not splendid, yet there is that which maintains distinctions without leaning on outward ornament. Why is this? Because his mind is rectified. When the mind is rectified, his spirit, thoughts, and deliberations daily circulate and pervade everywhere within the seas, and as transformative governance operates, he can naturally fold his hands in composure without toil. That the flourishing of the Kingly Way reaches the point of taking all under Heaven as one family and the Central Lands as one person is not a matter of mere contrivance.

Rulers of later ages could not necessarily rectify their minds, yet they labored tirelessly, exhausting their thoughts and draining their cleverness to dazzle and pursue external things. Consequently, arbitrary and coercive severity was put into practice, only to end in exhaustion; binding and ensnaring …

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
絡之令施焉而沮藻繢彫飾之文工焉而敝其
爲治也日趨於苟且簡陋之歸偏曲而不通踦
缺而不具規摹所立不勝其淺隘陃小而去皇
極之中正王道之大全遠矣故曰粹而王駁而
伯王伯粹駁之判在幾微眇忽而其究懸於千
里不可不察也自夫世之人不核其根而徒課
效於末跡則曰素朴之化奚與夫驩虞之可喜
也必世之仁奚與夫速成之爲快也孰知王者
之治雖不規規圖耀於眾所見聞而浹肌膚淪
===
骨髓者固已膠結而不可解伯者日擾擾焉塗
天下之耳目而術之既窮則掩左而右動鎮前
而後起卒至於齟齬衡決而不可收拾王者之
業雖不能取成於倉卒而制定功立則垂之來
世詠歌舞蹈莫有厭斁之意伯者徇情以飾虛
於旦夕而一振之後無復餘味終霍然冰釋爾
矣譬猶樸桶椎輪利用於堅久而粉藻丹繪者
不歷時而渝和風甘雨收功於噓潤而衝溢凌
暴者不終朝而止假令以王伯而較論其治效
punctuated: 絡之令施焉而沮，藻繢彫飾之文工焉而敝。其爲治也，日趨於苟且簡陋之歸，偏曲而不通，踦缺而不具，規摹所立，不勝其淺隘陃小，而去皇極之中正、王道之大全遠矣。故曰：「粹而王，駁而伯。」王伯粹駁之判，在幾微眇忽，而其究懸於千里，不可不察也。自夫世之人不核其根，而徒課效於末跡，則曰：「素朴之化，奚與夫驩虞之可喜也？必世之仁，奚與夫速成之爲快也？」孰知王者之治，雖不規規圖耀於眾所見聞，而浹肌膚、淪骨髓者，固已膠結而不可解；伯者日擾擾焉塗天下之耳目，而術之既窮，則掩左而右動，鎮前而後起，卒至於齟齬衡決而不可收拾。王者之業，雖不能取成於倉卒，而制定功立，則垂之來世，詠歌舞蹈，莫有厭斁之意；伯者徇情以飾虛於旦夕，而一振之後，無復餘味，終霍然冰釋爾矣。譬猶樸桶椎輪，利用於堅久，而粉藻丹繪者，不歷時而渝；和風甘雨，收功於噓潤，而衝溢凌暴者，不終朝而止。假令以王伯而較論其治效，
translation_en:
… órdenes of binding and ensnarement are applied yet fall frustrated, and the refinements of ornate painting and carved embellishment are expertly wrought yet wear out in ruin. As for their governance, day by day it gravitates toward makeshift expediency and crude inadequacy: partial and crooked without reaching through, limping and defective without completeness. The framework they establish is overwhelmingly shallow, narrow, mean, and petty, far removed from the central rectitude of the August Ultimate and the great perfection of the Kingly Way.
