Therefore it is said: "When pure, one is a True King; when mixed, one is a Hegemon." The distinction between the purity of the True King and the admixture of the Hegemon lies in the most subtle and minute beginnings, yet in the end they are separated by a thousand li—this cannot go unexamined.

Because people of the world do not verify the root, but merely measure efficacy by superficial traces, they say: "How can plain and unadorned transformation compare to the delight of boisterous merriment (huanyu)? How can benevolence that takes a generation to mature compare to the satisfaction of quick success?" Who among them realizes that although the governance of a True King does not busily scheme to dazzle what the multitude sees and hears, that which soaks into the skin and flesh and penetrates the bones and marrow is already firmly bound together and cannot be undone? The Hegemon, day after day, restlessly smears over the ears and eyes of the world; yet once his stratagems are exhausted, he covers the left only for the right to stir, suppresses the front only for the rear to rise up, until at last everything falls into discord and bursts its banks beyond recovery. Although the enterprise of a True King cannot be brought to completion in haste, once his institutions are settled and his achievements established, they are handed down to future generations, who sing and dance in praise of them without ever growing weary. The Hegemon indulges passions to dress up empty appearances for a single morning or evening; after a single burst of vigor, there is no lingering savor, and in the end it vanishes suddenly like melting ice. It is just like uncarved wooden vessels and solid, spoke-less wheels, which are useful for their durability and permanence, whereas things adorned with white powder, water-plant patterns, and vermilion paint fade and spoil before much time has passed; or like gentle breezes and sweet rains, which achieve their effect by softly moistening, whereas surging floods and violent storms cease before the morning is out. Even if we were to compare the True King and the Hegemon merely in terms of the efficacy of their governance…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
固有相萬者矣周德下替伯之盛者莫尚乎齊
桓九合一匡攘夷尊華之功非不燁然可觀也
然宮中七市女閭七百其本之不端而徒以詐
力之習媮取近利故一振矜而叛者蠭起功烈
曾不能以訖身仲尼之徒恥而不道誠小之也
漢之興也承敝捄變不務襲跡於三代而雜伯
王道行之夫王之與伯金之鍮石玉之碔砆禾
之稂莠也邪正之幾間不容髮雜而行之是伯
而已矣何王之足云哉然則世變之趨將汎汎
===
乎如舟流之靡届而走丸峻坂之必極也三代
之盛其終不復矣乎嗟乎曦馭馳於蒙谷晨而
晅耀蟄蟲潛於坏戶春則振鳴故法古以興化
者知道之君也矯世以易俗者善治之主也漢
文帝一尚恭儉而貫朽粟紅煙火萬里唐太宗
一敦仁義而外戶不閉行旅不齎糧夫文帝之
恭儉彊勉而非純也太宗之仁義假襲而非真
也而其效已章灼若是矣況粹乎一出於正者
功化之隆又當何如哉荀卿曰國者巨用之則
punctuated: 固有相萬者矣。周德下替，伯之盛者莫尚乎齊桓。九合一匡、攘夷尊華之功，非不燁然可觀也；然宮中七市，女閭七百，其本之不端，而徒以詐力之習，媮取近利，故一振矜而叛者蠭起，功烈曾不能以訖身。仲尼之徒恥而不道，誠小之也。漢之興也，承敝捄變，不務襲跡於三代，而雜伯王道行之。夫王之與伯，金之鍮石、玉之碔砆、禾之稂莠也。邪正之幾，間不容髮，雜而行之，是伯而已矣，何王之足云哉！然則世變之趨，將汎汎乎如舟流之靡届，而走丸峻坂之必極也，三代之盛，其終不復矣乎？嗟乎！曦馭馳於蒙谷，晨而晅耀；蟄蟲潛於坏戶，春則振鳴。故法古以興化者，知道之君也；矯世以易俗者，善治之主也。漢文帝一尚恭儉，而貫朽粟紅，煙火萬里；唐太宗一敦仁義，而外戶不閉，行旅不齎糧。夫文帝之恭儉，彊勉而非純也；太宗之仁義，假襲而非真也，而其效已章灼若是矣。況粹乎一出於正者，功化之隆，又當何如哉！荀卿曰：「國者，巨用之則
translation_en: …there is indeed a ten-thousandfold difference between them. When the virtue of the Zhou declined, none among the flourishing hegemons surpassed Duke Huan of Qi 齊桓. His achievements in nine times assembling the lords and once rectifying the realm, and in repelling the barbarians and honoring the Chinese, were not without brilliant splendor to behold. Yet with seven markets inside his palace and seven hundred brothels, his foundation was not upright. He merely relied on habits of deceit and force to opportunistically seize immediate profit; thus, the moment he grew boastful and arrogant, rebels swarmed up like bees, and his meritorious achievements could not even last out his own lifetime. The disciples of Confucius were ashamed to speak of him, truly considering him petty. When the Han arose, inheriting a decadent system and remedying its crises, it did not strive to follow in the footsteps of the Three Dynasties, but practiced a mixture of the ways of the hegemon and the true king. Now, the true king and the hegemon are like gold and brass, jade and worthless stone, or grain and weeds. The subtle dividing line between crooked and upright does not admit a hair's breadth; to mix them in practice is simply to be a hegemon—how could it be worthy of being called the way of the true king! If this is so, then will the trend of worldly decline drift aimlessly like an unmoored boat that never reaches shore, or roll down a steep slope like a pellet that must hit the bottom, so that the flourishing of the Three Dynasties will never be restored? Alas! Though the sun's chariot races down into the Meng Valley, at dawn it shines brightly again; though hibernating insects hide within their sealed burrows, in spring they stir and chirp. Therefore, he who models himself on antiquity to revive transformative teaching is a ruler who understands the Way; he who rectifies the age to change customs is a sovereign skilled in governance. As soon as Emperor Wen of Han 漢文帝 esteemed reverence and frugality, the strings of cash rotted in the treasuries, the grain turned red with age in the granaries, and hearth fires stretched for ten thousand li; as soon as Emperor Taizong of Tang 唐太宗 emphasized benevolence and righteousness, outer doors were not bolted at night and travelers did not need to carry provisions. Now, Emperor Wen's reverence and frugality were forced rather than pure, and Taizong's benevolence and righteousness were borrowed rather than genuine, yet their results were already as manifest and brilliant as this. How much greater, then, would be the flourishing of achievements and moral transformation for one whose actions issue purely and entirely from what is upright! Xun Qing 荀卿 (Xunzi) said: "As for the state, if one uses it on a grand scale, then…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
大本大而王蘇軾氏曰王道不可以小用也夫
人君不能恢拓治功於至大者特繇正之未至
耳誠純心定志不駁雜於功利之私不遷惑於
因循之陋則上理可登而三王可四此固還至
而立有效者也君天下者尚無阻其至大而務
先圖其至正也哉
表
擬
上以
御製聽
經筵官講大學衍義詩示輔臣輔臣依韻恭
和
命彙爲一冊名曰翊學詩謝表嘉靖六年
李藻
同考試官敎諭樊批敘事冲融摛詞貫徹模寫
明良意象忠敬藹然他作非不工有此翩翩神采否耶
同考試官學正翁批語如戛石意若貫珠六朝
之精華唐宋之風度此表兼得之矣
punctuated:
大，本大而王。蘇軾氏曰：「王道不可以小用也。」夫人君不能恢拓治功於至大者，特繇正之未至耳。誠純心定志，不駁雜於功利之私，不遷惑於因循之陋，則上理可登，而三王可四，此固還至而立有效者也。君天下者，尚無阻其至大，而務先圖其至正也哉！
表
擬上以御製《聽經筵官講〈大學衍義〉詩》示輔臣，輔臣依韻恭和，命彙爲一冊，名曰《翊學詩》謝表〔嘉靖六年〕
李藻
同考試官敎諭樊批：敘事冲融，摛詞貫徹，模寫明良意象，忠敬藹然。他作非不工，有此翩翩神采否耶？
同考試官學正翁批：語如戛石，意若貫珠，六朝之精華，唐宋之風度，此表兼得之矣。
translation_en:
… is great; when the foundation is great, one reigns as a true king." Su Shi 蘇軾 said: "The Kingly Way cannot be put to small use." Indeed, when a ruler is unable to expand the achievements of governance to the utmost greatness, it is merely because his rectitude has not yet reached its utmost. If he truly purifies his mind and fixes his resolve—unadulterated by the selfishness of utilitarian gain and unswayed by the base habit of passive routine—then supreme order can be attained, and he can become a fourth alongside the Three Kings. This is assuredly something that comes round immediately and produces instant results! May he who rules all under Heaven not balk at what is utmost in greatness, but strive first to plan for what is utmost in rectitude!

Memorial

A Simulated Memorial of Thanks for the Emperor Showing to the Grand Secretaries His Imperially Composed "Poem on Listening to the Classics Mat Officials Lecture on the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning" (Daxue yanyi 大學衍義), Which the Grand Secretaries Reverently Matched in Rhyme, and Ordering That They Be Compiled into a Volume Entitled Poems Assisting Learning (Yixue shi 翊學詩) [6th Year of Jiajing (1527)]

Li Zao 李藻

Associate Examiner and Instructor Fan comments: The narration of events is harmonious and smooth, and the phrasing is thorough and coherent. In depicting the imagery of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers, its loyalty and reverence are graciously manifest. Other compositions are not unskillful, but do they possess such vibrant spirit and grace?

Associate Examiner and Director of Studies Weng comments: The diction is like striking resonant stone, and the meaning is like a string of pearls. The quintessential brilliance of the Six Dynasties and the poised elegance of the Tang and Song are both captured in this memorial.

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭趙批莊重典則非馳騁浮靡者
考試官教諭林批敘述敷揚曲盡四六之妙
嘉靖六年某月某日具官臣某等伏蒙
聖恩以臣等恭和
御製聽
經筵官講大學衍義詩
命彙爲一冊名曰翊學詩臣等誠懽誠忭稽首
頓首謹奉
表稱
===
謝者
天啟
宸聰千古契簡編之要
雲回
睿藻
九重錫台輔之光虫吟慙和於
玉音貂續幸登於
寶冊
嘉名不朽
punctuated:
考試官教諭趙批：莊重典則，非馳騁浮靡者。
考試官教諭林批：敘述敷揚，曲盡四六之妙。

嘉靖六年某月某日，具官臣某等，伏蒙聖恩，以臣等恭和御製聽經筵官講《大學衍義》詩，命彙爲一冊，名曰《翊學詩》。臣等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首，謹奉表稱謝者。天啟宸聰，千古契簡編之要；雲回睿藻，九重錫台輔之光。虫吟慙和於玉音，貂續幸登於寶冊。嘉名不朽，
translation_en:
Examiner Instructor Zhao's comment: Solemn and classic in form; not one of those unrestrained,华麗 and superficial pieces.
Examiner Instructor Lin's comment: Its narration and exposition fully capture the subtleties of four-six parallel prose.

On a certain day of a certain month in the sixth year of the Jiajing era (1527), Your servants so-and-so, holding full official titles, have humbly received Imperial Grace: because Your servants respectfully matched the rhymes of the Imperially Composed Poem on Listening to the Classics Mat Officials Lecture on the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi), Your Majesty ordered that the poems be compiled into a single volume titled Poems Assisting Learning (Yixue shi). Your servants, truly joyful and elated, bow our heads to the ground and reverently present this memorial to express our gratitude.

Heaven opens the Imperial intelligence, grasping across a thousand ages the essence of the bamboo slips and scrolls; clouds swirl in the sagely literary compositions, as the Ninefold Palace bestows glory upon the chief ministers. With our insect-like chirping, we are ashamed to match Your jade tones; yet like dog-tails joined to sable, our verses have the fortune to be entered into the precious volume. This auspicious title shall never perish, …

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
休命曷揚竊以歌敕時幾本大舜謨聞之後銘
申敬義實太公書受之餘惟王者能自得
師非聖人莫之有作上能率下宣鹿野之
周行臣亦媚君答鳧涇以令德同聲唱和
協力進修自典學寖荒而摛詞亦戾過沛
興思猛士安事詩書橫汾致慕佳人空施
仁義投戈講業書徒細於札行開館延儒
製乃希於宮體即句聯殿閣僅撤炎蒸至
詩進牡丹祗賢博奕風斯下矣文在茲乎
===
恭惟
皇帝陛下
剛健粹精
神明宣哲河清雲見兆載應於大橫日就月
將志彌勤於小毖尊
親饗
帝本仁孝以綏猷稽古求聞識行言而畜德謂
魯聖闡皇王之祕揭三綱八目於遺書而
宋儒探經史之精備四要六條於衍義會
punctuated: 休命曷揚？竊以歌敕時幾，本大舜謨聞之後；銘申敬義，實太公書受之餘。惟王者能自得師，非聖人莫之有作。上能率下，宣鹿野之周行；臣亦媚君，答鳧涇以令德。同聲唱和，協力進修。自典學寖荒，而摛詞亦戾。過沛興思猛士，安事詩書；橫汾致慕佳人，空施仁義。投戈講業，書徒細於札行；開館延儒，製乃希於宮體。即句聯殿閣，僅撤炎蒸；至詩進牡丹，祗賢博奕。風斯下矣，文在茲乎？恭惟皇帝陛下，剛健粹精，神明宣哲。河清雲見，兆載應於大橫；日就月將，志彌勤於小毖。尊親饗帝，本仁孝以綏猷；稽古求聞，識行言而畜德。謂魯聖闡皇王之祕，揭三綱八目於遺書；而宋儒探經史之精，備四要六條於衍義。會
translation_en: …and how could Your beneficent mandate be sufficiently extolled? Your servant humbly reflects that the song admonishing mindfulness of time and subtleincipience originated after Great Shun heard the counsels; the inscriptions reiterating reverence and righteousness came indeed after the Grand Duke received the book. Only a true king is able to find a teacher for himself, and none but a sage could have composed such works. When the ruler can lead his subordinates, he proclaims the grand highway at the deer-plain; when ministers in turn show devotion to their lord, they respond at the duck-filled Jing River with virtuous conduct. With one voice they sing and harmonize, joining forces to advance in self-cultivation. Once devotion to learning gradually fell into neglect, literary composition likewise went astray. When passing through Pei aroused thoughts of fierce warriors, what use was made of the Odes and Documents? When crossing the Fen River evoked longing for a fair lady, benevolence and righteousness were applied in vain. Throwing down halberds to discourse on learning, writings were merely meticulous in tiny script on slips; opening halls to invite scholars, compositions emulated only the Palace Style. Even when linked verses were composed in palace pavilions, they served merely to dispel the summer heat; and when poems were presented on peonies, they were simply slightly better than board games. How low the customs had fallen! Does culture reside in such things? Your servant reverently reflects that Your Majesty the Emperor is firm, vigorous, pure, and refined, divinely luminous and manifestly wise. The Yellow River runs clear and auspicious clouds appear, as omens repeatedly correspond to the Great Horizontal divination sign; advancing daily and progressing monthly, Your resolve grows ever more diligent in the spirit of the "Little Caution" ode. Honoring Your parents and sacrificing to the Supreme Lord, You ground Your tranquil governance in benevolence and filial piety; examining antiquity and seeking learning, You remember bygone words and deeds to accumulate virtue. You consider that the Sage of Lu elucidated the secrets of sovereigns and kings, setting forth the Three Guiding Principles and Eight Steps in his transmitted book [the Great Learning]; and that the Song-dynasty Confucian probed the essence of the Classics and Histories, providing in full the Four Essentials and Six Articles in his Extended Meaning [of the Great Learning]. This work was once…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
書
高皇之廡壁屢進
列祖之經帷爰
納臣言用恢
天聽窮百代聖賢之奧恍若見諸羹牆探千古
得失之林粲如陳諸指掌心通耳順已融
吾道於青編
旨遠思深遂煥斯文於
紫極義追風雅道遡噩渾聊借體夫五言不取
===
朴於六代若帝中闈命申發危微如孔教
悟心退明忠恕戒堯言於時謹勒湯誨以
日新
光踰河洛之文
寵被絲綸之地固非游情翰墨
琬琰徒頒實亦
訪落臣鄰瓊瑤望報顧念臣等十五雖從於
大學三千莫得於宗傳誦經未達六情補
袞曾無一字何人筆老能賡慶曆之詩有賦言
punctuated: 書高皇之廡壁，屢進列祖之經帷；爰納臣言，用恢天聽。窮百代聖賢之奧，恍若見諸羹牆；探千古得失之林，粲如陳諸指掌。心通耳順，已融吾道於青編；旨遠思深，遂煥斯文於紫極。義追風雅，道遡噩渾，聊借體夫五言，不取朴於六代。若帝中闈命，申發危微；如孔教悟心，退明忠恕。戒堯言於時謹，勒湯誨以日新。光踰河洛之文，寵被絲綸之地。固非游情翰墨，琬琰徒頒；實亦訪落臣鄰，瓊瑤望報。顧念臣等十五雖從於大學，三千莫得於宗傳；誦經未達六情，補袞曾無一字。何人筆老，能賡慶曆之詩？有賦言
translation_en: …was inscribed upon the corridor walls of the Exalted Emperor (Gaozong/Taizu) and repeatedly presented at the classical lecture mats of the Successive Ancestors; thereupon You accepted Your servant's words, thereby broadening Your Heavenly hearing. Exhausting the profundities of the sages and worthies of a hundred generations, it is as if seeing them in one's soup and on one's walls; exploring the forest of successes and failures across a thousand ages, it is as bright as displaying them upon the palm of one's hand. With mind comprehending and ear receptive, You have already fused Our Way into the bamboo slips of history; with far-reaching purport and deep thought, You thus make this culture shine forth in the Purple Forbidden Enclosure. In principle pursuing the Airs and Odes (of the Classic of Poetry), and in the Way tracing back to the solemn and浑 (unadorned antiquity of the Book of Documents), You merely borrowed the form of five-syllable verse without adopting the artifice [?] of the Six Dynasties. It is like the Emperor (Shun) in the central court issuing his charge to expound upon the precariousness of the human mind and the subtlety of the moral mind; it is like Confucius's teaching awakening the mind, retiring (like Zengzi) to clarify loyalty and reciprocity. You take warning from Yao's words to be ever cautious, and engrave Tang's instructions so as to renew Yourself daily. Its brilliance surpasses the patterns of the Yellow River Chart and the Luo Script, and its favor extends over the place where imperial decrees are drafted (the Hanlin Academy and Grand Secretariat). Truly, this is not merely indulging sentiments in brush and ink, or bestowing jade tablets in vain; in reality, as You take counsel at the outset of Your reign with Your ministerial associates, You bestow precious jades in hope of a return. Yet, reflecting upon ourselves, although Your servants entered the Great Learning at fifteen, among the three thousand disciples we have failed to grasp the orthodox transmission; in reciting the Classics we have not mastered the six emotions, and in mending the imperial robes we have not contributed a single word. Whose brush is seasoned enough to match in rhyme the poems of the Qingli era? Though there be rhapsodies whose words…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
微尚約魏徵之禮庶暄日無忘於田叟豈
陽春可和於巴人天維顯思莫答保明之
望公何能爾翻承挺直之褒廼萃成書載
名翊學志交於泰信已如地如
天聲應於
乾安得從龍從虎且
聖功常習雖羽翼以何施惟
帝度益弘乃菲葑之罔弃遂令螢爝依光於
日月碔砆綴質於
===
球琳竝載
金函長傳
璧府緊黃扉之盛事為
丹扆之
殊恩敢不祗奉
王言懋襄
天德脩予作醴勉抒啓沃之忠示我佛肩少助
緝熙之學非誠意正心不獻遠法宋臣惟齊家
治
punctuated: 微，尚約魏徵之禮。庶暄日無忘於田叟，豈《陽春》可和於巴人？天維顯思，莫答保明之望；公何能爾，翻承挺直之褒。廼萃成書，載名《翊學》。志交於泰，信已如地如天；聲應於乾，安得從龍從虎？且聖功常習，雖羽翼以何施；惟帝度益弘，乃菲葑之罔弃。遂令螢爝依光於日月，碔砆綴質於球琳。竝載金函，長傳璧府。緊黃扉之盛事，為丹扆之殊恩。敢不祗奉王言，懋襄天德？脩予作醴，勉抒啓沃之忠；示我佛肩，少助緝熙之學。非誠意正心不獻，遠法宋臣；惟齊家治
translation_en: … subtle, yet held back by the etiquette accorded to Wei Zheng. Perchance the warm sun is not forgotten by the old peasant in the fields, yet how could the elevated melody "Vibrant Spring" be harmonized by a rustic of Ba? "Heaven's decree is clear indeed," yet we cannot live up to the expectation that we "preserve and enlighten" the throne; "how are you dukes capable of this," yet in turn we receive praise for uprightness and candor! Now these writings have been gathered into a book and given the title *Assisting in Learning* (Yixue). When aspirations commune in the hexagram Tai (Peace), truly it is already like Earth and like Heaven; when voices resonate in the hexagram Qian (The Creative), how could we attain to following the dragon and following the tiger? Moreover, Your Sagely merit is constantly practiced—even if we wished to act as wings of support, what could we contribute? Only because Your Imperial magnanimity grows ever broader are even humble turnips and radishes not cast aside. Thus You have allowed fireflies and torches to depend upon the brilliance of the Sun and Moon, and common stones to join their substance with fine jades. Together they are recorded in the Golden Casket and long transmitted in the Jade Repository. Truly this is a grand event for the Yellow Portal of the Secretariat, and an extraordinary grace from the Vermilion Screen of the throne! How dare we not reverently uphold the King's words and diligently assist Heaven's virtue? Using us to make sweet wine, we shall strive to pour forth our loyalty in enlightening and enriching Your mind; asking us to bear the burden on our shoulders, we shall slightly aid Your learning of continuous radiance. Presenting nothing other than making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind, we take as our distant model the ministers of the Song; hoping only for the regulation of the family and the ordering of…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
國是期上符文后伏願
始終遜志
夙夜殫心廣明德以新民允已
治三二典觀人文而成化不獨
言七六經股肱喜哉
元首起哉歌載賡於虞室泮奐游矣優游休矣
音永矢於周岡臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
===
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁場
策五道
第一問
饒位
同考試官訓導林批我
皇上講學勤政慶服千古子能揚厲其
punctuated:
國是期，上符文后。伏願始終遜志，夙夜殫心。廣明德以新民，允已治三二典；觀人文而成化，不獨言七六經。股肱喜哉，元首起哉，歌載賡於虞室；泮奐游矣，優游休矣，音永矢於周岡。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叁場
策五道
第一問
饒位
同考試官訓導林批：我皇上講學勤政，慶服千古。子能揚厲其
translation_en:
…the state is our aspiration, so as to match the cultured sovereigns above. We humbly pray that from beginning to end Your Majesty will maintain a humble mind, and from dawn to night exhaust Your heart; broaden Your illustrious virtue to renew the people, so that Your governance truly surpasses the Two Canons; observe human culture to transform the world, so that Your words not merely surpass the Six Classics. "The limbs rejoice! The head rises!"—may the song be sung once more as in the halls of Yu; "Relaxed and wandering! At leisure and at rest!"—may the melody be pledged forever on the ridges of Zhou. Your servant, overcome with the utmost emotion and trepidation in gazing up at Heaven and looking up to the Sage, respectfully presents this memorial of gratitude to inform the Throne.

Third Session
Five Policy Essays
First Question
Rao Wei
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Lin comments: Our August Emperor pursues learning and is diligent in governance, winning joyful submission through the ages. The candidate is able to extol its…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
盛而猶以晏見陳奏惓惓致望忠悃溢乎詞矣
同考試官教諭陳批朝講非二事政學無二理
有味哉其言之也末欲廣延眾論益懇
聖修是深知靖獻之義者
考試官教諭趙批美不忘規詞意懇至
考試官教諭林批敘述詳明忠讜見于言外
執事發策而首以
朝
講之制下詢承學承學蓬累而居不闚
===
扆黼之略丹鉛而誦豈堪
旃廈之議雖然亦射執事之策耳聖王之治
天下也雖秉靈體睿而不敢自謂神聖也
思天下之戴已者尊則思所以副其求而
襁褓之者甚備將副其求則思所以察其
瘼而規畫之者甚詳將詳其畫則不待其
事會而預設衡鑑以俟之者不得不審故
出以應夫棼籍入以正其幽眇日鰓鰓焉
而不遑暇豫誠思天命宜嚴而民嵒不可
punctuated:
盛，而猶以晏見、陳奏惓惓致望，忠悃溢乎詞矣。
同考試官教諭陳批：朝、講非二事，政、學無二理。有味哉，其言之也！末欲廣延眾論、益懇聖修，是深知靖獻之義者。
考試官教諭趙批：美不忘規，詞意懇至。
考試官教諭林批：敘述詳明，忠讜見于言外。
執事發策，而首以朝講之制下詢承學。承學蓬累而居，不闚扆黼之略；丹鉛而誦，豈堪旃廈之議？雖然，亦射執事之策耳。聖王之治天下也，雖秉靈體睿，而不敢自謂神聖也。思天下之戴已者尊，則思所以副其求而襁褓之者甚備；將副其求，則思所以察其瘼而規畫之者甚詳；將詳其畫，則不待其事會而預設衡鑑以俟之者不得不審。故出以應夫棼籍，入以正其幽眇，日鰓鰓焉而不遑暇豫，誠思天命宜嚴，而民嵒不可…
translation_en:
…splendor, while still earnestly expressing hopes regarding informal audiences and the presentation of memorials; loyal sincerity overflows from the words.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Chen comments: Court audiences and classic-mat lectures are not two separate matters; governance and learning do not have two separate principles. How meaningful are his words! At the end, he wishes to broadly invite public discussion and ever more earnestly urges Imperial self-cultivation; he is one who deeply understands the meaning of quiet devotion and presenting counsel to the sovereign.
Examiner and Instructor Zhao comments: While praising, he does not forget to offer admonition; the words and intent are earnest and thorough.
Examiner and Instructor Lin comments: The exposition is detailed and clear, and loyal, forthright counsel is visible beyond the words themselves.
Your Excellency has posed the policy question, inquiring first of this junior scholar concerning the institutions of court audiences and classic-mat lectures. Living in humble obscurity, this junior scholar has not glimpsed the grand strategies behind the imperial screen and axe-embroidered hangings; reciting texts with vermilion and lead, how could I be worthy of deliberations beneath the felt-lined imperial halls? Even so, I shall venture a reply to Your Excellency's policy question. When the sage kings governed All under Heaven, though they were endowed with spiritual intelligence and embodied wisdom, they did not dare call themselves divinely sage. Reflecting on how exalted was the veneration in which All under Heaven held them, they thought about how to fulfill the people's needs and nurture them as if in swaddling clothes with utmost completeness. Wishing to fulfill their needs, they thought about how to examine their distress and plan for them in utmost detail. Wishing to make their plans detailed, they could not but be thorough in establishing scales and mirrors in advance to await the convergence of affairs before they even arose. Therefore, going out to respond to the tangled multitude of affairs and retiring within to rectify the subtle and abstruse recesses of the mind, day after day they were anxiously diligent without leisure for ease and comfort, truly reflecting that the Mandate of Heaven must be held in awe and the rugged perils of the people's sentiments cannot…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
不畏也蓋自有君臣以來則有會朝之制
而後世之可詳者在周官矣師氏之誥曰
王日視朝於路寢門外天以日運故健日
月以日行故明一日二日萬幾故昧爽丕
顯坐以待旦蟲飛而會盈日出而視朝朝
退而聽於路寢日中而考政日夕而糾虔
天刑日入而潔奉粢盛當是時芻蕘之所
陳如臨師保邇言之所察若籍故府自常
伯常任至於虎賁綴衣趣馬小尹左右攜
===
僕百司庶府必皆吉士自公卿至於列士
師瞍矇工庶人親戚瞽史耆艾皆有賦誦
故有朝之名而未始無講之實也自秦迨
漢而制寖異焉叔孫通起朝儀務尊君卑
臣趨於簡闊至於宣帝五日一聽事而公
卿之進見益疎唐宋而後大氐皆因漢制
故願治之主無以廣嘉聞延讜論於是有
若光武數引公卿郎將講論經理夜分乃
寐矣有若唐太宗命學士杜如晦等十八
punctuated: 不畏也。蓋自有君臣以來，則有會朝之制，而後世之可詳者，在《周官》矣。師氏之誥曰：「王日視朝於路寢門外。」天以日運故健，日月以日行故明。一日二日萬幾，故昧爽丕顯，坐以待旦；蟲飛而會盈，日出而視朝，朝退而聽於路寢，日中而考政，日夕而糾虔天刑，日入而潔奉粢盛。當是時，芻蕘之所陳，如臨師保；邇言之所察，若籍故府。自常伯、常任至於虎賁、綴衣、趣馬、小尹、左右攜僕、百司庶府，必皆吉士；自公卿至於列士、師、瞍、矇、工、庶人、親戚、瞽、史、耆、艾，皆有賦誦。故有朝之名，而未始無講之實也。自秦迨漢，而制寖異焉。叔孫通起朝儀，務尊君卑臣，趨於簡闊。至於宣帝，五日一聽事，而公卿之進見益疎。唐、宋而後，大氐皆因漢制，故願治之主，無以廣嘉聞、延讜論。於是有若光武，數引公卿郎將講論經理，夜分乃寐矣；有若唐太宗，命學士杜如晦等十八
translation_en: …not be feared. Indeed, ever since there have been rulers and ministers, there has been the institution of court audiences, and what later ages can examine in detail is found in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan). The admonition of the Master Tutor (Shishi) says: "The King holds daily court outside the gate of the State Chamber." Heaven is vigorous because it revolves daily; the sun and moon are bright because they travel daily. In one day or two days there are ten thousand myriad affairs; therefore, in the dim light of dawn he was grandly illustrious, sitting and waiting for daybreak. When the insects flew, the assembly filled the court; when the sun rose, he held court; when the court retired, he heard governance in the State Chamber; at midday, he examined administration; in the evening, he reverently attended to the heavenly punishments; at sunset, he purely offered the sacrificial grains. At that time, what grass-cutters and firewood-gatherers presented was received as if facing Grand Tutors and Grand Protectors; the examination of simple words was as if consulting the old archives. From the Permanent Seniors (Changbo) and Permanent Functionaries (Changren) down to the fierce warriors (Huben), keepers of the robes (Zhuiyi), masters of the royal stables (Quma), minor directors (Xiaoyin), personal attendants, and the hundred offices and myriad treasuries—all had to be virtuous gentlemen. From the dukes and ministers down to the ranked servicemen, music masters, blind musicians, artisans, commoners, relatives, blind chroniclers, scribes, and elders—all offered their recitations and admonitions. Thus, there was the name of holding court, and never without the reality of lecturing and discussion. From the Qin down to the Han, the system gradually changed. Shusun Tong 叔孫通 established the court ceremonial, striving to exalt the ruler and humble the ministers, tending toward brevity and distance. By the time of Emperor Xuan 宣帝, he heard affairs of state once every five days, and the audiences of dukes and ministers became increasingly infrequent. From the Tang and Song onward, they generally followed the Han system. Consequently, rulers who wished for good governance had no means to broaden their exposure to fine counsel or invite forthright discussions. Thereupon, there were rulers like Emperor Guangwu 光武, who frequently summoned dukes, ministers, and Gentlemen-Household Generals to lecture and discuss the principles of the Classics, going to sleep only at midnight; and there were rulers like Emperor Taizong of Tang 唐太宗, who commanded the Scholars Du Ruhui 杜如晦 and others, eighteen…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
人更直閤下討論經義矣至宋而後制益
加詳便殿經筵祕閣直廬晝侍講讀夜備
召對於是乎講制立焉然或免隻日或輟
寒暑故議者以爲徒循故事爲美談已耳
我
高皇帝之初下婺州也則禮其碩儒而講
帷幄中其後雖干戈倥偬而
手編不去
定鼎之後尤孜孜矣
===
慮俯仰而再周四海之外中夜思四方之事待
旦而行之
朝與
講皆如此其數數然也此所謂
帝王有用之學而經天下萬世無窮之心乎及
夫定爲儀注肇自正統初載
累朝以來循蹈無易我
皇上
聖資
punctuated: 人，更直閤下，討論經義矣。至宋而後，制益加詳，便殿經筵，祕閣直廬，晝侍講讀，夜備召對，於是乎講制立焉。然或免隻日，或輟寒暑，故議者以爲徒循故事，爲美談已耳。我高皇帝之初下婺州也，則禮其碩儒，而講帷幄中。其後雖干戈倥偬，而手編不去。定鼎之後，尤孜孜矣，慮俯仰而再周四海之外，中夜思四方之事，待旦而行之，朝與講皆如此其數數然也。此所謂帝王有用之學，而經天下萬世無窮之心乎！及夫定爲儀注，肇自正統初載，累朝以來，循蹈無易。我皇上聖資
translation_en:
… men to take turns on duty below the pavilion, discussing the meanings of the Classics. From the Song dynasty onward, the system became increasingly detailed: with Classics Colloquia in the side halls and duty quarters in the Imperial Archives, officials attended lectures and readings by day and stood ready for imperial summonses and responses by night; thereupon the system of imperial lectures was firmly established. Yet at times sessions were excused on odd-numbered days, or suspended during the winter cold and summer heat; thus critics considered it merely following routine precedent to make for a fine-sounding tale, and nothing more.

When our Exalted Emperor [Taizu] first conquered Wuzhou, he treated its eminent Confucian scholars with ritual courtesy and held lectures within his military tent. Thereafter, even amid the pressing urgency of warfare, he never let go of the volumes in his hand. After establishing the dynastic capital, he was even more diligent: his thoughts ranged above and below, twice encompassing all beyond the Four Seas; in the middle of the night he pondered the affairs of the four quarters, waiting for dawn to put them into action. Both his court audiences and his classical lectures were conducted with such frequent diligence as this. Is this not what is called the practical learning of emperors and kings, and the inexhaustible mind that orders the realm for ten thousand generations?

When it came to fixing these practices as formal ritual protocols, it began in the early years of the Zhengtong reign (1436–1449), and through successive reigns since then, they have been followed without change. Our Majesty, with his sage endowment …

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
天授
聖學日成其於率由古訓自然非强
臨御以來七載不𠖥蓋
朝之日一而
講之日二故
明主有日新之德而四海仰
臨照之神鏡治本矣昔者殷宗三祀其惟弗言
曰以台正於四方台恐德弗類旣得傅說
則曰爾交脩予罔予弃予惟克邁乃訓成
===
王即位始謀於廟其言憂思深遠若隕淵
谷而羣臣進戒獨以學問爲先故詩曰念
茲皇祖陟降庭止又曰維予小子不聰敬
止學有緝熙於光明佛時仔肩示我顯德
行夫不憂承式而憂其無多聞不憂多難
而憂其無繼序聖人之意遠矣
皇上之意即商宗周王之意也今
神睿益充
國家政體益習
punctuated: 天授，聖學日成，其於率由古訓，自然非强。臨御以來，七載不𠖥，蓋朝之日一而講之日二，故明主有日新之德，而四海仰臨照之神，鏡治本矣。昔者殷宗三祀，其惟弗言，曰：「以台正於四方，台恐德弗類。」旣得傅說，則曰：「爾交脩予，罔予弃，予惟克邁乃訓。」成王即位，始謀於廟，其言憂思深遠，若隕淵谷，而羣臣進戒，獨以學問爲先。故《詩》曰：「念茲皇祖，陟降庭止。」又曰：「維予小子，不聰敬止。學有緝熙於光明，佛時仔肩，示我顯德行。」夫不憂承式而憂其無多聞，不憂多難而憂其無繼序，聖人之意遠矣。皇上之意，即商宗、周王之意也。今神睿益充，國家政體益習，
translation_en:
… are bestowed by Heaven, and His sagely learning matures by the day; in following the ancient precepts, He does so naturally and without forcing Himself. For the seven years since He ascended the throne, He has been untiring: on one day He holds court, and on two days He attends the classical colloquium. Thus our enlightened ruler possesses daily-renewed virtue, while all within the Four Seas look up to the divine brilliance that shines down upon them—He has mirrored the very root of governance!

In antiquity, for three years King Gaozong of Yin did not speak; then he said, "Since it falls to me to bring order to the four quarters, I fear my virtue is not equal to Those before me." Once he had found Fu Yue, he said, "Do you constantly remonstrate with me to cultivate my virtue; do not abandon me, and I shall be able to tread the path of your instructions." When King Cheng of Zhou ascended the throne and first took counsel in the ancestral temple, his words were filled with deep and far-reaching anxiety, as though he were falling into a deep abyss; yet when his ministers offered admonitions, they placed learning and inquiry alone at the forefront. Thus the Book of Odes says: "Ever mindful of this August Ancestor, who ascends and descends in the court." And again it says: "I, the little child, am not perceptive in my reverence. By daily and unceasing study may I reach luminous clarity; assist me in bearing this heavy burden, and show me the way of manifest virtuous conduct." Truly, not to worry about upholding the established model, but to worry about lacking broad learning; not to worry about the multitude of difficulties, but to worry about failing to continue the royal succession—how far-reaching was the intention of the sages! The intention of His Majesty the Emperor is none other than the intention of Gaozong of Shang and King Cheng of Zhou. Now that His divine wisdom grows ever fuller and He becomes ever more conversant with the administrative ways of the state, …

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
特從輔臣之請輟揮翰之暇披省章奏與二三
執政切劘講肄煌煌乎無疆之
盛德大業其在兹矣迺執事復舉宋臣之議爲
問意欲
聖人之學純亦不已而願
皇上軼三五之上乎敢不補綴所聞效芹曝焉
夫詢事質疑非論不彰問駁相發情態溢
出竊聞
日講之際
===
德音無所辯難遂使執經者不得盡其說陳事
者無所見其裏則何以入理閫而廣意域
故韓維欲從容降接以盡臣下之情往復
研究以見聖人之奧似爲
今日言也一簣虧成十寒戕生日就月將始
於時習今近臣入直有時見不得亟
皇上退而與處者誰歟得無藏脩之時少而游
息之日多歟程顥有言涉書史覽古今乃
學之一端耳涵養氣質薰陶德性斯習與
punctuated: 特從輔臣之請，輟揮翰之暇，披省章奏，與二三執政切劘講肄，煌煌乎無疆之盛德大業，其在兹矣！迺執事復舉宋臣之議爲問，意欲聖人之學純亦不已，而願皇上軼三五之上乎？敢不補綴所聞，效芹曝焉。夫詢事質疑，非論不彰，問駁相發，情態溢出。竊聞日講之際，德音無所辯難，遂使執經者不得盡其說，陳事者無所見其裏，則何以入理閫而廣意域？故韓維欲從容降接以盡臣下之情，往復研究以見聖人之奧，似爲今日言也。一簣虧成，十寒戕生，日就月將，始於時習。今近臣入直有時，見不得亟，皇上退而與處者誰歟？得無藏脩之時少而游息之日多歟？程顥有言：「涉書史、覽古今，乃學之一端耳。涵養氣質，薰陶德性，斯習與
translation_en:
…he has specially heeded the request of the Grand Secretaries, setting aside his leisure for wielding the brush in order to peruse and examine memorials, mutually polishing and studying with two or three chief ministers—how resplendent! Boundless great virtue and grand enterprise lie right here! Yet Your Excellency again raises the discussions of the Song ministers as a question. Is it your desire that the sage's learning be pure and unceasing, wishing His Majesty to surpass the Three Emperors and Five Sovereigns? How could I dare not piece together what I have heard, offering it like a humble gift of wild celery or warm sun?

Now, in inquiring into affairs and resolving doubts, without discussion they are not made clear; when questions and refutations stimulate one another, the true conditions and nuances come pouring forth. I have heard in private that during the Daily Lectures, the Imperial voice engages in no debate or questioning. Consequently, those who hold the Classics cannot fully expound their explanations, and those who present affairs have no way to reveal their inner substance—how then can one enter the threshold of principle and broaden the realm of thought? Therefore, when Han Wei 韓維 wished for the ruler to receive his ministers with unhurried ease so as to fully draw out his subordinates' views, and to investigate back and forth so as to perceive the profound subtleties of the sages, it seems as if he were speaking for today.

Stopping one basketful short ruins the whole mound, and ten days of cold destroy what one day of warmth has grown; daily progress and monthly advance begin with constant practice. Nowadays, the close ministers enter for duty only at set times and cannot be seen frequently; when His Majesty retires, with whom does he dwell? Could it be that the times for secluded study are few, while the days of leisure and rest are many? Cheng Hao 程顥 once said: "Perusing books and histories and surveying past and present are merely one aspect of learning. Cultivating one's temperament and steeping and molding one's moral nature—whereby habit and…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
知長而化與心成亦
今之讜論也趙抃曰易有吉凶詩有美刺禮
有汙隆樂有治亂春秋有善惡史有得失
並舉則易見偏陳則難明迺經筵講吉不
講凶讀得不讀失言筌尚滯意匠將屈此
豈所謂臨文不諱耶愚恐
今之不無是也李淑曰自昔人主講讀本欲
因事立訓鑒往知今假借是名與近臣譚
議政事耳司馬光呂公著蘇軾諸臣風流
===
相形美政美事多自講筵發之如其佔畢
而已所益幾何此又愚之所望於
今者也猶有一焉曰
御應門
聰明四達
皇上之采聽弘矣而敷奏之禮尚略獻納之績
罔效非有司之過乎宋制臣僚朝辭日具
轉對景祐之詔後殿說書之日權引諸司
對事
punctuated: 知長而化與心成。」亦今之讜論也。趙抃曰：「《易》有吉凶，《詩》有美刺，《禮》有汙隆，《樂》有治亂，《春秋》有善惡，《史》有得失。並舉則易見，偏陳則難明。」迺經筵講吉不講凶，讀得不讀失，言筌尚滯，意匠將屈，此豈所謂臨文不諱耶？愚恐今之不無是也。李淑曰：「自昔人主講讀，本欲因事立訓，鑒往知今，假借是名，與近臣譚議政事耳。」司馬光、呂公著、蘇軾諸臣風流相形，美政美事，多自講筵發之。如其佔畢而已，所益幾何？此又愚之所望於今者也。猶有一焉，曰御應門。聰明四達，皇上之采聽弘矣，而敷奏之禮尚略，獻納之績罔效，非有司之過乎？宋制：臣僚朝辭日，具轉對；景祐之詔，後殿說書之日，權引諸司對事。
translation_en: … wisdom grows and transformation is completed within the mind." This, too, is a forthright counsel for today. Zhao Bian 趙抃 said: "The Book of Changes (Yi) has auspiciousness and misfortune; the Book of Odes (Shi) has praise and satire; the Book of Rites (Li) has decline and flourishing; the Book of Music (Yue) has order and chaos; the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) has good and evil; and the Histories (Shi) have successes and failures. When presented together, they are easy to perceive; when set forth one-sidedly, they are hard to understand." Yet at the Classics Colloquium (jingyan), they expound on the auspicious and not the unfortunate, and read of successes and not of failures. When the verbal trappings remain bogged down, the deeper meaning will be cramped—how could this be what is meant by not shunning taboo topics when confronting a text? I fear that today we are not entirely free of this. Li Shu 李淑 said: "From of old, when a ruler engaged in lecturing and reading, he originally intended to establish lessons based on events and to understand the present by mirroring the past, borrowing this name merely to discuss affairs of state with his close ministers." Ministers such as Sima Guang 司馬光, Lü Gongzhu 呂公著, and Su Shi 蘇軾 inspired one another with their noble bearing, and fine policies and admirable deeds were mostly initiated from the lecture mat. If it is nothing more than droning over texts, how much benefit can there be? This, again, is what I hope for today. There is still one more matter: namely, the Emperor's personal attendance at the Ying Gate (Yingmen). With his intelligence and insight reaching in all four directions, His Majesty's gathering and heeding of counsel is vast indeed; yet the ritual of presenting memorials in person remains abbreviated, and achievements in offering advice yield no results—is this not the fault of the authorities? Under the Song system, on the day officials took leave of the court, they prepared rotational audiences (zhuandui); and by the edict of the Jingyou reign (1034–1038), on days when lectures on books were held in the rear palace, the heads of various bureaus were provisionally led in to report on affairs. …

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
今制獨輔臣對
便殿自餘雖六卿公孤莫望
清光焉意者非典歟無論洪永之時卽蹇夏而
下代有宴見如蒙曠然發
明詔令部寺卿貳隨輔弼侍從之臣不時
召對
躬聽覽則庶務之情實具見數
考問則百官之忠僞周知上以廣
聖睿聰明之用下以責翼爲明聽之實此章化
===
軌物之大者也夫聖人所以動天地應神
明正萬物而成王治者必本乎眞實而已
故在上者審則儀道以建皇極非以飾羽
儀聳觀聽盛一代之典而已也銓經徵聖
以務脩身非以馳辨洽縟辭說人文化成
天下而已也酌史論世以資反躬非以託
褒貶考興廢虛評陳人之已事而已也議
政制事以謀治安非以脩節文糾度數搜
選庭間之馳驟而已也古之興王惟恐天
punctuated:
今制：獨輔臣對便殿，自餘雖六卿、公孤，莫望清光焉。意者非典歟？無論洪、永之時，卽蹇、夏而下，代有宴見。如蒙曠然發明詔，令部寺卿貳隨輔弼、侍從之臣不時召對。躬聽覽，則庶務之情實具見；數考問，則百官之忠僞周知。上以廣聖睿聰明之用，下以責翼爲明聽之實，此章化軌物之大者也。
夫聖人所以動天地、應神明、正萬物而成王治者，必本乎眞實而已。故在上者審則儀道以建皇極，非以飾羽儀、聳觀聽、盛一代之典而已也；銓經徵聖以務脩身，非以馳辨洽、縟辭說、人文化成天下而已也；酌史論世以資反躬，非以託褒貶、考興廢、虛評陳人之已事而已也；議政制事以謀治安，非以脩節文、糾度數、搜選庭間之馳驟而已也。古之興王，惟恐天
translation_en:
Under the present system, only the Grand Secretaries have audiences in the side halls; as for the rest, even the Six Ministers, the Three Dukes, and the Three Solitaries cannot hope to gaze upon the Emperor's radiant presence. Could it be that this is not the proper norm? Not to speak of the Hongwu and Yongle eras, even from the time of Jian Yi 蹇義 and Xia Yuanji 夏原吉 onward, in every reign there were informal audiences. If we might be favored with the broad issuance of a luminous edict ordering the Ministers, Chief Ministers, and Vice Ministers of the Ministries and Courts to accompany the Grand Secretaries and the officials in attendance to be summoned for audiences from time to time: through the Emperor's personal hearing and review, the actual circumstances of all affairs of state will be fully seen; through frequent questioning and examination, the loyalty or deceit of the hundred officials will be thoroughly known. Above, this will broaden the exercise of His Majesty's sage wisdom and keen perception; below, it will exact the reality of assisting in governance and lending clear hearing [as in the Book of Documents]. This is a great matter for manifesting moral transformation and setting the standard for all things.

Now, that whereby the sage moves heaven and earth, responds to the spirits, rectifies the myriad things, and brings kingly governance to completion must simply be rooted in genuine substance. Therefore, when the ruler above examines the model and patterns himself on the Way in order to establish the August Ultimate, it is not merely to adorn the ceremonial plumage, dazzle the eyes and ears of onlookers, and make grand the institutions of an age. When he weighs the Classics and verifies the teachings of the sages in order to devote himself to self-cultivation, it is not merely to display eloquent erudition, elaborate his discourse, and culturally transform the world. When he consults history and discusses past ages in order to aid self-reflection, it is not merely to entrust himself to praise and blame, investigate rise and fall, and idly criticize the bygone affairs of men of old. When he deliberates on governance and regulates affairs in order to plan for peace and order, it is not merely to refine ritual forms, correct numerical standards, and select for the court's brisk routines. The founding kings of antiquity only feared lest the world…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
下之不明已也故其學問猶之殖焉既培
蕋之又日溉焉而其於治猶農之有畔日
夜思之朝夕而行之行無越思此善經也
願
皇上脩德於淵蜎蠖濩之中而不待於
大廷
懋學於夢寐幽獨之際而不必於典訓
深慮於千百萬億之後而不止於眉睫
綜實於言語筆札之外而不因於緣飾務設誠
===
於內而致行之則
帝何以不三五而俗何以不唐虞哉愚生自忘
其迂輒誦所聞惟執事虞其然否
第二問
王守勝
同考試官訓導史批文章遞變諸士類能言之
惟印證古今推及世運此作獨得其要領亟收之以風靡麗者
同考試官訓導張批文體關乎士習代有盛衰
子能貫穿百家獨宗大雅而歸本于務學其得文家之三昧者耶
punctuated:
下之不明已也。故其學問猶之殖焉，既培蕋之，又日溉焉；而其於治，猶農之有畔，日夜思之，朝夕而行之，行無越思，此善經也。願皇上脩德於淵蜎蠖濩之中，而不待於大廷；懋學於夢寐幽獨之際，而不必於典訓；深慮於千百萬億之後，而不止於眉睫；綜實於言語筆札之外，而不因於緣飾。務設誠於內而致行之，則帝何以不三、五，而俗何以不唐、虞哉？愚生自忘其迂，輒誦所聞，惟執事虞其然否。

第二問
王守勝
同考試官訓導史批：文章遞變，諸士類能言之。惟印證古今，推及世運，此作獨得其要領，亟收之以風靡麗者。
同考試官訓導張批：文體關乎士習，代有盛衰。子能貫穿百家，獨宗大雅，而歸本于務學，其得文家之三昧者耶！
translation_en:
… [only feared that the world] would not be enlightened. Therefore, their learning was like cultivating plants: having banked up the roots, they also watered them daily. And their approach to governance was like a farmer having field boundaries: thinking on it day and night, putting it into practice morning and evening, with actions never straying beyond their thoughts—this is the good standard. I pray that His Majesty will cultivate his virtue in profound and quiet retirement [?], without waiting for the grand court; strive in learning during dreams and solitary moments, without relying solely on canonical injunctions; take deep thought for hundreds of millions of generations to come, without stopping at what is right before the eyes; and grasp reality beyond spoken words and written notes, without depending on superficial ornament. If he strives to establish sincerity within and carry it out in practice, then why should the Sovereign not equal the Three Emperors and Five Monarchs, and why should customs not match those of Yao (Tang) and Shun (Yu)? I, a foolish student, forgetting my own pedantry, have ventured to recite what I have heard; may Your Excellency judge whether it is so or not.

Second Policy Question
Wang Shousheng 王守勝
Comment by Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Shi 史: The successive changes in literary writing are something all the candidates are generally able to discuss. Only in verifying them against antiquity and the present and extending the inquiry to the fortunes of the age does this essay alone grasp the essential point. I urgently select it to serve as a corrective example to those who indulge in florid extravagance.
Comment by Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Zhang 張: Literary style is bound up with the habits of the literati, flourishing and declining from age to age. You are able to thread together the Hundred Schools, singly honoring great elegance while tracing the root back to devotion to learning—have you not attained the true samadhi (essential secret) of the master writers!

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭趙批〔氣格渾雄足爲詞壇赤幟〕
考試官教諭林批〔千古藝林品隲精當〕
嘗謂天下之事有可言而不可知者有可
知而不可言者氣之有淳澆也而文因以
高下此講藝之士所詳也然而轉移變化
之迹若有朕焉而不得其故此可言而不
可知者也文之有盛衰也而治因以隆汙
此識微之士所憂也然直析而僂陳之則
見以為汗漫而無當於實此可知而不可
===
言者也執事有槩於中而以文策士令揚
搉古今文章之變誠意不為文也愚生烏
足以知之然嘗讀易之渙矣渙之象曰風
行水上渙天下之至文夫風與水相遭而
天地之文以著人與世相閱而古今之變
以成故風不能不以地推移而文不能不
與時高下彼風之行於濫觴之淵也泓渟
泱攮有龍鱗而霧縠者焉風之文也及其
行於盤渦大峽而湍悍蕩颶起濤飛沫電
punctuated:
考試官教諭趙批：〔氣格渾雄，足爲詞壇赤幟。〕
考試官教諭林批：〔千古藝林，品隲精當。〕
嘗謂天下之事，有可言而不可知者，有可知而不可言者。氣之有淳澆也，而文因以高下，此講藝之士所詳也；然而轉移變化之迹，若有朕焉而不得其故，此可言而不可知者也。文之有盛衰也，而治因以隆汙，此識微之士所憂也；然直析而僂陳之，則見以為汗漫而無當於實，此可知而不可言者也。執事有槩於中，而以文策士，令揚搉古今文章之變，誠意不為文也。愚生烏足以知之？然嘗讀《易》之《渙》矣。《渙》之《象》曰：「風行水上，渙。」天下之至文，夫風與水相遭，而天地之文以著；人與世相閱，而古今之變以成。故風不能不以地推移，而文不能不與時高下。彼風之行於濫觴之淵也，泓渟泱攮，有龍鱗而霧縠者焉，風之文也；及其行於盤渦大峽，而湍悍蕩颶，起濤飛沫，電…
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: 〔Its spirit and style are vigorous and grand, worthy of standing as a red banner in the literary arena.〕
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: 〔Across the literary forest of all ages, its evaluations are precise and fitting.〕
It has been said that among the affairs of the world, there are things that can be spoken of yet cannot be truly fathomed, and things that can be fathomed yet cannot be readily spoken of. That the ethos of an age may be pure or thin, and that literature accordingly rises or falls in quality, is something that scholars who discuss the arts examine in detail; yet while the traces of its shifts and transformations seem to show subtle signs, one cannot grasp their underlying cause—this is what can be spoken of yet cannot be fathomed. That literature has its periods of flourishing and decline, and that governance accordingly prospers or decays, is something that scholars who perceive subtleties worry over; yet if one analyzes it bluntly and enumerates it point by point, it is regarded as diffuse and detached from reality—this is what can be fathomed yet cannot be spoken of. Your Honor, feeling a deep concern within, has posed a policy question to the candidates on the subject of literature, bidding us to assess and discuss the transformations of writing from antiquity to the present; truly your intention goes beyond mere literary composition. How could a foolish student like myself be capable of understanding this? Nevertheless, I have read the "Dispersion" (Huan) hexagram in the Classic of Changes (Yi). The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) for "Dispersion" states: "Wind blowing over water: Dispersion." As for the supreme patterns (wen) of the world, when wind and water encounter one another, the patterns of Heaven and Earth are made manifest; when human beings and their epochs pass through one another, the transformations of ancient and modern times are brought into being. Therefore, just as the wind cannot but shift according to the terrain, literature cannot but rise and fall with the times. When the wind moves over a deep pool where a stream first rises from a brimming goblet, the waters are deep, still, and softlyrippling, forming patterns like dragon scales and misty crepe—this is the pattern of the wind. When it moves through whirling eddies and great gorges, rushing fiercely and tossing in gales, raising great waves, flinging spray, and like lightning…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
激輪轉者亦風之文也及其行於洞庭彭
蠡之澤而汪洋浩渺浮天無岸連山歆雪
不可嚮遏者亦風之文也文之與時高下
亦若是而已矣是故五帝之事若有若無
三王之事若存若亡論者猶謂黃唐淳而
質虞夏質而變商周麗而雅又或稱虞夏
之書渾渾商書灝灝周書噩噩蓋取諸六
籍而萬世文藝之淵源肇焉春秋戰國之
文繼六籍而作而其理不及也然而攻竒
===
飾說本原百物極窈窕閎肆之談使後世
工文者雖出入萬變而未可得易斯已竒
矣兩漢之文竊春秋戰國之意用之而又
不及也然而椎雕為朴反華為質善叙事
理能得人情言之精者可以不朽斯已偉
矣晉宋六朝竊漢之詞用之而又不及也
然而善鎔鑄古人之言以耀光鬱采霞駁
雲譎如登赤城之嶠炫目動心麗而不淫
者矣唐人竊六朝之體用之而又不及也
punctuated: 激輪轉者，亦風之文也；及其行於洞庭、彭蠡之澤，而汪洋浩渺，浮天無岸，連山歆雪，不可嚮遏者，亦風之文也。文之與時高下，亦若是而已矣。是故五帝之事若有若無，三王之事若存若亡，論者猶謂黃、唐淳而質，虞、夏質而變，商、周麗而雅；又或稱《虞》、《夏》之書渾渾，《商書》灝灝，《周書》噩噩，蓋取諸六籍，而萬世文藝之淵源肇焉。春秋、戰國之文，繼六籍而作，而其理不及也；然而攻竒飾說，本原百物，極窈窕閎肆之談，使後世工文者雖出入萬變而未可得易，斯已竒矣。兩漢之文，竊春秋、戰國之意用之，而又不及也；然而椎雕為朴，反華為質，善叙事理，能得人情，言之精者可以不朽，斯已偉矣。晉、宋、六朝，竊漢之詞用之，而又不及也；然而善鎔鑄古人之言，以耀光鬱采，霞駁雲譎，如登赤城之嶠，炫目動心，麗而不淫者矣。唐人竊六朝之體用之，而又不及也；
translation_en: …darting like lightning and whirling like wheels—this too is the patterning of the wind. And when it moves across the marshes of Dongting and Pengli, vast and boundless, floating to the heavens without a shore, piling up mountains of billowed snow [?] that cannot be faced or checked—this too is the patterning of the wind. The rise and fall of literature with the times is simply like this and nothing more. Therefore, although the affairs of the Five Emperors seem at once to have existed and not existed, and the affairs of the Three Kings seem at once preserved and lost, commentators still say that the eras of the Yellow Emperor and Yao (Tang) were pure and unadorned, those of Shun (Yu) and Xia were unadorned yet evolving, and those of Shang and Zhou were florid yet refined; or again they state that the Documents of Yu and Xia are profound and vast (hunhun), the Documents of Shang are grand and boundless (haohao), and the Documents of Zhou are solemn and rigorous (e'e). Indeed, drawing from the Six Classics, the fountainhead of literary art for ten thousand generations had its beginning therein. The literature of the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods arose in succession to the Six Classics, yet its moral principle did not equal theirs. Nevertheless, in cultivating the extraordinary and adorning their arguments, tracing the origins of all things, and carrying subtle, expansive, and unbridled discourse to the utmost—so that even as masters of writing in later ages entered and departed through ten thousand variations, they could never alter or surpass them—this was already extraordinary. The literature of the Western and Eastern Han borrowed the ideas of the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods and employed them, yet again did not equal them. Nevertheless, in hammering carved ornament back into simplicity and returning华 (floridity) to substance, excelling at narrating affairs and principles, and succeeding in capturing human feelings, so that the finest of their words could achieve immortality—this was already magnificent. The Jin, Liu Song, and Six Dynasties borrowed the diction of the Han and employed it, yet again did not equal it. Nevertheless, they excelled at smelting and casting the words of the ancients to shine with brilliance and lush colors, dappled like rosy clouds and wondrously shifting like mist, so that it is like ascending the peaks of Chicheng: dazzling the eyes and stirring the heart, resplendent without being licentious. The men of the Tang borrowed the style of the Six Dynasties and employed it, yet again did not equal it; …

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
然而沈浸釀郁貫穿百家其詞平易爾雅
不為琦辯雖風骨靡而不振其韞富矣自
韓愈氏至於宋變唐人之體而去其辭而
又不及也然而探賾鉤深咀載道要刋落
華藻而歸之本根雖時有蕪陋然其淵源
正矣劉禹錫曰三代之文至戰國而病涉
秦漢復起漢之文至列國而病唐興復起
如是則盛衰有時勢極必返矣孰振之哉
而朱子謂韓文不如漢漢文不如先秦戰
===
國則直以古今風氣日趨於澆薄已耳孰
靡之哉此可言而不可知者也意者文之
有高下以氣之淳澆耶氣之有淳澆以運
之升降耶合之則古今之升降為一代而
分之則一代之升降為古今故觀之風與
水之推移而二子之說可互見也雖然渙
之文至矣然而聖人曰渙者離也物不可
以終離故授之以節又何以說也
國家文化宣朗與帝典王風比隆較烈自弘
punctuated: 然而沈浸釀郁，貫穿百家，其詞平易爾雅，不為琦辯，雖風骨靡而不振，其韞富矣。自韓愈氏至於宋，變唐人之體而去其辭，而又不及也。然而探賾鉤深，咀載道要，刋落華藻而歸之本根，雖時有蕪陋，然其淵源正矣。劉禹錫曰：「三代之文，至戰國而病，涉秦、漢復起；漢之文，至列國而病，唐興復起。」如是，則盛衰有時，勢極必返矣，孰振之哉？而朱子謂「韓文不如漢，漢文不如先秦、戰國」，則直以古今風氣日趨於澆薄已耳，孰靡之哉？此可言而不可知者也。意者文之有高下，以氣之淳澆耶？氣之有淳澆，以運之升降耶？合之則古今之升降為一代，而分之則一代之升降為古今。故觀之風與水之推移，而二子之說可互見也。雖然，渙之文至矣，然而聖人曰：「渙者，離也。物不可以終離，故授之以節。」又何以說也？國家文化宣朗，與帝典王風比隆較烈。自弘、
translation_en:
Yet they steeped themselves deeply and fermented a rich aroma, threading through the Hundred Schools; their diction was plain, accessible, and refined, avoiding奇巧 sophistry. Even though their vigor and structure grew slack and failed to rouse, what they held within was abundant indeed. From Han Yu 韓愈 down to the Song dynasty, writers altered the style of the men of Tang and cast off their diction, yet once again failed to equal them. Even so, they plumbed the abstruse and hooked out the profound, savoring and conveying the essentials of the Way, stripping away flowery ornament and returning to the fundamental root. Though at times their writing was overgrown or crude, its source and lineage were orthodox indeed.

Liu Yuxi 劉禹錫 said: "The literature of the Three Dynasties fell ill by the Warring States period, and revived as it passed into the Qin and Han; the literature of the Han fell ill by the era of the Divided Kingdoms, and revived with the rise of the Tang." If this is so, then flourishing and decline have their seasons, and when a trend reaches its extreme it must turn back—who then is the one that rouses it? Yet Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] maintained that "Han Yu's prose is not as good as that of the Han, and Han prose is not as good as that of the pre-Qin and Warring States," which simply regards the ethos of antiquity and the present as daily tending toward thinness and superficiality—who then is the one that makes it slacken? This is something that can be spoken of, yet cannot be fully known.

Could it be that literature has its high and low because the vital ethos (qi) is either pure or thin? And that the vital ethos is pure or thin because the cosmic cycle rises or falls? Taken together, the rise and fall of antiquity and the present form a single epoch; divided, the rise and fall of a single epoch form antiquity and the present. Therefore, if we observe the shifting movements of wind and water, the theories of the two masters can be seen to complement one another. Even so, the literary pattern of Dispersion (Huan 渙) is supreme; yet the Sage said: "Dispersion means separation. Things cannot end in separation, and therefore it is followed by Regulation (Jie 節)." How is this to be explained?

The literary culture of our Dynasty shines forth brightly, rivaling in splendor and brilliance the canons of the Emperors and the airs of the Kings. Since the Hongzhi (1488–1505) and Zhengde (1506–1521) eras…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
正以來鴻裁哲匠操觚登壇脩詞之子景
合雲起靡然嚮風家握隨侯人懷和氏口
不掛江左之籍目不涉唐宋之簡直欲極
騁逸軌於先秦兩漢之間而上與六籍接
跡豈不甚瓌壯哉執事乃憂其太過有意
還淳反朴一與之更始此非諸生之所及
也竊甞頫仰古今而求文之齊以高下以
爲其相習而不察者其過有六而詞不與
焉其相推而不可已者其敝有四而文亦
===
不與焉六過者繳繳然在文之中而四敝
者墨墨然出乎文之外所謂可知而不可
言者也甞言其似夫文者器也器各有體
體方圓也彼莊生論議之文也故雖徵之
以寓言而不可謂之史馬遷叙事之史也
故雖濟之以談說而不可謂之文今不思
遷之爲史也而槩模之以爲文是猶慕璧
之圓而規瓚之邸也失其裁矣是何也不
辨體之過也大塊噫而萬竅皆號比竹者
punctuated: 正以來，鴻裁哲匠，操觚登壇，脩詞之子，景合雲起，靡然嚮風。家握隨侯，人懷和氏，口不掛江左之籍，目不涉唐、宋之簡，直欲極騁逸軌於先秦、兩漢之間，而上與六籍接跡，豈不甚瓌壯哉！執事乃憂其太過，有意還淳反朴，一與之更始，此非諸生之所及也。竊甞頫仰古今，而求文之齊以高下，以爲其相習而不察者，其過有六，而詞不與焉；其相推而不可已者，其敝有四，而文亦不與焉。六過者，繳繳然在文之中；而四敝者，墨墨然出乎文之外，所謂可知而不可言者也。甞言其似：夫文者，器也，器各有體，體方圓也。彼莊生，論議之文也，故雖徵之以寓言，而不可謂之史；馬遷，叙事之史也，故雖濟之以談說，而不可謂之文。今不思遷之爲史也，而槩模之以爲文，是猶慕璧之圓而規瓚之邸也，失其裁矣。是何也？不辨體之過也。大塊噫而萬竅皆號，比竹者…
translation_en: …and Zhengde eras (1488–1521) onward, master craftsmen of grand literary designs have taken up their writing tablets and ascended the podium; students of rhetoric have gathered like shadows and risen like clouds, swept along by the prevailing trend. Every household clutches the Pearl of the Marquis of Sui, and every person cherishes the Jade of Mr. He; their mouths do not mention the books of the Southern Dynasties, and their eyes do not touch the bamboo slips of the Tang and Song. They wish nothing less than to gallop to the utmost along the unrestrained tracks of the pre-Qin and the two Han dynasties, and to follow directly in the footsteps of the Six Classics above—is this not magnificent and grand indeed! Yet Your Excellency worries that this goes too far, and intends to return to pureness and revert to simplicity, making a fresh start with them altogether; this is beyond what we students could have reached. I have privately reflected upon antiquity and the present, seeking the standards by which literature is judged high or low. I consider that in what people habitually practice without examination, there are six faults, and diction is not among them; in what they mutually promote without being able to stop, there are four abuses, and literary form is likewise not among them. The six faults are glaringly apparent within the writing itself, whereas the four abuses lie darkly outside the writing—this is what is meant by that which can be known yet cannot be put into words. Let me try to speak of them by way of analogy. Now literature is like a vessel; each vessel has its own form, and forms are either square or round. That Master Zhuang (Zhuangzi) wrote essays of discourse and argument; therefore, even though he substantiated them with parables, his work cannot be called history. Sima Qian wrote history that narrates events; therefore, even though he supplemented it with discussions and persuasions, his work cannot be called belles-lettres. Nowadays people do not consider that Sima Qian's work is history, and uniformly model themselves upon it to compose literary essays; this is like admiring the roundness of a bi jade disk and rounding off the square base of a zan libation ladle—it loses its proper measure. Why is this? It is the fault of not distinguishing genres. When the Great Clod breathes out, ten thousand hollows all roar; if one who arranges bamboo pipes…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
一一而吹之以稱於天籟則遠矣春氣生
而百昌皆遂雕玉者葉葉而鐫之以稱於
大巧則迂矣文而肖此至陋也是何也不
練氣之過也夫握徑寸之珠而衣褐入市
不以為窶家有敝帚享之千金而過者無
不唉也君子誠有高世之識則辭之所運
縱横曲直無所不可若必求工於偏解矜
激乎一致而以片語單辭仰模作者雖精
不逮矣是何也不廣識之過也梓慶之為
===
鐻也十年而不敢懷非譽巧拙栗林父之
承蜩不以天地萬物易蜩之翼彼篤於物
者猶若是若乃夫績文之士逐時以為工
偶世以為好失已者也是何也不定志之
過也夫五味調鼎而和羹之啜不辨酸鹹
五音成文而咸池之奏如出一管是故古
之為文者沉涵百氏醞釀千古茫乎泱泱
而不知其門若夫學一先生之言讀之而
可辨也則下矣是何也不儲學之過也夫
punctuated: 一一而吹之，以稱於天籟，則遠矣；春氣生而百昌皆遂，雕玉者葉葉而鐫之，以稱於大巧，則迂矣。文而肖此，至陋也。是何也？不練氣之過也。夫握徑寸之珠而衣褐入市，不以為窶；家有敝帚，享之千金，而過者無不唉也。君子誠有高世之識，則辭之所運，縱横曲直，無所不可；若必求工於偏解，矜激乎一致，而以片語單辭仰模作者，雖精不逮矣。是何也？不廣識之過也。梓慶之為鐻也，十年而不敢懷非譽巧拙；栗林父之承蜩，不以天地萬物易蜩之翼。彼篤於物者猶若是，若乃夫績文之士，逐時以為工，偶世以為好，失已者也。是何也？不定志之過也。夫五味調鼎，而和羹之啜不辨酸鹹；五音成文，而《咸池》之奏如出一管。是故古之為文者，沉涵百氏，醞釀千古，茫乎泱泱，而不知其門；若夫學一先生之言，讀之而可辨也，則下矣。是何也？不儲學之過也。夫
translation_en: … blows on them one by one in order to match the piping of heaven, he is far from the mark; when the vital breath of spring arises, the hundred flourishing things all come to fruition, yet if a jade-carver engraves them leaf by leaf in order to match the Great Artificer's skill, he is misguided indeed. For writing to resemble this is the height of crudeness. Why is this? It is the fault of not cultivating one's vital energy (qi). Now, if one holds a pearl an inch in diameter and enters the marketplace wearing coarse cloth, no one considers him impoverished; if a family possesses a worn-out broom and treasures it as worth a thousand pieces of gold, no passerby will fail to laugh at them. If a gentleman truly possesses insight that transcends the age, then in the deployment of his words—whether sweeping or restrained, indirect or straightforward—nothing will be amiss; whereas if he insists on seeking skill in one-sided interpretations, strains after a single fixed pattern, and relies on isolated phrases and single words to imitate the master writers of the past, even if he is meticulous, he will fall short. Why is this? It is the fault of not broadening one's insight. When Woodworker Qing (Zi Qing 梓慶) made a bell-stand, for ten years [?] he dared not harbor thoughts of blame or praise, skill or clumsiness; when Lilin Fu 栗林父 [the hunchback in *Zhuangzi*] caught cicadas, he would not trade the wings of a cicada for heaven, earth, and the myriad things. If even those who devote themselves to external things are like this, then as for scholars who weave literary compositions—chasing the trends of the time as skill, and conforming to the world to win favor—they are ones who have lost themselves. Why is this? It is the fault of not fixing one's resolve. Now, when the five flavors are blended in a cauldron, one who sips the harmonious broth cannot distinguish sour from salty; when the five notes form a musical composition, the performance of the *Xianchi* 咸池 music sounds as if it came from a single pipe. Therefore, the writers of antiquity immersed themselves in the hundred schools and steeped themselves in a thousand ages, vast and boundless, so that no one knew the gateway by which they entered; whereas if one merely studies the words of a single master, so that upon reading one's work the model can be recognized, that is inferior indeed. Why is this? It is the fault of not accumulating learning. Now, …

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
文者以神會者也得其似而未真是胡寛
之營新豐也得其真而未化是優孟之學
叔敖也古有以舞劒而悟書者入神矣若
乃不求其所以言而丹青藻綠惟其色之
是肖不亦遠哉是何也不會神之過也是
故文有六過而辭之工拙不與焉此世之
所習而不察也雖然未足憂也世之所憂
者在於頹波横流不知紀極視之若甚緩
而其關於世道之升降不啻形響故不可
===
弗之思矣請畢其說夫古之人非不能艶
采辯說窮極瑰麗以駭里耳也以為文而
至於夸則太俓而無統元氣漓矣故弗為
也又非不能哀歌伉慨眦裂髮指若彈鋏
擊筑之流也以為文而至於悲非治世之
音太和散矣故弗為也又非不能離析堅
白連類要眇若畫工之圖鬼魅也以為文
而至於怪是陋者之所託雅道流矣故弗
為也又非不能雕鏤刻畫棘喉滯吻以呈
punctuated: 文者，以神會者也。得其似而未真，是胡寛之營新豐也；得其真而未化，是優孟之學叔敖也。古有以舞劒而悟書者，入神矣。若乃不求其所以言，而丹青藻綠惟其色之是肖，不亦遠哉！是何也？不會神之過也。是故文有六過，而辭之工拙不與焉，此世之所習而不察也。雖然，未足憂也。世之所憂者，在於頹波横流，不知紀極，視之若甚緩，而其關於世道之升降不啻形響，故不可弗之思矣。請畢其說。夫古之人非不能艶采辯說、窮極瑰麗以駭里耳也，以為文而至於夸，則太俓而無統，元氣漓矣，故弗為也；又非不能哀歌伉慨、眦裂髮指，若彈鋏擊筑之流也，以為文而至於悲，非治世之音，太和散矣，故弗為也；又非不能離析堅白、連類要眇，若畫工之圖鬼魅也，以為文而至於怪，是陋者之所託，雅道流矣，故弗為也；又非不能雕鏤刻畫、棘喉滯吻以呈
translation_en: …writing is something grasped through the spirit. To capture its likeness without its true essence is like Hu Kuan 胡寬 building Xinfeng 新豐; to capture its true essence without achieving transformation is like Jester Meng (You Meng 優孟) imitating Sunshu Ao 叔敖. In antiquity, there were those who comprehended calligraphy by watching a sword dance—that was entering the realm of the spirit. If instead one does not seek the reason behind the words, and merely imitates their outward colors in vermilion, blue, and ornate green, is that not far off the mark? Why is this? It is the fault of failing to commune with the spirit. Therefore, in writing there are six faults, and the skill or clumsiness of the diction is not even among them; this is what the world practices habitually without examining. Even so, this is not yet cause enough for worry. What the world should worry about is that decadent waves are overflowing without bound or limit; looking at it, the matter seems quite unurgent, yet its bearing on the rise and fall of the moral order of the world is no less immediate than shadow to form or echo to sound, so one cannot fail to reflect upon it. Allow me to set forth the argument in full. Now, it is not that the ancients were incapable of艷 resplendent coloration and eloquent disputation, exhausting the extremes of magnificence to startle vulgar ears; they considered that when writing reaches the point of boastful exaggeration, it becomes too headlong and lacks unity, so that primal vitality is thinned out—therefore they did not do it. Nor is it that they were incapable of singing mournfully with impassioned fervor, eyes splitting and hair standing on end, like the sort who tapped the sword-hilt or struck the lute (zhu 筑); they considered that when writing reaches the point of sorrow, it is not the music of an ordered age, and supreme harmony is dissipated—therefore they did not do it. Nor is it that they were incapable of splitting "hard and white" (jianbai 堅白) and linking analogies in abstruse subtlety, like painters depicting ghosts and goblins; they considered that when writing reaches the point of the bizarre, it becomes the refuge of the shallow, and the way of elegance is swept away—therefore they did not do it. Nor is it that they were incapable of carving and engraving words, making them thorny to the throat and halting to the lips in order to display…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
其工也以爲文而至於巧言華道隱太朴
鑿矣故弗爲也此四者古人之所謂敝也
乃今講業之士盛稱引以爲高舉天下而
羣赴之若鵠不知其比於夸與悲而以爲
壯麗也不知其近於巧與怪而以爲瓌奇
也得非有所推而不已者乎夫六者之過
也過於文之中憂在文而不在世四者之
敝也敝於文之外憂在世而不在文此遠
識之士所爲察機於微眇而口不得言者
===
也乃執事又舉古著書論文者數家以資
諸生射覆此非所以索於文之外矣夫魏
文之爲典論直品第建安名家而陸機文
賦備述九變盡其曲折劉勰文心雕龍十
卷其詞辯博不可殫述而摯虞爲文章流
別論捃摭上下亦無餘蘊然皆藝苑之指
南而非世教之砥柱可略而無談矣愚獨
以爲
聖明在上誠欲還淳返朴以成
punctuated:
其工也；以爲文而至於巧，言華道隱，太朴鑿矣，故弗爲也。此四者，古人之所謂敝也，乃今講業之士，盛稱引以爲高，舉天下而羣赴之若鵠，不知其比於夸與悲而以爲壯麗也，不知其近於巧與怪而以爲瓌奇也，得非有所推而不已者乎？夫六者之過也，過於文之中，憂在文而不在世；四者之敝也，敝於文之外，憂在世而不在文。此遠識之士所爲察機於微眇，而口不得言者也。

乃執事又舉古著書論文者數家，以資諸生射覆，此非所以索於文之外矣。夫魏文之爲《典論》，直品第建安名家；而陸機《文賦》，備述九變，盡其曲折；劉勰《文心雕龍》十卷，其詞辯博，不可殫述；而摯虞爲《文章流別論》，捃摭上下，亦無餘蘊。然皆藝苑之指南，而非世教之砥柱，可略而無談矣。愚獨以爲聖明在上，誠欲還淳返朴，以成
translation_en:
…their artistry; yet they held that when writing reaches the point of clever artifice, words become華 [flowery] while the Way is obscured, and primordial simplicity is chiseled away, so they refused to do it. These four things are what the ancients called corruptions. Yet scholars pursuing their studies today lavishly praise and cite them as lofty, and the whole world flocks to them in droves as if aiming at a target. Unaware that such writing borders on boastfulness and sorrow, they regard it as magnificent; unaware that it approaches clever artifice and weirdness, they regard it as extraordinary. Could this not be the result of trends being pushed ever onward without cease? Now, the faults of the six types are faults within writing itself; the concern lies with literature and not with the world. The corruptions of the four types are corruptions that go beyond writing; the concern lies with the world and not with literature. This is why men of far-sighted discernment perceive the subtle signs of change in their faintest beginnings, even when their mouths cannot speak of them.

Now Your Excellency has further cited several ancient authors who wrote treatises on literature, so as to test us students in guessing the hidden sources; yet this is not the way to seek what lies beyond writing itself. When Emperor Wen of Wei (Cao Pi 曹丕) composed the Normative Discourses (Dianlun 典論), he merely ranked the celebrated writers of the Jian'an 建安 era; Lu Ji 陸機 in his Poetic Exposition on Literature (Wenfu 文賦) gave a complete account of the nine transformations, exhausting all their intricacies; Liu Xie 劉勰 in the ten scrolls of his Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons (Wenxin diaolong 文心雕龍) used language so eloquent and wide-ranging that it cannot be fully recounted; and Zhi Yu 摯虞, in composing the Discourse on the Streams and Branches of Literature (Wenzhang liubie lun 文章流別論), gathered material from antiquity to the present, leaving nothing unexplored. Yet all of these are merely compasses for the garden of letters, not pillars for the moral instruction of the age; they may be passed over without discussion. I alone hold that with the Sacred and Enlightened Ruler above, if he truly wishes to restore purity and return to simplicity so as to achieve…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
一代文明之治則莫若使人務學務學者何以
博文強識爲能而不以虛辭籍也又莫若
正本正本者何以六經孔孟爲宗而不以
百家之說間也又莫若尚實尚實者何以
好脩篤行爲賢而不以浮華取也如是則
靡巧之敝革淳朴之原啟而治道之隆見
矣此易之所謂節也
第三問
方鳴盛
===
同考試官教諭樊批鴻鉅之士雅先識量于能
尚論先哲究極本原足覘胸中抱負矣
同考試官學正翁批古大臣不標能見奇而斷
斷休休所建豎自別是作援引詳確而軒輊較然他日必可任重者
考試官教諭趙批即子所陳說蘊藉可知
考試官教諭林批才德大小之辨允爲確論
古之所謂大受者有應天下之識有勝天
下之量者也識者何高視玄覽創思遠圖
揆善敗之端究是非之紀萬物竝興莫不
punctuated:
一代文明之治，則莫若使人務學。務學者何？以博文強識爲能，而不以虛辭籍也。又莫若正本。正本者何？以六經、孔、孟爲宗，而不以百家之說間也。又莫若尚實。尚實者何？以好脩篤行爲賢，而不以浮華取也。如是，則靡巧之敝革，淳朴之原啟，而治道之隆見矣。此《易》之所謂「節」也。

第三問
方鳴盛
同考試官教諭樊批：鴻鉅之士，雅先識量。于能尚論先哲，究極本原，足覘胸中抱負矣。
同考試官學正翁批：古大臣不標能見奇，而斷斷休休，所建豎自別。是作援引詳確，而軒輊較然，他日必可任重者。
考試官教諭趙批：即子所陳說，蘊藉可知。
考試官教諭林批：才德大小之辨，允爲確論。

古之所謂大受者，有應天下之識，有勝天下之量者也。識者何？高視玄覽，創思遠圖，揆善敗之端，究是非之紀，萬物竝興，莫不
translation_en:
… the enlightened governance of an entire era, then nothing is better than causing men to devote themselves to learning. What is meant by devoting oneself to learning? It is to take breadth of learning and retentiveness of memory as ability, rather than relying on empty verbiage. Furthermore, nothing is better than rectifying the fundamentals. What is meant by rectifying the fundamentals? It is to take the Six Classics, Confucius (Kong), and Mencius (Meng) as the standard, without allowing the doctrines of the Hundred Schools to intrude. Furthermore, nothing is better than prizing substance. What is meant by prizing substance? It is to regard the love of self-cultivation and earnest conduct as worthiness, rather than selecting men on the basis of superficial華 ornamentation. If this is done, then the abuses of extravagant artifice will be reformed, the wellspring of honest simplicity will be opened, and the flourishing of the way of governance will become manifest. This is what the Book of Changes (Yi) calls "regulation" (jie).

Question Three
Fang Mingsheng 方鳴盛
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Fan 樊: Men of grand stature always put insight and capacity first. You are able to critically evaluate the former sages and exhaustively trace things to their fundamental source; this is sufficient to reveal the aspirations within your breast.
Comment by Associate Examiner Confucian School Director Weng 翁: The great ministers of antiquity did not flaunt their abilities or display novelty; rather, single-minded and broad-minded, their achievements naturally stood apart. This essay's citations are detailed and exact, and its weighing of relative merits is crystal clear—here is someone who will surely be capable of bearing heavy responsibilities in the future.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zhao 趙: From what you have set forth, the depth of your inner cultivation can be known.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Lin 林: Your distinction between great and small in talent and virtue is truly a definitive argument.

Those who in antiquity were said to be capable of undertaking great responsibilities possessed the insight to respond to all under Heaven and the capacity to bear the weight of all under Heaven. What is insight? Looking from on high and perceiving the profound, originating thoughts and planning far ahead, measuring the beginnings of success and failure, and investigating the governing principles of right and wrong—when the myriad things arise together, there is none that does not…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
響應明不足道也量者何幷包兼蓄一齊
殊軌以靜持躁以重待輕險夷輻輳莫之
動搖弘不足道也識而擴之以量然後權
疑制變應天下而不窮量而濟之以識然
後員大荷艱勝天下而不匱自古及今所
以極立人紀恢翊世運撥亂反正排難解
紛必此人者爲之而非世之所幾矣嗟夫
士當其居常無事扼捥鼓頰天下非難爲
也卒有意外之變禍福利害亟如迅霆旋
===
轉易形呼吸異狀有不但顏怖肝怵然而
自喪者乎無有矣甚至得失憂喜之微口
吻所不道一旦感於心之所易忽而發於
情之所難隱有不暴越其底裏而莫之韜
匿者乎無有矣若此者固非才之不足也
程子有言人惟識量不可强今人有所見
卑下者識量不足也而張子韶謂器局欲
大識見欲遠宋人議論好窮本原依於道
德則所稱引必有試矣請先言其義夫世
punctuated: 響應，明不足道也。量者何？幷包兼蓄，一齊殊軌，以靜持躁，以重待輕，險夷輻輳，莫之動搖，弘不足道也。識而擴之以量，然後權疑制變，應天下而不窮；量而濟之以識，然後員大荷艱，勝天下而不匱。自古及今，所以極立人紀、恢翊世運、撥亂反正、排難解紛，必此人者爲之，而非世之所幾矣。嗟夫！士當其居常無事，扼捥鼓頰，天下非難爲也。卒有意外之變，禍福利害，亟如迅霆，旋轉易形，呼吸異狀，有不但顏怖肝怵，然而自喪者乎？無有矣。甚至得失憂喜之微，口吻所不道，一旦感於心之所易忽，而發於情之所難隱，有不暴越其底裏而莫之韜匿者乎？無有矣。若此者，固非才之不足也。程子有言：「人惟識量不可强。今人有所見卑下者，識量不足也。」而張子韶謂：「器局欲大，識見欲遠。」宋人議論，好窮本原，依於道德，則所稱引必有試矣。請先言其義。夫世
translation_en:
…respond like an echo; mere perspicacity is not worth mentioning. What is capacity? It embraces and stores all things together, unifying divergent paths, countering restlessness with calm and meeting levity with gravity; though peril and safety converge like spokes at a hub, nothing can shake it—mere breadth is not worth mentioning. When insight is broadened by capacity, only then can one weigh doubts and master change, responding to the world without exhaustion. When capacity is aided by insight, only then can one shoulder what is great and bear what is arduous, sustaining the world without depletion. From antiquity to the present, establishing the ultimate standards of human order, expanding and supporting the fortunes of the age, quelling disorder and restoring the right, and resolving difficulties and untangling confusions—such feats have always been accomplished by men of this kind, who are rarely to be hoped for in the world.

Alas! In ordinary times when nothing is amiss, a scholar clasps his wrists and wags his cheeks in talk, as if nothing in the world were difficult to accomplish. Yet when an unexpected crisis suddenly arises, and fortune and misfortune, advantage and harm strike as swiftly as a thunderbolt—whirling about and shifting form, changing shape between one breath and the next—is there anyone who does not merely pale in the face and tremble in his liver, utterly losing his composure? There is none. Even in slight matters of gain and loss, sorrow and joy, which he would never deign to speak of with his lips, once he is stirred where his mind easily overlooks its guard and gives vent to feelings that are hard to conceal, is there anyone who does not expose his innermost depths, unable to hide them? There is none. In cases such as these, the fault certainly does not lie in an insufficiency of talent.

Master Cheng (Chengzi 程子) once said: "Only a person's insight and capacity cannot be forced. When people today hold base and shallow views, it is because their insight and capacity are insufficient." And Zhang Zishao 張子韶 (Zhang Jiucheng 張九成) said: "One's vessel and scope should be great; one's insight and vision should be far-reaching." The discussions of the men of Song loved to probe fundamental origins and relied upon the Way and its virtue; thus what they cited and commended must have been put to the test. title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
所謂識者不以其權奇慧辨為察而已乎
而實非也譬之登高登塊阜之丘則十里
不能隱登名都之鎮則百里不能隱登岱
華之巔而天下弗能隱也所處高焉耳矣
夫世所謂量者不以其儃慢迂恢為容而
已乎而又非也譬之量物以鍾釡受則升
斗不能滿以江河受則鍾釡不能滿以尾
閭歸墟受而天下弗能滿也所蓄深焉耳
矣是故其豫之有素其徵之有時其持之
===
有故其出之有宜往往以卒然之應而關
天下之安危以偶然之感而定終身之優
劣是故天下之事有所迫焉而易懾而氣
不為之撓有所交焉而易惑而目不為之
眩有所發焉而易擾而志不為之亂有所
拂焉而易怨而色不為之怍有所觸焉而
易驚而神不為之動此所謂識與量也而
明問所指者即其人矣可得而揚搉之乎
夫桓溫操問鼎之謀而陳兵新亭之下廷
punctuated: 所謂識者，不以其權奇慧辨為察而已乎？而實非也。譬之登高：登塊阜之丘，則十里不能隱；登名都之鎮，則百里不能隱；登岱華之巔，而天下弗能隱也，所處高焉耳矣。夫世所謂量者，不以其儃慢迂恢為容而已乎？而又非也。譬之量物：以鍾釡受，則升斗不能滿；以江河受，則鍾釡不能滿；以尾閭歸墟受，而天下弗能滿也，所蓄深焉耳矣。是故其豫之有素，其徵之有時，其持之有故，其出之有宜，往往以卒然之應而關天下之安危，以偶然之感而定終身之優劣。是故天下之事，有所迫焉而易懾，而氣不為之撓；有所交焉而易惑，而目不為之眩；有所發焉而易擾，而志不為之亂；有所拂焉而易怨，而色不為之怍；有所觸焉而易驚，而神不為之動。此所謂識與量也，而明問所指者即其人矣，可得而揚搉之乎？夫桓溫操問鼎之謀，而陳兵新亭之下，廷
translation_en: …what the world calls insight: is it not merely taking cleverness,奇 novelty, sharpness, and eloquence to be discernment? Yet in reality it is not so. Compare it to ascending a height: if one ascends a mound of earth, then ten li cannot be hidden from view; if one ascends the guardian mountain of a famed metropolis, then a hundred li cannot be hidden; if one ascends the peaks of Mount Tai or Mount Hua, then the whole world cannot be hidden—it is simply that the vantage point one occupies is high! And as for what the world calls capacity: is it not merely taking laxity, remissness, circuitousness, and broadness to be tolerance? Yet again it is not so. Compare it to measuring things: if one receives them with a zhong or fu vessel, then a sheng or dou cannot fill it; if one receives them with the Yangtze or the Yellow River, then a zhong or fu cannot fill it; if one receives them with the Weilü drain and the Guixu abyss of the ocean, then the whole world cannot fill it—it is simply that what is stored within is deep! Therefore, their preparation is grounded in habitual cultivation, their verification comes at the right moment, what they uphold has a solid basis, and what they bring forth suits what is appropriate. Often, through a sudden response, they determine the security or peril of the empire, and through a chance stirring, they settle the superiority or inferiority of an entire life. Thus, among the affairs of the world, when something presses upon them so that one would easily be terrified, their spirit is not bent by it; when things cross before them so that one would easily be deluded, their eyes are not dazzled by them; when something breaks out so that one would easily be thrown into confusion, their will is not disordered by it; when something thwarts them so that one would easily feel resentment, their countenance is not discomposed by it; when something strikes against them so that one would easily be startled, their mind is not moved by it. This is what is meant by insight and capacity. And the figures to whom Your enlightened question refers were just such men—may I be permitted to discuss and evaluate them? Now, Huan Wen 桓溫 harbored the scheme of inquiring after the imperial tripods [usurping the throne] and arrayed his troops below Xinting 新亭; the court…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
臣皆爼上肉耳然而謝安從容就坐談咲
自如辭未及畢而壁後之甲解矣是大傅
以一咲之驩而存晉之宗祊也回紇以傾
國之師侵至涇陽兩京如纍卵耳然子儀
單騎出見使之下馬羅拜交臂求和日隂
未移而勝負之機决矣是令公以一騎之
任而安唐之社稷也此非當人之所易懾
而不撓者乎以丞相而失印人之所徬徨
而急索者而裴度不問也左右復白果於
===
故處得之此何以故當吏人之竊急而隘
之則其情易敗而匿益堅緩而開之則其
間可乗而跡易觧故以不索索之也方大
閱而嵩呼人之所怖愕而急止者而張詠
弗駭也亦下馬東北嵩呼攬轡復行衆不
敢譁又何以故當萬衆讙嘵之時以令禁
之或反激而爲亂而置之不問且至難以
自明故以不止止之也此非當人之所易
惑而不眩者乎魏兵西下蜀以一旅當之
punctuated: 臣皆爼上肉耳。然而謝安從容就坐，談咲自如，辭未及畢，而壁後之甲解矣。是大傅以一咲之驩，而存晉之宗祊也。回紇以傾國之師侵至涇陽，兩京如纍卵耳。然子儀單騎出見，使之下馬羅拜，交臂求和，日隂未移，而勝負之機决矣。是令公以一騎之任，而安唐之社稷也。此非當人之所易懾而不撓者乎？以丞相而失印，人之所徬徨而急索者，而裴度不問也，左右復白，果於故處得之。此何以故？當吏人之竊，急而隘之，則其情易敗而匿益堅；緩而開之，則其間可乗而跡易觧，故以不索索之也。方大閱而嵩呼，人之所怖愕而急止者，而張詠弗駭也，亦下馬東北嵩呼，攬轡復行，衆不敢譁。又何以故？當萬衆讙嘵之時，以令禁之，或反激而爲亂，而置之不問，且至難以自明，故以不止止之也。此非當人之所易惑而不眩者乎？魏兵西下，蜀以一旅當之，
translation_en: …the court officials were all like meat on a chopping block. Yet Xie An 謝安 calmly took his seat, chatting and laughing as usual; before his words were even finished, the armored soldiers behind the wall were dismissed. Thus the Grand Mentor (taifu), with the joy of a single laugh, preserved the ancestral temple of the Jin dynasty. The Uyghurs (Huihe), with the entire army of their realm, invaded as far as Jingyang 涇陽, and the Two Capitals were as precarious as a stack of eggs. Yet Guo Ziyi 郭子儀 rode out alone on a single horse to meet them, causing them to dismount and bow in rows, clasping their arms to sue for peace; before the sun's shadow had even shifted, the decisive turn of victory and defeat was settled. Thus the Duke of Zhongshu (Linggong), taking responsibility upon a single horse, secured the altars of soil and grain of the Tang dynasty. Is this not being unyielding in the face of what easily terrifies others? For a Grand Councilor (chengxiang) to lose his official seal is something over which people would pace about in anxiety and urgently search; yet Pei Du 裴度 did not ask after it, and when his attendants reported again, they indeed found it in its old place. Why was this? When a clerk steals it, if one presses urgently and corners him, his crime is easily exposed and he will hide it all the more firmly; if one is unhurried and leaves an opening, he can take advantage of the interval and his tracks are easily absolved—thus he searched for it by not searching for it. Just as a grand military review was underway and the troops shouted "Long live the Emperor!" (songhu)—something at which people would be terrified and shocked and would urgently try to stop—Zhang Yong 張詠 was not startled; he too dismounted, faced northeast to shout "Long live the Emperor!", and then took up his reins and rode on, so the multitude dared not make an uproar. And why was this? At a moment when ten thousand men are clamoring, if one uses orders to forbid them, it might instead provoke them into rebellion; yet if one sets it aside and asks no questions, it would become difficult to clear oneself—thus he stopped it by not stopping it. Is this not remaining undazzled in the face of what easily bewilders others? When the armies of Wei marched west and Shu faced them with a single brigade…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
此何時也費禕乃圍棋對戲終日無倦而
識者知其辦賊契丹入寇車駕親幸澶淵
此何時也寇準方飲博歡呼倦而熟寐而
人主恃以無憂又何以故蓋兩國之壘旣
陳士而視吾之舉措爲安危也而吾以動
示之則恇怯而不振敵而視吾之淺深爲
進退也而吾以靜示之則恫疑而不前矣
此非當人之所易擾而不亂者乎狄仁傑
不知婁師德之薦巳也而欲出之於外師
===
德不自明也於是仁傑歎曰婁公盛德我
爲所包容久矣寇準不知王旦之薦巳也
而數短之於上旦不爲慍也且對眞宗曰
準對上無所隱益見其忠直夫二者非奇
節也獨以世之論交者當其聲名相藉之
時則異形爲肝膽而至於權位相軋之日
則同心爲胡越况於施德而不知者乎故
二公者可謂當人之所易怨而不忤矣裴
行儉以器識論人者也其平都支出所獲
punctuated: 此何時也？費禕乃圍棋對戲，終日無倦，而識者知其辦賊。契丹入寇，車駕親幸澶淵，此何時也？寇準方飲博歡呼，倦而熟寐，而人主恃以無憂。又何以故？蓋兩國之壘旣陳，士而視吾之舉措爲安危也，而吾以動示之，則恇怯而不振；敵而視吾之淺深爲進退也，而吾以靜示之，則恫疑而不前矣。此非當人之所易擾而不亂者乎？狄仁傑不知婁師德之薦巳也，而欲出之於外，師德不自明也。於是仁傑歎曰：「婁公盛德，我爲所包容久矣。」寇準不知王旦之薦巳也，而數短之於上，旦不爲慍也，且對眞宗曰：「準對上無所隱，益見其忠直。」夫二者非奇節也，獨以世之論交者，當其聲名相藉之時，則異形爲肝膽；而至於權位相軋之日，則同心爲胡、越，况於施德而不知者乎？故二公者，可謂當人之所易怨而不忤矣。裴行儉以器識論人者也，其平都支，出所獲
translation_en: … what a critical moment this was! Yet Fei Yi 費禕 played weiqi (Go) with a guest all day without tiring, and men of discernment knew from this that he could handle the invaders. When the Khitan invaded and the imperial carriage went in person to Chanyuan 澶淵, what a critical moment this was! Yet Kou Zhun 寇準 was drinking, gambling, and cheering, and when tired he fell fast asleep, while the sovereign relied on him to remain free of worry. And why was this so? Because once the ramparts of the two states are arrayed against each other, our own troops look to our every move to judge their safety or peril—if we show them agitation, they will grow fearful and lose heart; the enemy too looks to our depth of composure to decide whether to advance or retreat—if we show them calm, they will grow apprehensive and hesitate to press forward. Is this not remaining unperturbed where others are easily thrown into turmoil? Di Renjie 狄仁傑 did not know that Lou Shide 婁師德 had recommended him, and wished to have him sent out to a provincial post, yet Shide did not explain the truth for himself. Thereupon Renjie sighed and said, "Lord Lou is of abundant virtue; I have long been encompassed by his tolerance!" Kou Zhun did not know that Wang Dan 王旦 had recommended him, and repeatedly spoke of his shortcomings before the Emperor, yet Dan showed no displeasure, and moreover replied to Emperor Zhenzong 眞宗, "Zhun conceals nothing when speaking before Your Majesty, which all the more reveals his loyalty and rectitude." Now, these two cases were not extraordinary feats of integrity in themselves. It is only that among those in the world who speak of friendship, when they rely on each other to bolster their reputations, men in separate bodies act as close as liver and gall; yet when the day comes that they jostle over power and position, men of one mind become as estranged as the Hu 胡 of the north and the Yue 越 of the south—how much more so when one bestows a favor and the recipient does not even know of it! Thus these two lords may truly be said to have remained free of offense where others easily bear resentment. Pei Xingjian 裴行儉 was a man who judged others by their capacity and insight. When he pacified Duzhi 都支, he brought out the captured …

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
瑪瑙盤以示蕃酋將士忽爲軍士所跌而
色不少吝韓琦以寛厚稱者也其鎭大名
有獻玉杯二隻者一日出以宴客爲侍吏
所碎而神色不變夫二者至瑣事也然常
人之情當其志有所持或可以辭千乗而
至於情無所攝不能不失聲於破缶况千
金之璧乎故二公者可謂當人之所易驚
而不動矣夫使天下之事皆可以持筹預
計而運之掌握有知者盡能索耳惟其出
===
於卒然之應而有所不及圖故機之敏鈍
懸而識之高下列矣天下之事皆可以迫
性閑欲以號招名聲有足者能企及也惟
其出於偶然之感而有所不能强故體之
靜躁異而量之深淺形矣之數子者有應
天下之識有勝天下之量者也識足以應
天下故能當機立斷如迅弩之機敵不及
距而又擴之以量量足以勝天下故能從
容制動如萬仞之壁物不能搖而又濟之
punctuated: 瑪瑙盤以示蕃酋將士，忽爲軍士所跌，而色不少吝；韓琦以寛厚稱者也，其鎭大名，有獻玉杯二隻者，一日出以宴客，爲侍吏所碎，而神色不變。夫二者，至瑣事也。然常人之情，當其志有所持，或可以辭千乗，而至於情無所攝，不能不失聲於破缶，况千金之璧乎？故二公者，可謂當人之所易驚而不動矣。夫使天下之事，皆可以持筹預計，而運之掌握，有知者盡能索耳。惟其出於卒然之應，而有所不及圖，故機之敏鈍懸，而識之高下列矣；天下之事，皆可以迫性閑欲，以號招名聲，有足者能企及也。惟其出於偶然之感，而有所不能强，故體之靜躁異，而量之深淺形矣。之數子者，有應天下之識，有勝天下之量者也。識足以應天下，故能當機立斷，如迅弩之機，敵不及距，而又擴之以量；量足以勝天下，故能從容制動，如萬仞之壁，物不能搖，而又濟之
translation_en: …an agate platter to show the foreign chieftains and his officers and men; suddenly a soldier stumbled and broke it, yet his expression showed not the slightest regret. Han Qi 韓琦 was renowned for his generosity and magnanimity; when he was garrisoning Daming 大名, someone presented him with a pair of jade cups.
