One day he brought them out to feast his guests, and they were shattered by an attending clerk, yet his expression did not change. Now, these two incidents are utterly trivial matters. Yet in the nature of ordinary people, when their resolve is braced for something, they may be able to decline a state of a thousand chariots; but when their emotions are caught off guard, they cannot help crying out in dismay over a broken earthen jar—how much more so over a jade worth a thousand pieces of gold! Therefore, these two lords may be said to have remained unmoved in situations where others are easily startled. Now, suppose all affairs in the world could be calculated in advance with counting rods and manipulated in the palm of one's hand—anyone with intelligence could thoroughly figure them out. It is only because things arise requiring a sudden response where there is no time to plan that the gulf between agility and sluggishness at the critical juncture becomes wide, and the superiority or inferiority of one's insight is ranked. And suppose in all affairs in the world one could constrain one's nature and curb one's desires in order to court reputation and fame—anyone with feet could stand on tiptoe and reach it. It is only because things arise from a chance stimulus where one cannot force a posture that the difference between a composed and a restless disposition becomes distinct, and the depth or shallowness of one's capacity takes form. These several gentlemen possessed the insight to respond to the world and the capacity to bear the weight of the world. When insight is sufficient to respond to the world, one can make immediate decisions at the critical juncture, like the trigger of a swift crossbow that the enemy has no time to resist—and furthermore broaden it with capacity. When capacity is sufficient to bear the weight of the world, one can calmly control movement, like a cliff of ten thousand ren 仞 that external things cannot shake—and furthermore complement it…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
以識豪傑之士所以名成而不墮功立而
不穨垂鴻光於圖史流景燿於春秋也而
孔子之所謂大受者歟嗟夫士何其難論
也材有短長器有大小小者不可使大而
大亦不可以爲小短者不可使長而長亦
不可以爲短是故夏后氏之鼎鑄以九牧
之金度之廟堂爲國傳器然以之烹雞則
不能爲釜鬵之用吳鉤湛盧陸截犀兕水
斷鳧鵠萬戶之都不易而以之苴履則無
===
以效刀錐之能何者大小異分而長短殊
宜也故曰有大略者不可責以捷巧有小
智者不可任以大功今夫機智才辯之士
下者因時浮沉與波上下參偶比周以準
主意見便而赴知難而避不爲福始不爲
禍先其趨會投機非不工也左圓中規右
方協矩循令而行按法而治小文細謹白
黑不渝其奉官貞度非不當也或好謀喜
功見奇賈慧釋結應劇歘如轉圜舂如導
punctuated: 以識。豪傑之士所以名成而不墮，功立而不穨，垂鴻光於圖史，流景燿於春秋也。而孔子之所謂「大受」者歟！嗟夫，士何其難論也！材有短長，器有大小。小者不可使大，而大亦不可以爲小；短者不可使長，而長亦不可以爲短。是故夏后氏之鼎，鑄以九牧之金，度之廟堂，爲國傳器，然以之烹雞，則不能爲釜鬵之用；吳鉤、湛盧，陸截犀兕，水斷鳧鵠，萬戶之都不易，而以之苴履，則無以效刀錐之能。何者？大小異分，而長短殊宜也。故曰：「有大略者不可責以捷巧，有小智者不可任以大功。」今夫機智才辯之士：下者因時浮沉，與波上下，參偶比周，以準主意，見便而赴，知難而避，不爲福始，不爲禍先，其趨會投機非不工也；左圓中規，右方協矩，循令而行，按法而治，小文細謹，白黑不渝，其奉官貞度非不當也；或好謀喜功，見奇賈慧，釋結應劇，歘如轉圜，舂如導
translation_en:
…with insight. This is why heroic men of worth achieve fame that never falls and establish merit that never crumbles, leaving behind great brilliance in historical records and shedding bright luster through the ages. Is this not what Confucius (Kongzi 孔子) called being capable of "great responsibilities"?

Alas, how difficult it is to evaluate scholars! Talents have their shortcomings and strengths, and vessels have their small and large capacities. What is small cannot be made large, yet what is large likewise cannot be made to serve as small; what is short cannot be made long, yet what is long likewise cannot be made to serve as short. Therefore, the tripods of the Xia (夏) dynasty were cast from the metal tribute of the Nine Pastors and placed in the ancestral temple as heirloom vessels of the state; yet if one used them to boil a chicken, they could not serve the function of an ordinary pot or cauldron. A curved blade of Wu (吳鉤) or the sword Zhanlu (湛盧) can slice through rhinoceroses on land and sever wild ducks and swans in the water—they would not be traded even for a city of ten thousand households—yet if one used them to patch shoes, they could not match the effectiveness of a cobbler's knife or awl. Why is this? Because large and small have different allotments, and long and short suit different uses. Thus it is said: "Those who possess grand strategy cannot be demanded to show nimble cleverness; those who possess petty intelligence cannot be entrusted with great achievements."

Now consider scholars of quick wit, talent, and eloquence: The lowest among them drift up and down with the times, rising and falling with the waves, forming cliques and colluding to gauge the ruler's intentions; they rush toward advantage when they see it and shy away when they sense difficulty, never initiating good fortune and never standing at the forefront of disaster—their skill in seizing opportunities and exploiting the moment is by no means clumsy. Others draw circles with their left hand that match the compass and squares with their right that fit the T-square, acting in strict accordance with orders and governing by the letter of the law, scrupulous in minor formalities and petty details, never blurring black and white—their adherence to official duties and upholding of regulations is by no means improper. Still others are fond of stratagems and eager for exploits, displaying novelty and peddling cleverness, untangling knots and handling complex affairs as swiftly as turning a sphere and striking like guiding into…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
竅燒其精營以馳騖於世其樹聲進趣非
不利也談者察於一辭審於一技華言婾
說縱橫四出辯解連環捷過炙轂其晰微
研理非不奧也然而明於切切之迹而不
知大節之所由廉於間間之智而不知大
數之所紀誠使豪傑之士與之挈長於尺
寸較重於銖兩則有所不及矣要以定難
持傾應卒制決於咄嗟轉盻之間而樹蓋
世絕倫之績則其相懸也豈不甚哉何也
===
大受之才與小節異百司羣吏以用為才
者也故其才在技數將相大臣以不用為
才者也故其才在識量劉邵曰一官之任
以一味協五味一國之政以無味和五味
則明於大小之分而通於長短之宜者矣
雖然識有所蔽量有所塞今夫離朱之目
天下之至明也一塵眯之則不見丘山外
有所蔽也魏王之瓠可實五石呺然大也
堅而無竅則不能受卮水中有所塞也利
punctuated: 竅，燒其精營以馳騖於世，其樹聲進趣非不利也；談者察於一辭，審於一技，華言婾說，縱橫四出，辯解連環，捷過炙轂，其晰微研理非不奧也。然而明於切切之迹，而不知大節之所由；廉於間間之智，而不知大數之所紀。誠使豪傑之士與之挈長於尺寸、較重於銖兩，則有所不及矣；要以定難持傾，應卒制決於咄嗟轉盻之間，而樹蓋世絕倫之績，則其相懸也，豈不甚哉？何也？大受之才與小節異。百司羣吏，以用為才者也，故其才在技數；將相大臣，以不用為才者也，故其才在識量。劉邵曰：「一官之任，以一味協五味；一國之政，以無味和五味。」則明於大小之分，而通於長短之宜者矣。雖然，識有所蔽，量有所塞。今夫離朱之目，天下之至明也，一塵眯之，則不見丘山，外有所蔽也；魏王之瓠，可實五石，呺然大也，堅而無竅，則不能受卮水，中有所塞也。利
translation_en:
… cavities, burning away their vital spirit to gallop about in the world; their establishing of a reputation and advancing of their ambitions is by no means ineffective. Disputants scrutinize a single phrase and master a single skill; with ornate words and specious theories shooting forth in all directions, they untangle interlocking puzzles and are nimbler in speech than "Greasing the Axle" (Zhigu). Their analysis of subtleties and investigation of principles are by no means unprofound. Yet they are clear about trifling traces while ignorant of whence great integrity arises; they are sharp in petty cleverness while ignorant of the governing threads of the grand design. Truly, if a heroic man of outstanding talent were to measure lengths against them in inches and feet, or weigh against them in grains and ounces, he would fall short of them in some respects. Yet when it comes to settling crises and shoring up what is tottering, responding to emergencies and making decisive judgments in the blink of an eye or the heave of a sigh, and establishing achievements that overshadow the age and are beyond compare—how vast indeed is the gulf between them! Why is this so?

The talent for great responsibilities differs from minor scruples. The various bureaus and multitude of lesser officials are those who take practical utility as talent; therefore, their talent lies in technical skills. Generals, chief councilors, and great ministers are those who take non-utility as talent; therefore, their talent lies in insight and capacity. Liu Shao 劉邵 said: "The duty of a single office uses one flavor to harmonize the five flavors; the governance of an entire state uses flavorlessness to blend the five flavors." This shows a clear understanding of the distinction between great and small, and a thorough grasp of what is appropriate to strengths and weaknesses. Even so, insight can be obscured, and capacity can be obstructed. Now, the eyes of Li Zhu 離朱 were the sharpest in the world, yet if a single speck of dust blinded them, he could not see hills and mountains—because there was something obscuring them from without. The gourd of the King of Wei 魏王 could hold five piculs and was hollowly huge, yet if it were solid and lacked an opening, it could not receive a single goblet of water—because there was something obstructing it from within. When profit…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
蔽之外則識易昏私塞之中則量易隘而
全才不幾於世矣故程子又謂學進則識
進識進則量進則學不可已也而學之要
在思誠誠則明明則不可蔽而量益宏誠
則虛虛則不可塞而識益遠故能適變無
方利用不匱定乎内外之分而辨乎榮辱
之境也夫伯昏瞀人之射臨百仞之淵足
外垂而神不慄當此之時禍福利害猶浮
芥也痀僂丈人之承蜩累丸二而不墜身
===
如厥株枸當此之時得失憂喜猶飛塵也
誠之至也士而論功名於當世若伯昏瞀
人之射與丈人之承蜩也則卓矣
第四問
袁時徹
同考試官訓導余批〔謀道成于相資此化理之〕
〔本子能推□□□剴切詳明□□□□□□□□□□□□□□粲〕
同考試官教諭李批〔□□□□之旨洞析治原而〕
〔國體民情歷歷中竅此經世之策非徒餖飣爲工者〕
punctuated:
蔽之外，則識易昏；私塞之中，則量易隘，而全才不幾於世矣。故程子又謂：「學進則識進，識進則量進。」則學不可已也。而學之要在思誠。誠則明，明則不可蔽，而量益宏；誠則虛，虛則不可塞，而識益遠。故能適變無方，利用不匱，定乎内外之分，而辨乎榮辱之境也。夫伯昏瞀人之射，臨百仞之淵，足外垂而神不慄，當此之時，禍福利害猶浮芥也；痀僂丈人之承蜩，累丸二而不墜，身如厥株枸，當此之時，得失憂喜猶飛塵也。誠之至也。士而論功名於當世，若伯昏瞀人之射與丈人之承蜩也，則卓矣。

第四問
袁時徹
同考試官訓導余批：〔謀道成于相資，此化理之本。子能推□□□，剴切詳明，□□□□□□□□□□□□□□粲。〕
同考試官教諭李批：〔□□□□之旨，洞析治原，而國體民情，歷歷中竅。此經世之策，非徒餖飣爲工者。〕
translation_en:
…[when pursuit of profit] obscures it from the outside, one's insight is easily darkened; when selfishness blocks it from the inside, one's capacity is easily narrowed, and complete talent is rarely seen in the world. Therefore, Master Cheng (Chengzi 程子) also said: "When learning advances, insight advances; when insight advances, capacity advances." Thus learning cannot cease. And the essential point of learning lies in reflecting upon sincerity. When one is sincere, one is clear-sighted; when one is clear-sighted, one cannot be obscured, and one's capacity becomes ever broader. When one is sincere, one is receptive; when one is receptive, one cannot be blocked, and one's insight becomes ever more far-reaching. Therefore, one can adapt to change without limit and put things to advantageous use without exhaustion, fixing the distinction between inner and outer and discerning the boundary between honor and disgrace. Consider the archery of Bohun Maoren 伯昏瞀人: standing at the edge of an abyss a hundred ren deep, with his feet overhanging the brink, his spirit did not tremble; at that moment, fortune and misfortune, advantage and harm, were like floating bits of straw. Or consider the hunchbacked old man catching cicadas: balancing two pellets on his pole without dropping them, he held his body like a dry tree stump and a withered branch; at that moment, gain and loss, grief and joy, were like flying dust. Such is the ultimate degree of sincerity. If a scholar-official approaches merit and fame in his own age in the manner of Bohun Maoren's archery and the old man's catching of cicadas, he will be truly outstanding.

Fourth Policy Question
Yuan Shiche 袁時徹
Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Yu 余: 〔Planning the Way is achieved through mutual support; this is the foundation of transformative governance. You are able to extend […], incisive, thorough, and clear, […] brilliant.〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Li 李: 〔On the purport of […], he penetrates to the source of governance, and regarding the dignity of the state and the conditions of the people, every point hits the mark. This is a policy essay for ordering the world, not one that merely takes pride in piecing together ornate phrases.〕

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭趙批議論縱橫無□策體
考試官教諭林批遠猷卓識深于時政有裨
天下之治必上下相說而後成而其機未
始不得於相畏夫治人之與見治於人也
分迥然殊也而相說之與相畏也情判然
別也然而勢固有相待而成而理固有相
因而至者上不畏下是以其下爲可侮也
侮而不已民且仇上故君子之不可失者
在人心也下不畏上是以其上爲可翫也
===
翫而不已君且仇下故小人之不可犯者
在紀綱也議者徒見先王煕皞之世百辟
萬姓驩忻交通以爲伾伾榛榛之俗固然
而孰知其所繇來蓋未始不從稟稟兢兢
而得也今不謹其所繇始而徒望於說道
之成至或師心任愛剖去藩籬一切儆懼
維持之義廢而不講即家人父子猶不能
以愛勝而以施之上下之際幾何其不潰
壞而卒以亂哉請因明問所及言之嘗聞
punctuated:
考試官教諭趙批：議論縱橫，無□策體。
考試官教諭林批：遠猷卓識，深于時政有裨。
天下之治，必上下相說而後成，而其機未始不得於相畏。夫治人之與見治於人也，分迥然殊也；而相說之與相畏也，情判然別也。然而勢固有相待而成，而理固有相因而至者。上不畏下，是以其下爲可侮也；侮而不已，民且仇上，故君子之不可失者在人心也。下不畏上，是以其上爲可翫也；翫而不已，君且仇下，故小人之不可犯者在紀綱也。議者徒見先王煕皞之世，百辟萬姓驩忻交通，以爲伾伾榛榛之俗固然，而孰知其所繇來，蓋未始不從稟稟兢兢而得也。今不謹其所繇始，而徒望於說道之成，至或師心任愛，剖去藩籬，一切儆懼維持之義廢而不講。即家人父子猶不能以愛勝，而以施之上下之際，幾何其不潰壞而卒以亂哉！請因明問所及言之。嘗聞…
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Zhao's comment: "The argument ranges freely and is completely fitting for [?] the form of a policy essay."
Examiner and Instructor Lin's comment: "Far-reaching counsel and outstanding insight, deeply beneficial to current governance."
The governance of the empire is necessarily accomplished only when superiors and inferiors delight in one another, yet the pivot of this never fails to be obtained from their standing in awe of one another. Now, governing others and being governed by others are vastly different in status; delighting in one another and standing in awe of one another are distinctly separate in sentiment. Nevertheless, circumstances inherently depend on one another to reach completion, and principles inherently build upon one another to arrive at their end. If superiors do not stand in awe of inferiors, they regard their inferiors as subject to abuse; when abuse does not cease, the people will come to resent their superiors—thus what the gentleman must never lose is the hearts of the people. If inferiors do not stand in awe of superiors, they regard their superiors as subject to trifling; when trifling does not cease, the ruler will come to resent his inferiors—thus what the petty man must never violate is the laws and institutions. Commentators merely see that in the peaceful and prosperous ages of the former kings, the hundred officials and myriad commoners communicated in joyful harmony, and they assume that those bustling and flourishing customs were simply so by nature; yet who knows that the source from which they came was never attained except through trembling caution and reverent care! Nowadays, if one is not heedful of how it begins and merely hopes for the completion of the Way of mutual delight—even to the point of following one's own inclinations and indulging in affection, tearing down protective barriers, and abandoning without discussion all principles of vigilance, awe, and maintenance of order—even within a family between father and son, affection alone cannot prevail; if this is applied to the relations between superiors and inferiors, how long before everything collapses into ruin and ends in disorder? I beg to speak of this in response to what your clear question has touched upon. I have heard…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
之易曰說以先民民忘其勞說以犯難民
忘其死說之大民勸矣哉此以言上下之
相說也蓋唐虞三代之治上下之情相通
上之視下真如赤子疾痛疴癢必關其身
下之視上真如父兄緩急休戚必同其慮
說者謂太和在成周宇宙間於時狴犴設
而不用機穽懸而不入上安所虞其下而
下安所猜其上哉然考諸詩書傳記所稱
凜凜乎人心之防而兢兢焉紀綱之飭若
===
恒見其可畏而不見其可說者書曰民可
近不可下又曰愚夫愚婦一能勝予此上
畏下之說也詩云維桑與梓必恭敬止又
云豈不爾思畏子不敢此下畏上之說也
夫聖人豈不樂有其皞皞而顧為是以相
聳動哉要以知上下之說不得之於說而
得之於畏耳秦不師古而日斬刈其民漢
興破觚為圓居官者長子孫似知所以聯
人心矣而閭巷之雄以武犯禁景武之世
punctuated: 之《易》曰：「說以先民，民忘其勞；說以犯難，民忘其死。說之大，民勸矣哉！」此以言上下之相說也。蓋唐、虞、三代之治，上下之情相通：上之視下，真如赤子，疾痛疴癢，必關其身；下之視上，真如父兄，緩急休戚，必同其慮。說者謂太和在成周宇宙間，於時狴犴設而不用，機穽懸而不入，上安所虞其下，而下安所猜其上哉？然考諸《詩》、《書》、傳、記所稱，凜凜乎人心之防，而兢兢焉紀綱之飭，若恒見其可畏，而不見其可說者。《書》曰：「民可近，不可下。」又曰：「愚夫愚婦，一能勝予。」此上畏下之說也。《詩》云：「維桑與梓，必恭敬止。」又云：「豈不爾思？畏子不敢。」此下畏上之說也。夫聖人豈不樂有其皞皞，而顧為是以相聳動哉？要以知上下之說，不得之於說，而得之於畏耳。秦不師古，而日斬刈其民。漢興，破觚為圓，居官者長子孫，似知所以聯人心矣，而閭巷之雄，以武犯禁，景、武之世，
translation_en: … it from the Book of Changes (Yi): "When through joy he leads the people, the people forget their toil; when through joy he faces difficulties, the people forget their death. How great is joy—the people are encouraged by it indeed!" This speaks of the mutual delight between superior and inferior. In the governance of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, the feelings of those above and those below communicated freely: superiors regarded their inferiors truly as newborn infants, whose every ache, pain, and itch necessarily concerned their own persons; inferiors regarded their superiors truly as fathers and elder brothers, whose urgencies, joys, and sorrows necessarily shared their same anxieties. Commentators say that Supreme Harmony filled the universe of the accomplished Zhou: at that time prisons were established yet went unused, traps and pitfalls were set yet none fell into them—why would superiors ever guard against their inferiors, and why would inferiors ever suspect their superiors? Yet when we examine what is recounted in the Book of Odes (Shi), the Book of Documents (Shu), and the commentaries and records, there is a trembling vigilance in guarding human hearts and a cautious care in rectifying discipline and order, as if they constantly saw what was to be feared rather than what was to be delighted in. The Book of Documents says: "The people should be cherished, not looked down upon." It also says: "Even a simple man or simple woman can triumph over me." This is the doctrine of superiors fearing inferiors. The Book of Odes says: "Even the mulberry and the catalpa must be treated with reverence." It also says: "How could I not long for you? Yet I fear you and do not dare." This is the doctrine of inferiors fearing superiors. Now, how could the sages not take pleasure in serene and contented harmony, instead acting thus to alarm and rouse one another? In essence, they knew that mutual delight between superior and inferior is not attained through delight itself, but through awe and fear. Qin did not take antiquity as its teacher, and daily slaughtered and mowed down its people. When Han arose, it pared away sharp corners to make things round, and those who held office raised sons and grandsons in their posts, seeming to understand how to bind human hearts together. Yet strongmen of the lanes and alleys violated prohibitions by force of arms; in the reigns of Emperors Jing and Wu, …

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
是以有游俠之誅若郭解諸人駢首就戮
似知所以振紀綱矣而鷹擊之吏快意屠
割元封之不是以有酷吏之任太史公以
好奇之才而身罹蠶室之禍見酷吏寵遇
之如此而游俠誅死之若彼故其辭多疾
首於酷吏而惓贊於游俠頗爲有慨而然
要之疾是也而贊非也紀綱人心相恃而
爲治游俠酷吏相倚而爲非下之不得不
畏上猶上之不得不畏下也是故死生制
===
命有受無反從下言之則爲治民從上言
之則爲教辟虐我則仇其君實甚從上言
之則爲誼辟從下言之則爲亂民何以明
其然也昔者周厲王川防其口而不能免
流彘之菑衛懿公鶴棄其民而無與共榮
澤之難此不畏下之致也夫人心也彼其
于民撫劒疾視之不暇而何暇於赤子之
視哉山陽亡徒蘇令起漢梅福以爲匹夫
窺國家之權輕而與上爭衡羽林虎賁擅
punctuated: 是以有游俠之誅，若郭解諸人駢首就戮，似知所以振紀綱矣；而鷹擊之吏快意屠割，元封之不，是以有酷吏之任。太史公以好奇之才，而身罹蠶室之禍，見酷吏寵遇之如此，而游俠誅死之若彼，故其辭多疾首於酷吏，而惓贊於游俠，頗爲有慨而然。要之，疾是也，而贊非也。紀綱、人心相恃而爲治，游俠、酷吏相倚而爲非。下之不得不畏上，猶上之不得不畏下也。是故死生制命，有受無反，從下言之則爲治民，從上言之則爲教辟；「虐我則仇」，其君實甚，從上言之則爲誼辟，從下言之則爲亂民。何以明其然也？昔者周厲王川防其口，而不能免流彘之菑；衛懿公鶴棄其民，而無與共榮澤之難：此不畏下之致也，夫人心也。彼其于民，撫劒疾視之不暇，而何暇於赤子之視哉？山陽亡徒蘇令起，漢梅福以爲匹夫窺國家之權輕，而與上爭衡；羽林、虎賁擅…
translation_en:
…For this reason there was the execution of the wandering knights-errant (youxia), such that men like Guo Jie 郭解 were put to death side by side, which seemed to show an understanding of how to rouse the laws and institutions. Yet hawk-like, rapacious officials took pleasure in slaughtering and carving up the people; because of the failings [? 元封之不] of the Yuanfeng era (110–105 BCE), there was consequently the employment of harsh officials (kuli). The Grand Historian (Taishigong, i.e., Sima Qian 司馬遷), possessing a talent fond of the extraordinary and having personally suffered the calamity of the silkworm chamber (castration), saw how harsh officials were favored and treated like this, while knights-errant were executed and died like that. Therefore, in his words he often bitterly resented the harsh officials while earnestly praising the knights-errant, doing so largely out of personal indignation. In sum, his resentment was right, but his praise was wrong. Laws and institutions and the hearts of the people depend on each other to achieve order; knights-errant and harsh officials feed off each other to do wrong. That those below cannot but fear those above is just like how those above cannot but fear those below.

Therefore, when life and death are determined by command, and there is only acceptance without defiance—spoken of from the perspective of those below, this makes for orderly people; spoken of from the perspective of those above, this makes for an instructive ruler [? 教辟]. When "if he mistreats us, he is our enemy," the fault of the ruler is extreme indeed—spoken of from the perspective of those above, this serves as a righteous admonition to the ruler; spoken of from the perspective of those below, this makes for rebellious people. How can we make clear that this is so? In antiquity, King Li of Zhou 周厲王 stopped up the people's mouths like damming a river, yet he could not escape the disaster of exile to Zhi 彘; Duke Yi of Wei 衛懿公 abandoned his people for the sake of his cranes, and so had no one to share in his peril at the Marsh of Rong 榮澤. This was the result of not fearing those below—of losing [? 夫] the hearts of the people. When those above scarcely have enough time to clutch their swords and glare fiercely at the people, what leisure do they have to regard them as newborn infants? When the fugitive convict Su Ling 蘇令 of Shanyang 山陽 rose up, Mei Fu 梅福 of the Han considered it a case of a commoner spying the lightness of the state's authority and contending for power with the ruler above. When the Rapid as Tigers (huben) and Forest of Plumes (yulin) imperial guards arbitrarily…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
殺征西將軍魏主不問高歡見而散財結
客此不畏上之效也失紀綱也彼其於君
揭竿嘑呼之不暇而何暇於父兄之衞哉
苟爲上者而亟反之知吾恃人心以安也
惕然覆舟朽索之是戒而不敢過求於下
則下必親而就之夫上方其畏時易感耳
不圖吾民之易使至于此也是安得不愈
說其下乎爲下者而亟反之知吾賴紀綱
以生也惕然三尺五刑之是懷而不敢責
===
===
望於上則上必親而安之夫下方其畏時
易德耳不圖吾君之易事至於斯也夫安
得不愈說其上乎卽是而古治之所以萃
叔世之所以離其大要可知已我
國家重熙累洽之化二百餘年來而我
皇上汲汲於太平之求七禩於茲矣然貪夫屠
伯之臯不絕於彈事而犯上干紀之刑時
挂於司敗或者以爲太平之未洽而思古
說道之難復愚則以爲
punctuated: 殺征西將軍，魏主不問，高歡見而散財結客。此不畏上之效也，失紀綱也。彼其於君，揭竿嘑呼之不暇，而何暇於父兄之衞哉？苟爲上者而亟反之，知吾恃人心以安也，惕然覆舟朽索之是戒，而不敢過求於下，則下必親而就之。夫上方其畏時，易感耳；不圖吾民之易使至于此也，是安得不愈說其下乎？爲下者而亟反之，知吾賴紀綱以生也，惕然三尺五刑之是懷，而不敢責望於上，則上必親而安之。夫下方其畏時，易德耳；不圖吾君之易事至於斯也，夫安得不愈說其上乎？卽是而古治之所以萃、叔世之所以離，其大要可知已。我國家重熙累洽之化二百餘年來，而我皇上汲汲於太平之求，七禩於茲矣。然貪夫屠伯之臯不絕於彈事，而犯上干紀之刑時挂於司敗。或者以爲太平之未洽，而思古說道之難復；愚則以爲
translation_en:
…murdered the General Who Conquers the West (Zhengxi jiangjun), the ruler of Wei did not hold them accountable; witnessing this, Gao Huan 高歡 dispersed his wealth to bind retainers to himself. This is the consequence of not fearing those above; it is the loss of laws and discipline. When they regard their ruler, they hardly have time enough to raise bamboo poles and shout in rebellion—what leisure would they have to defend him as a father or elder brother?

If those above urgently reverse this, knowing that we rely on the hearts of the people for security, and vigilantly take warning from the metaphors of the capsizing boat and the rotten reins so as not to make excessive demands upon those below, then those below will surely draw near and attach themselves to them. When those above are in a state of fear, they are easily moved; unexpectedly finding that our people are this easy to employ, how could they not take ever greater pleasure in those below? And if those below urgently reverse this, knowing that we depend on laws and discipline to survive, and vigilantly keep in mind the three-foot statute strips and the Five Punishments so as not to make resentful demands upon those above, then those above will surely draw near and give them peace. When those below are in a state of fear, they easily feel gratitude; unexpectedly finding that our ruler is this easy to serve, how could they not take ever greater pleasure in those above? From this, the essential reasons why governance in antiquity brought people together and why in later ages of decline they fell apart can be known.

Our dynasty's transformative rule of cumulative splendor and harmony has lasted for over two hundred years, and Our Majesty has been earnestly seeking grand peace for seven years now. Yet the crimes of greedy men and ruthless officials never cease in the impeachments, and punishments for offending superiors and violating discipline are constantly registered with the judicial officials (sibai). Some consider that grand peace has not yet been fully realized and reflect on how difficult it is to restore the ancient way of mutual pleasure; I, however, consider that…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
今日之政不患於上下之閒不相說而猶患
於相畏之未至夫所謂上者非必於
九重百戾之謂也自開府而下凡一命之寄一
成之長職在治民者皆得謂之上也所謂
下者非必於甕牖繩樞之謂也自齊民而
上凡鄉之搢紳學之青衿聽治於長者皆
得謂之下也今天下之吏爲
天子牧養元元豈無不侮不虐凜凜於四民之
上稱任職其人哉然而蔬戾恣睢顛倒三
===
尺法日漁獵而草艾之者不可謂無其人
也甚者上愚其監司之耳目而下箝其民
之吻舌明視而莫敢誰何者有矣天下之
民爲
國家供賦稅豈無不怨不庸兢兢於當世之
網稱醇固其俗哉然而誣上行私把持吏
長短日幸其有事而輕重之者不可謂無
其俗也甚者陰售其排陷之術而公倡爲
讙呼之禍迫逐而使之去者有矣有一於
punctuated: 今日之政，不患於上下之閒不相說，而猶患於相畏之未至。夫所謂上者，非必於九重、百戾之謂也；自開府而下，凡一命之寄、一成之長，職在治民者，皆得謂之上也。所謂下者，非必於甕牖、繩樞之謂也；自齊民而上，凡鄉之搢紳、學之青衿，聽治於長者，皆得謂之下也。今天下之吏為天子牧養元元，豈無不侮不虐，凜凜於四民之上，稱任職其人哉？然而蔬戾恣睢，顛倒三尺法，日漁獵而草艾之者，不可謂無其人也。甚者上愚其監司之耳目，而下箝其民之吻舌，明視而莫敢誰何者有矣。天下之民為國家供賦稅，豈無不怨不庸，兢兢於當世之網，稱醇固其俗哉？然而誣上行私，把持吏長短，日幸其有事而輕重之者，不可謂無其俗也。甚者陰售其排陷之術，而公倡為讙呼之禍，迫逐而使之去者有矣。有一於
translation_en: … in today's governance, the worry is not that superiors and inferiors fail to delight in one another, but rather that their mutual awe has not yet reached its fullness. Now, what is meant by "superiors" does not necessarily refer only to the ninefold palace of the ruler or the hundred high officials [? 百戾, for 百辟]. From Grand Coordinators who maintain Secretariat-level staffs (kaifu) on down, all who hold even a first-grade commission or serve as heads of a single district of ten square li—whose duty lies in governing the people—may be called superiors. What is meant by "inferiors" does not necessarily refer only to impoverished folk living behindpottery-shard windows and rope-hinged doors. From the common people on up, all the retired gentry of the countryside and the blue-collared students of the schools who submit to the governance of their local magistrates may be called inferiors. Today, among the officials of the empire who shepherd and nourish the common people for the Son of Heaven, how could there not be men who neither insult nor oppress them, who stand in reverent awe above the four classes of people, and who are praised as equal to their offices? And yet, it cannot be said that there are none who are cruel and arbitrary [? 蔬戾, for 暴戾], turning the three-foot bamboo tablets of the law upside down, daily preying upon the people like fish or game and mowing them down like grass. In extreme cases, there are those who above hoodwink the eyes and ears of their surveillance commissioners and intendants, and below gag the mouths and tongues of their people, so that everyone looks on openly yet none dares challenge them. Among the people of the empire who supply taxes and corvée for the state, how could there not be customs that are free of resentment and duplicity [? 不庸], cautiously abiding within the laws of the present age, and praised as pure and steadfast? And yet, it cannot be said that there are no customs of slandering superiors to pursue private ends, holding leverage over officials' faults and merits, and daily hoping for trouble so as to manipulate matters to their own advantage. In extreme cases, there are those who secretly peddle their schemes of exclusion and entrapment, and publicly instigate the calamity of clamorous mobs, pressuring and driving officials into leaving. If even one of …

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
效是一邑之長終不能有其民而無告之
民終不能安其上也夫欲使上之必畏其
在重監司之責乎漢宣帝綜核之政本以
救武帝酷吏之失也大節如嚴延年猶以
酷誅而況其他乎路溫舒之疏可誦已今
誠使監司時以此意提撕而覺察之使夫
殃民者必不容於堯舜之世然後擇其善
者而示以
賜金露冕之寵則庶乎吏務循良而下樂有易
===
事之長矣欲使下之必畏其在重守令之
權乎漢景武游俠之誅本以救惠文法網
之寬也行義如郭解猶以族死而況其下
乎公孫弘之請可思已今誠使守令時以
其權震攝而摧破之使夫犯上者必不容
於堯舜之世然後煦其良者而示以
減租賜復之恩則庶乎民重犯法而上樂有易
使之民矣行之以畫一需之以久道如是
而曰詖道之必不可成古治之必不可復
punctuated: 效，是一邑之長終不能有其民，而無告之民終不能安其上也。夫欲使上之必畏，其在重監司之責乎？漢宣帝綜核之政，本以救武帝酷吏之失也。大節如嚴延年，猶以酷誅，而況其他乎？路溫舒之疏可誦已。今誠使監司時以此意提撕而覺察之，使夫殃民者必不容於堯、舜之世；然後擇其善者，而示以賜金露冕之寵，則庶乎吏務循良，而下樂有易事之長矣。欲使下之必畏，其在重守令之權乎？漢景、武游俠之誅，本以救惠、文法網之寬也。行義如郭解，猶以族死，而況其下乎？公孫弘之請可思已。今誠使守令時以其權震攝而摧破之，使夫犯上者必不容於堯、舜之世；然後煦其良者，而示以減租賜復之恩，則庶乎民重犯法，而上樂有易使之民矣。行之以畫一，需之以久道，如是而曰詖道之必不可成，古治之必不可復，
translation_en: …[this] effect [for "此"?], then the head of a county will ultimately be unable to hold on to his people, and the helpless people will ultimately be unable to rest secure under their superiors. Now if one wishes to ensure that superiors truly feel awe, does it not lie in increasing the responsibility of the Surveillance Officials (jiansi)? Emperor Xuan of Han's policy of comprehensive verification was originally intended to remedy the failings of the harsh officials under Emperor Wu. Even a man of great integrity like Yan Yannian 嚴延年 was executed for cruelty—how much more so the others! The memorial of Lu Wenshu 路溫舒 is well worth reciting. Today, if Surveillance Officials are truly made to constantly remind and inspect with this principle in mind, ensuring that those who bring calamity upon the people are never tolerated in an age of Yao and Shun, and afterward the good among them are selected and shown the favor of bestowing gold and granting ceremonial caps, then perhaps officials will strive to be upright and benevolent, and those below will rejoice in having superiors who are easy to serve. If one wishes to ensure that those below truly feel awe, does it not lie in increasing the authority of the Prefects and Magistrates (shouling)? The execution of wandering knights-errant under Emperors Jing and Wu of Han was originally intended to remedy the laxity of the legal net under Emperors Hui and Wen. Even a man of righteous conduct like Guo Jie 郭解 was executed along with his clan—how much more so those inferior to him! The request of Gongsun Hong 公孫弘 is well worth pondering. Today, if Prefects and Magistrates are truly made to constantly overawe and crush [the unruly] with their authority, ensuring that those who offend against their superiors are never tolerated in an age of Yao and Shun, and afterward the good among them are cherished and shown the grace of reducing land taxes and granting exemptions from corvée, then perhaps the people will be reluctant to violate the law, and superiors will rejoice in having people who are easy to govern. Carry this out with uniformity and wait upon it through long-enduring governance; if it is done like this and yet one says that the Kingly Way [reading 王道 for 詖道?] certainly cannot be accomplished and the governance of antiquity certainly cannot be restored…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
則愚未之信也雖然猶有進於此者億萬
人之心萃而注于
人主之一心而所謂紀綱亦即此心之迹耳故
夫一方之饑祲而
賢主八珍之膳若不下咽匹夫瞋目而扞格
九重之榮衛爲不流通毋恃威於鈇鉞毋藏富
於府庫恭默之思時幾之敕不下
殿陛間而其精已旁皇周浹於蔀屋窮簷之
下矣此又吏治所繇察而民俗所繇成也
===
愚敢以是爲吾
君獻
第五問
涂嘉會
同考試官教諭樊批經生譚時務匪激則紆子
能籌畫機宜揣摩情變仰措諸行事粹然其受福乎
同考試官教諭朱批四議皆江藩所急洞弊切
者猶或難之是作區畫周詳各有成算可以仰副考誠之實矣
考試官教諭趙批指陳時事鑿鑿可行
punctuated:
則愚未之信也。雖然，猶有進於此者。億萬人之心，萃而注于人主之一心，而所謂紀綱，亦即此心之迹耳。故夫一方之饑祲，而賢主八珍之膳若不下咽；匹夫瞋目而扞格，九重之榮衛爲不流通。毋恃威於鈇鉞，毋藏富於府庫，恭默之思、時幾之敕，不下殿陛間，而其精已旁皇周浹於蔀屋窮簷之下矣。此又吏治所繇察，而民俗所繇成也。愚敢以是爲吾君獻。

第五問
涂嘉會
同考試官教諭樊批：經生譚時務，匪激則紆。子能籌畫機宜，揣摩情變，仰措諸行事，粹然其受福乎！
同考試官教諭朱批：四議皆江藩所急，洞弊切者猶或難之。是作區畫周詳，各有成算，可以仰副考誠之實矣。
考試官教諭趙批：指陳時事，鑿鑿可行。
translation_en:
…then I, in my simplicity, would not believe it. Even so, there is something that goes still further than this. The minds of hundreds of millions of people gather and focus upon the single mind of the ruler of men, and what we call laws and discipline are merely the outward traces of this mind. Thus, when a single region suffers famine or calamity, the worthy ruler finds his delicacies of the Eight Treasures hard to swallow; when a single commoner glares in anger and resists, the vital energies of the ninefold palace cease to flow freely. Do not rely on the awe of battle-axes and halberds; do not hoard wealth in treasuries and storehouses. When reverent, silent reflection and timely vigilance at the subtle springs of action take place without even descending the steps of the throne hall, their essence has already ranged far and wide to pervade the humblest thatched cottages below. This, in turn, is whereby the governance of officials is scrutinized and popular customs are formed. In my simplicity, I venture to offer this to my sovereign.

Question Five
Tu Jiahui 涂嘉會
Associate Examiner Fan 樊, Instructor, comments: When scholars of the classics discuss current affairs, if they are not overly strident, they are迂腐 [circuitous and impractical]. You are able to plan for opportune measures and gauge changing circumstances; if held up and put into practice, how purely would blessings be received!
Associate Examiner Zhu 朱, Instructor, comments: All four proposals address urgent needs of the Jiangxi provincial administration; even those who penetrate deeply into abuses find them difficult to resolve. This essay's plans and arrangements are thorough and detailed, each having a well-formed calculation, so that it can respectfully fulfill the substance of examining sincerity [?].
Examiner Zhao 趙, Instructor, comments: It points out and sets forth current affairs in a way that is solidly grounded and practicable.

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭林批識見不羣必留心經濟者
君子之議法也其猶醫者之視疾也以無
疾之人無故而投之藥則汗漫而不中窾
會待其已成而後藥之則疾逃於膏肓而
不可救故善用藥者在於未病病脉之時
而善用法者在於未亂亂法之漸道窮而
後法法久而弊將復生法立而後治治久
而勢將復蠹此正君子用劑之時也後世
稱治安者無若漢文帝而賈生慟哭流涕
===
於其側彼其頌文帝之治者未嘗不甚賈
生之言然而生之言歷三世猶若蓍鑑也
則文帝之治安繇生言也昔者杞人憂積
氣之將墮天下皆咲之扁鵲三見桓侯而
走後世神其術焉今夫譚戰格於櫜弓臥
戈之日而慮盈縮於粟紅貫朽之時外戶
不閉而郊塲之是虞中邦成賦而徭征之
是恤是杞人之類也然而脉微病矣失今
不治後且瘕積衡決故議法者寧為賈生
punctuated:
考試官教諭林批：識見不羣，必留心經濟者。

君子之議法也，其猶醫者之視疾也。以無疾之人，無故而投之藥，則汗漫而不中窾會；待其已成而後藥之，則疾逃於膏肓而不可救。故善用藥者，在於未病病脉之時；而善用法者，在於未亂亂法之漸。道窮而後法，法久而弊將復生；法立而後治，治久而勢將復蠹，此正君子用劑之時也。後世稱治安者無若漢文帝，而賈生慟哭流涕於其側。彼其頌文帝之治者，未嘗不甚賈生之言；然而生之言歷三世猶若蓍鑑也，則文帝之治安繇生言也。昔者杞人憂積氣之將墮，天下皆咲之；扁鵲三見桓侯而走，後世神其術焉。今夫譚戰格於櫜弓臥戈之日，而慮盈縮於粟紅貫朽之時，外戶不閉而郊塲之是虞，中邦成賦而徭征之是恤，是杞人之類也。然而脉微病矣，失今不治，後且瘕積衡決。故議法者寧為賈生…
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Lin comments: "His insight and judgment are extraordinary; he must be someone who pays close attention to statecraft."

When the gentleman deliberates on laws, it is just like a physician examining an illness. If one administers medicine without reason to a person who has no illness, it is aimless and misses the vital points; if one waits until the illness is already fully formed before applying medicine, then the illness flees into the vital region below the heart and cannot be cured. Therefore, he who is skilled at using medicine acts at the moment when the illness is not yet manifest in a diseased pulse; and he who is skilled at using laws acts at the gradual inception when disorder has not yet disrupted the laws. When the Way is exhausted, laws are instituted, and when laws endure for a long time, abuses will arise again; when laws are established, order is achieved, and when order endures for a long time, circumstances will decay again—this is precisely the time for the gentleman to apply his prescription.

In later ages, none was more praised for peace and order than Emperor Wen of Han (r. 180–157 BCE), yet Master Jia [Jia Yi 賈誼] wept bitterly and shed tears by his side. Those who extolled the rule of Emperor Wen never failed to consider Master Jia's words excessive; yet Master Jia's words remained like divining stalks and a mirror across three generations, so the peace and order under Emperor Wen actually derived from the Master's words. In antiquity, the man of Qi worried that the massed ether of the heavens was about to fall, and everyone in the world laughed at him; Bian Que 扁鵲 saw Marquis Huan three times and fled, and later generations revered his art as divine. Now, to speak of battle arrays in days when bows are cased and halberds laid down, to worry over surpluses and deficits in times when grain rots in the granaries and strings of cash decay in the vaults, to fret over the frontier defenses when outer doors do not need to be bolted, or to be anxious about corvée and exactions when revenues are regularly fixed in the central realm—this is akin to the man of Qi. Yet the pulse shows a faint illness; if we fail to treat it now, later it will form chronic obstructions and burst forth out of control. Therefore, he who deliberates on laws would rather utter Master Jia's…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
之過言而不願爲越人之術以自神也江
右非無事之國也地儉而寡於入民貧而
騖於利境錯於四壤而多隱伏之姦博徒
游客三五於都市椎埋鼓鑄之輩潛伏於
深山大澤有司小不當其意輒羣起而譟
呼盜賊直須時耳比歲數稔國無大興作
取辦於民猶尚鰓鰓可畏如此設不幸有
旱潦饑饉之菑胡以待之幸賴
聖天子在上剔弊源振積弛赫然下考成之
===
令月課歲程諸司惴慄奉職不敢後譬之於
人豢養偷惰之軀筋駑肉緩一旦而整齊
訓飭之振袖策步而精彩已燁然見矣式
遏斯舉鳴吠晏然潯陽彭蠡之間商舶宵
濟豈非所謂治安之券歟而執事者猶欲
引繩批根以副
聖天子綜核之實意甚盛心也江右一時事寧
復有大於兵事財用之當備乎屯守賦役
之當議乎以一身視之屯守身之郛廓也
punctuated: 之過言，而不願爲越人之術以自神也。江右非無事之國也。地儉而寡於入，民貧而騖於利，境錯於四壤而多隱伏之姦。博徒游客，三五於都市；椎埋鼓鑄之輩，潛伏於深山大澤。有司小不當其意，輒羣起而譟呼，盜賊直須時耳。比歲數稔，國無大興作，取辦於民，猶尚鰓鰓可畏如此；設不幸有旱潦饑饉之菑，胡以待之？幸賴聖天子在上，剔弊源，振積弛，赫然下考成之令，月課歲程，諸司惴慄奉職不敢後。譬之於人，豢養偷惰之軀，筋駑肉緩，一旦而整齊訓飭之，振袖策步，而精彩已燁然見矣。式遏斯舉，鳴吠晏然，潯陽、彭蠡之間，商舶宵濟，豈非所謂治安之券歟？而執事者猶欲引繩批根，以副聖天子綜核之實意，甚盛心也。江右一時事，寧復有大於兵事、財用之當備乎？屯守、賦役之當議乎？以一身視之，屯守，身之郛廓也；
translation_en: …exaggerated warnings of Master Jia (賈生), rather than wishing to practice the art of the man of Yue [Bian Que 扁鵲] just to make oneself appear miraculous. Jiangxi (江右) is no trouble-free province. Its land is barren and yields scanty revenue; its people are impoverished and scramble after profit; its borders interlock with neighboring regions on all four sides and harbor many hidden miscreants. Gamblers and wandering idlers gather in threes and fives in the cities and markets; grave-robbers, murderers, and illicit coiners lurk in deep mountains and vast marshes. If the local authorities displease them even slightly, they immediately rise up in crowds and clamor; banditry awaits only the right moment to break out. In recent years there have been several good harvests, and the state has undertaken no great public works drawing upon the people, yet the situation remains so precariously fearful. If, unfortunately, disasters of drought, flood, and famine were to occur, how could we cope with them? Fortunately, we rely on the Sacred Son of Heaven above, who roots out the sources of abuse, revives long-standing laxity, and has majestically issued the order for the Evaluation of Achievements (考成), assessing performance monthly and setting annual quotas, so that all officials tremble in awe and attend to their duties without daring to lag behind. Compare this to a person whose pampered and indolent body has slack sinews and flabby flesh: once he is disciplined and drilled, he shakes out his sleeves and strides forward, and his vigor already shines forth brilliantly. With measures of suppression thus enacted, the realm is so peaceful that dogs and cocks are heard in tranquility, and between Xunyang (潯陽) and Lake Pengli (彭蠡) merchant vessels cross even at night—is this not what is called a guarantee of peace and order? Yet Your Excellency still wishes to apply the plumb-line and strike at the roots in order to fulfill the Sacred Son of Heaven's earnest intention of comprehensive verification; this is a most noble aspiration. Among the pressing affairs of Jiangxi today, could there be anything greater than the need to prepare for military affairs and fiscal resources? Or the need to deliberate upon garrison defense and taxation and corvée labor? Viewed in terms of a single human body, garrison defense is the outer wall of the body;…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
財用身之腸胃也而賦役者養身之梁肉
也兵事者治身之鍼砭也郭廓欲强腸胃
欲實梁肉藉其滋養鍼砭賴其辟除舍是
而語攝生妄矣江右故無兵頃寇發虔南
則調兵柯氏再發盱江則募兵浙省柯氏
應而跋扈之漸啓浙兵應而驛騷之累滋
邇乃稍稍廢置更募土兵則有分營掎角
之設不可謂無兵矣顧衞所之額戍日朘
削於武弁之誅求部帥按空籍而召漕輓
===
勢且不給安望其蹶張超距也其募在民
間者常兵名為兵而實以供郡縣之郵使
精兵名為精而實無以異於市井之游手
是不遇敵聞鉦鼓即色變而走耳保甲之
法雖行暮夜嘯呼閉戶無應者卒遇大敵
而以驅之赴湯火得乎如是而武備曰脩
未也食足而後可以養兵府庫充倉廩實
而後可以當緩急今之時非甚絀也歲登
二熟餘糧棲畝而撫填諸使又力宣
punctuated: 財用，身之腸胃也；而賦役者，養身之梁肉也；兵事者，治身之鍼砭也。郭廓欲强，腸胃欲實，梁肉藉其滋養，鍼砭賴其辟除，舍是而語攝生，妄矣。江右故無兵。頃寇發虔南，則調兵柯氏；再發盱江，則募兵浙省。柯氏應，而跋扈之漸啓；浙兵應，而驛騷之累滋。邇乃稍稍廢置，更募土兵，則有分營掎角之設，不可謂無兵矣。顧衞所之額戍，日朘削於武弁之誅求；部帥按空籍而召，漕輓勢且不給，安望其蹶張超距也？其募在民間者，常兵名為兵，而實以供郡縣之郵使；精兵名為精，而實無以異於市井之游手。是不遇敵，聞鉦鼓即色變而走耳。保甲之法雖行，暮夜嘯呼，閉戶無應者；卒遇大敵，而以驅之赴湯火，得乎？如是而武備曰脩，未也。食足而後可以養兵，府庫充、倉廩實而後可以當緩急。今之時，非甚絀也。歲登二熟，餘糧棲畝，而撫填諸使又力宣
translation_en: … fiscal resources are the body's bowels and stomach; taxes and corvée are the fine grain and meat that nourish the body; and military affairs are the acupuncture needles and stone probes that cure the body. The outer walls must be strong, the bowels and stomach must be full, fine grain and meat are relied upon for nourishment, and needles and stone probes are depended upon to expel ailments—to speak of preserving life while setting these aside is absurd. Jiangxi originally had no troops of its own. Recently, when bandits erupted in southern Ganzhou (Qiannan 虔南), troops were mobilized from the Ke 柯 clan; when they erupted again along the Xu River (Xujiang 盱江), soldiers were recruited from Zhejiang province. When the Ke clan responded, the beginnings of recalcitrance were opened; when the Zhejiang soldiers responded, the burden of agitation along the postal routes grew worse. Lately, these have been gradually discontinued and replaced by recruiting local militia, establishing divided camps for mutual support like horns and legs—so it cannot be said that there are no troops. Yet the quota of garrison guards is daily pared away by the extortions of military officers; when unit commanders call them up from empty registers, there are not even enough of them to manage the grain transport—how could one hope for them to draw heavy crossbows with their feet and leap over obstacles? As for those recruited from among the people: the regular troops are soldiers in name, but in reality they merely serve as couriers for the prefectures and counties; the elite troops are elite in name, but in reality they are no different from idle loafers in the marketplaces. Even without encountering the enemy, at the mere sound of gongs and drums they change color and flee! Although the mutual-security (baojia 保甲) system is in place, when alarms are shouted in the night, people bar their doors and no one responds; if they suddenly encounter a formidable enemy, can one drive them into boiling water and fire? Under such circumstances, to say that military preparedness is in good order—not yet! Only when food is sufficient can troops be maintained, and only when the treasuries are full and the granaries well stocked can emergencies be met. The present time is not one of extreme scarcity. Two harvests are gathered each year, surplus grain rests in the fields, and the Grand Coordinators and various commissioners vigorously proclaim…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
德意而節縮之是宜以財力雄諸郡國奈之何
其猶枵然待餔之腹也累歲之儲括於先
年之指使贖鍰之積罄於每歲之濟邊語
公儲則豪右之隱沒者駕言於逋負語京
輸則大猾之侵牟者株累於平民常平義
倉之設秪以滋出納之弊而嗷嗷者未實
沾也蠲貸減編之惠或以入墨吏之囊而
嗤嗤者未盡知也宗祿歲逋而月掛有司
東拄而西搘甚者籌十金之費袖手相視
===
而莫之措如是而尚可謂財用之裕乎江
右之地四接於閩廣蘄黃衢歙諸郡包以
崇山聯以長江浸以巨匯此亦天險之國
也而藩籬未固堂奧素虛如姚源之變飄
忽而至衢信宸濠之發瞋目而越九江足
爲往事之鏡已比者寧州盜作上厪
聖衷駐官設備而後厎定夫寧州發而後成備
也其爲未發之寧州者非一所也大都層
巘疊壘我常得與姦人共之我能守則險
punctuated:
德意而節縮之，是宜以財力雄諸郡國，奈之何其猶枵然待餔之腹也？累歲之儲，括於先年之指使；贖鍰之積，罄於每歲之濟邊。語公儲，則豪右之隱沒者，駕言於逋負；語京輸，則大猾之侵牟者，株累於平民。常平、義倉之設，秪以滋出納之弊，而嗷嗷者未實沾也；蠲貸、減編之惠，或以入墨吏之囊，而嗤嗤者未盡知也。宗祿歲逋而月掛，有司東拄而西搘，甚者籌十金之費，袖手相視而莫之措。如是，而尚可謂財用之裕乎？
江右之地，四接於閩、廣、蘄、黃、衢、歙諸郡，包以崇山，聯以長江，浸以巨匯，此亦天險之國也。而藩籬未固，堂奧素虛。如姚源之變，飄忽而至衢、信；宸濠之發，瞋目而越九江，足爲往事之鏡已。比者寧州盜作，上厪聖衷，駐官設備而後厎定。夫寧州發而後成備也，其爲未發之寧州者，非一所也。大都層巘疊壘，我常得與姦人共之。我能守，則險…
translation_en:
…His Majesty's benevolent intentions and economize; thus, this province ought to surpass other commanderies and principalities in financial strength. Why is it, then, that it remains like an empty stomach waiting to be fed? The reserves accumulated over many years were swept away at the direction of authorities in previous years; the savings from redemption fines are exhausted by the annual transfers to aid the frontier. When we speak of public reserves, powerful families who secretly embezzle them shift the blame onto tax arrears; when we speak of shipments to the capital, great scoundrels who profiteer from them implicate the common people to cover the shortfalls. The establishment of Ever-Normal and Charitable Granaries serves only to breed abuses in collection and disbursement, while the crying, starving masses receive no real benefit; the mercies of tax remissions, relief loans, and reduced assessments sometimes go straight into the pockets of corrupt clerks, while the simple, ignorant folk are not even fully aware of them. The stipends for imperial clansmen fall into arrears year after year and remain unpaid month after month. The local authorities prop things up in the east only to have them give way in the west; in extreme cases, when trying to raise an expenditure of ten taels of silver, they stand with their hands in their sleeves looking at one another, unable to find a way to provide it. Under such circumstances, how can our financial resources still be called abundant?

The territory of Jiangxi borders on the various prefectures of Fujian, Guangdong, Qizhou, Huangzhou, Quzhou, and Shexian on all four sides. Encompassed by lofty mountains, linked by the Yangtze River, and watered by the great confluence of Poyang Lake, this too is a land of natural strategic barriers. Yet its outer defenses are not secure, and its inner heartland has long been hollow. For instance, during the rebellion at Yaoyuan, the rebels swept like a whirlwind all the way to Quzhou and Guangxin; when Zhu Chenhao rose in revolt, in the blink of an eye he crossed beyond Jiujiang—these suffice to serve as a mirror of past events. Recently, bandits arose in Ningzhou, causing concern to His Majesty's sacred heart; only after officials were stationed there and defenses established was the region finally pacified. Now, defenses were only completed in Ningzhou after the outbreak occurred; yet the places that are like Ningzhou before its outbreak are by no means just one! For the most part, thetiered peaks and overlapping mountain fastnesses are terrain that we must constantly share with wicked men. If we are able to defend them, then the strategic strongholds…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
爲我有而盜不能窺我不能守則險爲盜
有而我不能奪今之形勢雖壯有如一旦
有萑苻之雄乘危而據迅突而來有能扼
其吭而拊其背乎愚以爲封守未可言固
也賦役之有條編也自江右始也其法計
口受庸緣畝定直悉籍其一歲之費而輸
之於官官爲召募民無擾焉朝而輸金暮
而安臥江右之人安之以爲良法久矣顧
其始之議法也十三郡之輕重苦樂已抱
===
不均之歎而好名者又取成額而日裁之
於是乎費益繁而用愈不給則有那借有
預徵那借而官困矣預徵而民困矣逮夫
法行之久民不見德而惟上誅求之怨甚
者飛詭以亂籍匿產以逃租上戶高枕而
素封窮丁箠楚而莫措則差銀之入日削
而募役枵腹于公庭有司坐困而莫可誰
何矣形見勢屈官且不能使其民卽以謂
賦役之平可乎夫是四者
punctuated:
爲我有，而盜不能窺；我不能守，則險爲盜有，而我不能奪。今之形勢雖壯，有如一旦有萑苻之雄，乘危而據，迅突而來，有能扼其吭而拊其背乎？愚以爲封守未可言固也。

賦役之有條編也，自江右始也。其法計口受庸，緣畝定直，悉籍其一歲之費而輸之於官，官爲召募，民無擾焉。朝而輸金，暮而安臥，江右之人安之，以爲良法久矣。顧其始之議法也，十三郡之輕重苦樂，已抱不均之歎；而好名者又取成額而日裁之，於是乎費益繁而用愈不給，則有那借，有預徵。那借而官困矣，預徵而民困矣。逮夫法行之久，民不見德，而惟上誅求之怨。甚者飛詭以亂籍，匿產以逃租；上戶高枕而素封，窮丁箠楚而莫措。則差銀之入日削，而募役枵腹于公庭，有司坐困而莫可誰何矣。形見勢屈，官且不能使其民，卽以謂賦役之平，可乎？夫是四者，
translation_en:
… belong to us, and bandits cannot spy upon them; if we are unable to defend them, then those strategic passes will belong to the bandits, and we will not be able to wrest them back. Although the present topography is formidable, suppose one day a chieftain from the reed marshes takes advantage of a precarious moment to seize a stronghold and charges forth swiftly—is there anyone capable of gripping him by the throat and striking him on the back? In my humble opinion, our border defenses cannot yet be called secure.

The Single Whip method (tiaobian) of taxation and corvée labor originated in Jiangxi (Jiangyou). Under this system, labor service is assessed by counting heads and payments are fixed according to acreage; all the expenses for an entire year are registered and paid over to the officials, who then hire laborers on the people's behalf, leaving the populace undisturbed. Paying silver in the morning and sleeping peacefully by evening, the people of Jiangxi have been content with it and have long regarded it as a fine method. Yet when the law was first deliberated, the thirteen prefectures already harbored sighs of inequality over the relative weight and hardship or ease of their burdens. Moreover, those fond of a reputation for frugality took the established quotas and curtailed them day by day. Consequently, as expenses grew ever more numerous and funds increasingly insufficient, there arose the practices of misappropriating funds from other accounts and collecting taxes in advance. With misappropriation, the officials are distressed; with advance collection, the people are distressed. Once the system had been in operation for a long time, the people no longer saw its benevolence, feeling only resentment toward their superiors' exactions. In extreme cases, they use flying transfers and fraudulent registrations to throw the tax registers into confusion, or conceal property to evade land taxes; upper-tier households rest on high pillows in untaxed wealth, while poor adult males are flogged and have nowhere to turn. Thus the income from corvée silver dwindles daily, hired laborers go with empty bellies in the public courts, and the local authorities sit helplessly in distress, unable to do anything about it. When flaws are exposed and authority is exhausted, officials cannot even command their own people—how then can one say that taxation and corvée are equitable? Now, as for these four matters, …

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖天子所以責成於下而百執事所以告成于
吾
君以爲如是足矣而積弊之當究乃更有隱然
可憂而未可卽安者是故兵銷而言戎器
之除易曉也粒絶而議饘粥之給易明也
羊亡而補牢計易行也絃絶而更調說易
入也惟夫人以爲治而中抱不可測之憂
法以爲良而中涵不可繼之實則譚者見
謂迂狂而聽者每忽而難入此良醫所爲
===
苦心於察微而策士所爲先事而太息也
管敬仲以區區瀕海之齊作內政以寓軍
令使其民夜戰聲相聞晝戰目相見而桓
公遂以覇天下今之江北非必盡弱於齊
也愚以爲官軍隱占之罰
令甲最嚴倘可按籍而覈數乎丁戶清勾之
苦遠涉異國倘可就近而充籍乎毋曰有
精兵之名也分曹角射誰以五兵將程其
能而實敎之陣乎毋曰有保甲之名也比
punctuated:
聖天子所以責成於下，而百執事所以告成于吾君，以爲如是足矣；而積弊之當究，乃更有隱然可憂而未可卽安者。是故兵銷而言戎器之除，易曉也；粒絶而議饘粥之給，易明也；羊亡而補牢，計易行也；絃絶而更調，說易入也。惟夫人以爲治，而中抱不可測之憂；法以爲良，而中涵不可繼之實，則譚者見謂迂狂，而聽者每忽而難入。此良醫所爲苦心於察微，而策士所爲先事而太息也。
管敬仲以區區瀕海之齊，作內政以寓軍令，使其民夜戰聲相聞，晝戰目相見，而桓公遂以覇天下。今之江北，非必盡弱於齊也。愚以爲官軍隱占之罰，令甲最嚴，倘可按籍而覈數乎？丁戶清勾之苦，遠涉異國，倘可就近而充籍乎？毋曰有精兵之名也，分曹角射，誰以五兵將，程其能而實敎之陣乎？毋曰有保甲之名也，比
translation_en:
… are what the Sacred Son of Heaven requires to be accomplished by his subordinates, and what the hundred officials report as accomplished to our Sovereign, thinking that doing thus is sufficient; yet among the accumulated abuses that ought to be investigated, there are still more that are secretly worrisome and do not allow one to rest easy right away. Therefore, when troops are disbanded, speaking of the readiness of weapons is easy to understand; when grain runs out, discussing the provision of gruel and porridge is easy to make clear; when the sheep is lost, the plan to mend the fold is easy to carry out; when the string snaps, the advice to restring and retune the instrument is easy to accept. Only when people consider things to be well-governed while inside there lurk unfathomable worries, or consider the laws to be sound while inside they harbor the reality of being unsustainable—then those who speak of it are regarded as impractical and mad, and those who listen routinely ignore it and find it hard to accept. This is why a skilled physician takes pains to observe the subtle signs, and why a strategist sighs deeply before events unfold.

Guan Jingzhong [Guan Zhong 管仲], with the mere coastal state of Qi, instituted domestic administration so as to embed military command within it, making its people hear one another's voices when fighting at night and see one another's eyes when fighting by day, and Duke Huan 桓公 thereby became hegemon over the realm. Today's Jiangbei [or Jiangxi] is not necessarily altogether weaker than Qi. In my humble opinion, the punishment for the covert private employment of government troops is most severe in the statutory codes; could we not examine the registers and verify their actual numbers? As for the hardship of clearing and drafting military-service households, which forces men to travel far to distant provinces, could we not allow them to fill the ranks in nearby garrisons instead? Do not say that we have the name of "elite troops": when dividing them into squads to compete in archery, who leads them with the five weapons, tests their abilities, and truly instructs them in battle formations? Do not say that we have the name of "mutual security (baojia 保甲)": when five-household groups (bi)…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
間族黨聯屬以時督課之實而守望相助
乎聯鄉兵千落於各郡以防小盜而萃精
兵二千於中權以防大寇若是何殊於內
政之作也鼂錯論積貯於恭儉之朝其言
堯湯之水旱國無捐瘠者歸於蓄積之多
愚以爲郡邑
京師之外府也今太倉之粟陳陳相因泉流
鏹積而獨使外府空虛非計也正供之入
不敢望番田租之賜不敢望半若九江贛
===
州之稅與贖鍰之例進者不可力請而留
乎倉穀累積非侵歲不發腐之是弃有用
之物於地而繩之則坐無罪之人於法曷
若以新易陳以銀代粟而相兼以待用乎
姦胥大猾聽其盜用鉅萬而不之覺是有
司之過計也業已發之亟正其誅沒入其
產而毋縱其攀染以累良民可乎積逋之
盡
赦驛傳之免編
punctuated:
間族黨聯屬，以時督課之實，而守望相助乎？聯鄉兵千落於各郡以防小盜，而萃精兵二千於中權以防大寇，若是，何殊於內政之作也？

鼂錯論積貯於恭儉之朝，其言堯、湯之水旱，國無捐瘠者，歸於蓄積之多。愚以爲郡邑，京師之外府也。今太倉之粟，陳陳相因，泉流鏹積，而獨使外府空虛，非計也。正供之入，不敢望番，田租之賜，不敢望半，若九江、贛州之稅，與贖鍰之例進者，不可力請而留乎？倉穀累積，非侵歲不發。腐之，是弃有用之物於地；而繩之，則坐無罪之人於法。曷若以新易陳，以銀代粟，而相兼以待用乎？姦胥大猾，聽其盜用鉅萬而不之覺，是有司之過計也。業已發之，亟正其誅，沒入其產，而毋縱其攀染以累良民，可乎？積逋之盡赦，驛傳之免編，
translation_en:
…link the five-family groups, twenty-five-family neighborhoods, hundred-family clans, and five-hundred-family communities together, supervising and assessing them in earnest at regular intervals so that they assist one another in keeping watch and defending themselves? If we organize local militia across thousands of settlements in each prefecture to guard against petty bandits, while concentrating two thousand elite troops at the central command to guard against major marauders—doing so, how would this differ from [Guan Zhong's] institution of internal administration?

Chao Cuo 鼂錯 discussed accumulating grain reserves during a reverent and frugal reign, stating that during the floods and droughts of Yao 堯 and Tang 湯, the reason the state had no one abandoned or starving was due to the abundance of stored reserves. I humbly consider the prefectures and counties to be the outer treasuries of the Capital. Today, the grain in the Grand Granary piles up layer upon old layer, and strings of cash flow in and accumulate, yet to leave the outer treasuries alone empty is poor planning. As for the regular tax revenues, we dare not hope for their remission [?]; as for the bestowal of land-tax exemptions, we dare not hope for a half-reduction. Yet when it comes to the commercial taxes of Jiujiang 九江 and Ganzhou 贛州, as well as the redemption fees that are routinely forwarded to the court, could we not earnestly petition to retain them locally? Granary grain accumulates over time and is not disbursed except in years of famine. To let it rot is to cast useful goods upon the ground; yet to prosecute thegranary keepers according to the law is to convict innocent people of crimes. Why not exchange the old grain for new, substitute silver for grain, and combine both methods in readiness for use? As for corrupt clerks and great scoundrels, allowing them to embezzle tens of thousands without noticing is the oversight of the local authorities. Once their crimes have been exposed, would it not be proper to swiftly execute their punishment and confiscate their property, while refusing to let them falsely implicate and burden good citizens? The complete pardoning of accumulated tax arrears and the exemption from postal-relay service assessments…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
上恩至渥也而間有復徵此何為者也今使未
徵者亟歸之民而已輸者悉入之公官帑
實而民沾實惠可乎他如復水利於陂塘
脩義倉於鄉社國有九年之蓄而下有不
涸之倉庶幾哉富於貯積之議矣宋華徵
之議曰屯守之地當其衝要則一人可以
敵萬非其衝要則萬夫不足以敵一今之
衝要自寧州而外可議者猶多也九江據
金陵上游湖口為鄱湖綰轂厥險在澤關
===
津之當警者也其更添舟師而耀之武乎
玉山為入浙之衝鉛山當入閩之扼厥險
在陸門戶之當嚴者也亦甞飭亭鄣以示
之限乎長寧界萬山之中反側子初定設
狼心未息一縣令能制其命乎是不可不
加之備也婺源與楚接壤亡命者多竄匿
其中戍守稍不慎不復蹈寧州之轍乎是
不可不預之防也謹斥堠明信地繕雉堞
布干掫是泰山而四維之也華氏之議有
punctuated:
上恩至渥也，而間有復徵，此何為者也？今使未徵者亟歸之民，而已輸者悉入之公，官帑實而民沾實惠，可乎？他如復水利於陂塘，脩義倉於鄉社，國有九年之蓄，而下有不涸之倉，庶幾哉富於貯積之議矣。

宋華徵之議曰：「屯守之地，當其衝要，則一人可以敵萬；非其衝要，則萬夫不足以敵一。」今之衝要，自寧州而外，可議者猶多也。九江據金陵上游，湖口為鄱湖綰轂，厥險在澤，關津之當警者也，其更添舟師而耀之武乎？玉山為入浙之衝，鉛山當入閩之扼，厥險在陸，門戶之當嚴者也，亦甞飭亭鄣以示之限乎？長寧界萬山之中，反側子初定，設狼心未息，一縣令能制其命乎？是不可不加之備也。婺源與楚接壤，亡命者多竄匿其中，戍守稍不慎，不復蹈寧州之轍乎？是不可不預之防也。謹斥堠，明信地，繕雉堞，布干掫，是泰山而四維之也，華氏之議有
translation_en:
… represents the most generous grace from His Majesty; yet in some cases taxes are being levied again—what is the reason for this? Now, if we promptly return what has not yet been levied to the people, while bringing all that has already been paid into the public treasury, so that the official coffers are filled and the people receive real benefit, would that be feasible? As for other measures, such as restoring waterworks in reservoirs and ponds, and repairing charitable granaries in rural communities, so that the state has nine years of reserves and the people below have inexhaustible granaries—this would come close indeed to a proposal for enriching our stores!

In the Song dynasty, Hua Zheng’s (華徵) discourse stated: "Where garrisoned defenses occupy a strategic chokepoint, one man can hold off ten thousand; where they do not occupy a strategic chokepoint, ten thousand men are not enough to hold off one." Among today’s strategic points, aside from Ningzhou (寧州), there are still many worth discussing. Jiujiang (九江) commands the upper reaches above Jinling (金陵), and Hukou (湖口) serves as the hub of Lake Poyang (鄱湖); their natural defenses lie in the waters, making them passes and fords where vigilance is required. Should we add more naval forces there to display our military might? Yushan (玉山) is the thoroughfare into Zhejiang, and Yanshan (鉛山) guards the pass into Fujian; their natural defenses lie on land, making them gateways that must be strictly secured. Have we also put the frontier posts and barriers in order to mark clear boundaries? Changning (長寧) is bordered by myriad mountains, where rebellious elements have only recently been pacified; suppose their wolfish ambitions have not yet ceased—can a single District Magistrate control their fate? Here it is imperative to increase preparedness. Wuyuan (婺源) [?] borders Chu (楚, Huguang), and fugitives often flee and hide within it; if the garrison guard is even slightly careless, will we not follow once again in the tracks of Ningzhou? Here it is imperative to take precautions in advance. To maintain vigilant lookout beacons, clearly define assigned defense sectors, repair battlements, and deploy night patrols—this is to make the realm as stable as Mount Tai supported at all four corners. Master Hua’s proposal has …

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
徵已蘇軾氏之議賦役曰戶無常賦視地
以為賦人無常役視賦以為役故其在元
祐時常欲兼顧募衙前而用之今之議法
非有改于條編之舊也郡縣之賦不齊而
偏累者重困業不能不取之民夫亦總十
三郡而酌劑之使得其平乎戶田之弊不
一而飛詭為最甚即不能一一丈量之能
所在為一清查而使疲民蒙福乎與其掣
襟露肘而為不終日之計曷若明增其所
===
未備以免於那借預徵之弊此不為可行
而可繼乎與其顰首蹙額而忍視此嗷嗷
之役曷若半輸銀於官半徵役於力此不
為兩用而兩利乎凡吾所為議以救其窮
而使之行非絀其辭而別為議即子瞻復
生不易吾言矣是在古人為已試之方而
在今時為對病之藥執事者倘不迂書生
言而條舉次第行之實務應聲而毋以彌
文塞責言可底績而毋以持久怠成庶
punctuated: 徵已。蘇軾氏之議賦役曰：「戶無常賦，視地以為賦；人無常役，視賦以為役。」故其在元祐時，常欲兼顧募、衙前而用之。今之議法，非有改于條編之舊也。郡縣之賦不齊，而偏累者重困，業不能不取之民，夫亦總十三郡而酌劑之，使得其平乎？戶田之弊不一，而飛詭為最甚，即不能一一丈量之，能所在為一清查，而使疲民蒙福乎？與其掣襟露肘而為不終日之計，曷若明增其所未備，以免於那借、預徵之弊，此不為可行而可繼乎？與其顰首蹙額而忍視此嗷嗷之役，曷若半輸銀於官，半徵役於力，此不為兩用而兩利乎？凡吾所為議以救其窮而使之行，非絀其辭而別為議，即子瞻復生，不易吾言矣。是在古人為已試之方，而在今時為對病之藥。執事者倘不迂書生言，而條舉次第行之，實務應聲而毋以彌文塞責，言可底績而毋以持久怠成，庶
translation_en: …has been verified. When Master Su Shi 蘇軾 discussed taxes and corvée labor, he said: "Households have no fixed tax; tax is assessed according to their land. People have no fixed labor service; labor service is assessed according to their tax." Therefore, during the Yuanyou 元祐 era, he always wanted to combine hired service and the courthouse service (yaqian 衙前) and employ them together. Today's deliberations on the law do not seek to alter the established Single-Whip (tiaobian 條編) system. The tax burdens across prefectures and counties are uneven, and those disproportionately burdened suffer severely. Since resources must inevitably be drawn from the people, could we not take the thirteen prefectures as a whole and adjust the allocations among them so as to achieve equity? The abuses in household and land registration are manifold, with fraudulent transfer and false registration (feigui 飛詭) being the worst. Even if we cannot resurvey every single plot, can we not conduct a thorough audit in each locality so that the exhausted populace may enjoy relief? Rather than pulling one's lapel only to expose the elbow—resorting to stopgap measures that cannot last a single day—why not openly augment what is insufficiently provided for, thereby avoiding the abuses of misappropriation and advance collection? Would this not be both practicable and sustainable? Rather than furrowing one's brow and hardening one's heart to watch these wailing laborers, why not have half paid in silver to the authorities and half levied in physical labor? Would this not employ both methods to the benefit of both sides? All that I propose is meant to remedy the system's exhaustion and make it workable, not to reject the existing terms and invent a separate doctrine; even if Zizhan 子瞻 (Su Shi) were to live again, he would not change my words. Among the ancients, these were already proven prescriptions, and in our own time, they are medicines suited to the illness. If you, sir, do not dismiss a scholar's words as impractical, but set them forth item by item and put them into effect in order—responding with genuine effort rather than shirking responsibility through empty formalities, and bringing words to actual fruition rather than growing lax as time wears on—then perhaps…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
朝廷之
德意日宣而考成之實政斯在矣雖然此猶其
末也一人之身所恃以久植而不仆者非
在元氣乎所恃以日運而不息者非在血
脉乎今之所謂考成譬猶神氣之振刷耳
若元氣內損而不固血脉內壅而不周乃
欲於精爽動盪之間求其燁而不槁亦已
難矣孔子曰君子學道則愛人小人學道
則易使也今江右之民多糊其口於四方
===
而懵于上下之分特異中州要之其本不
植而其情不相攝矣如欲使元氣之固其
必也綏之以養如欲使血脉之周其必也
漸之以敎此非可以歲月致也是在
聖天子所作新於上而百執事所奉行於下何
如耳斯意也卽紀綱法度猶不能與而況
於簿書期會之間乎賈生曰醫能治之而
上不使愚非其人也敢因執事之問而竭
所聞以對
punctuated: 朝廷之德意日宣，而考成之實政斯在矣。雖然，此猶其末也。一人之身，所恃以久植而不仆者，非在元氣乎？所恃以日運而不息者，非在血脉乎？今之所謂考成，譬猶神氣之振刷耳。若元氣內損而不固，血脉內壅而不周，乃欲於精爽動盪之間，求其燁而不槁，亦已難矣。孔子曰：「君子學道則愛人，小人學道則易使也。」今江右之民，多糊其口於四方，而懵于上下之分，特異中州。要之，其本不植，而其情不相攝矣。如欲使元氣之固，其必也綏之以養；如欲使血脉之周，其必也漸之以敎。此非可以歲月致也，是在聖天子所作新於上，而百執事所奉行於下何如耳。斯意也，卽紀綱法度猶不能與，而況於簿書期會之間乎？賈生曰：「醫能治之，而上不使。」愚非其人也，敢因執事之問，而竭所聞以對。
translation_en: … the benevolent intentions of the Court will be proclaimed daily, and the substantive governance of performance evaluation (kaocheng 考成) will reside right here. Even so, these are still only the secondary branches. In a single person's body, does not that upon which it relies to stand long without falling lie in its primordial vitality (yuanqi 元氣)? Does not that upon which it relies to circulate daily without ceasing lie in its blood and vessels? What is today called performance evaluation is comparable merely to rousing and brushing up the spirit. If the primordial vitality is damaged within and not secure, and the blood and vessels are obstructed within and do not circulate throughout, then trying amidst the agitation of the vital spirit to seek that it remain radiant and not wither away is already difficult indeed. Confucius said: "When the superior man learns the Way, he loves others; when the petty man learns the Way, he is easy to employ." Today the people of Jiangxi (Jiangyou 江右) mostly eke out a living in the four quarters, and are ignorant of the distinctions between superior and inferior, differing markedly from the Central Plains. In sum, their root is not planted, and their sentiments are not mutually bound together. If one wishes to make the primordial vitality secure, one must pacify them through nourishment; if one wishes to make the blood and vessels circulate throughout, one must imbue them gradually through instruction. This is not something that can be achieved in mere months and years; it depends simply on how the Sacred Son of Heaven brings about renewal above, and how all the officials carry it out below. Even overarching laws and institutions cannot partake of this meaning, how much less the realm of administrative registers and scheduled deadlines! Master Jia [Jia Yi 賈誼] said: "The physician is able to cure it, yet the ruler does not employ him." Stupid as I am, I am not that man, yet I venture on the basis of Your Excellency's question to exhaust what I have heard in reply.

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
我
皇上紀元之七禩歲在己卯亶安
之辰教諭成孚實應御史聘
主江西試入其疆而覩田畯
饁婦之至喜蓋黍苗芃芃如
也入其國而覩都人士之盛
===
衣冠楚如也始入簾而御史
董百執事懲毖以聽則內外
斬如已閱諸士所為文多矯
矯國香餘膏剩馥至不可盡
收拾而拔其尤者九十五人
以
獻則所謂楚材翹翹者也於戲
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

我皇上紀元之七禩，歲在己卯，亶安之辰，教諭成孚實應御史聘，主江西試。入其疆，而覩田畯、饁婦之至喜，蓋黍苗芃芃如也；入其國，而覩都人士之盛，衣冠楚如也。始入簾，而御史董百執事懲毖以聽，則內外斬如。已，閱諸士所為文，多矯矯國香，餘膏剩馥，至不可盡收拾，而拔其尤者九十五人以獻，則所謂楚材翹翹者也。於戲！
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the seventh year of Our August Emperor's reign, the cyclical year jimao (1579), at the time of the autumn examination, I, Instructor Cheng Fu 成孚, in fact responded to the invitation of the Censor to preside over the Jiangxi examination. Entering its borders, I witnessed the great joy of the farm supervisors and the women bringing food to the fields, for the millet shoots were luxuriant indeed; entering its capital, I witnessed the flourishing of the gentlemen of the metropolis, their robes and caps neat and splendid indeed. When I first entered behind the curtain, the Censor directed all the officiating functionaries to attend to their duties with caution and care, so that both inside and outside were strictly ordered. Thereafter, examining the essays composed by the scholars, many were outstanding "national fragrances" (guoxiang), with such lingering richness and surplus aroma that they could not all be gathered in; and we selected the finest among them, ninety-five men, to present to the throne—truly what may be called the towering talents of Chu! Alas! …

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
胡此都人士之盛歟天下中
原之地敝於四爭而其餘皆
以海墺荒陬為徼獨此地沃
壤四包而衽席其內自黃虞
以來不大受兵燹厥土所出
無丹青赭堊瑊玏南金之屬
可當於蜀漢無珠琲翠翹朱
===
提鞨靺之珍可當於南海六
詔無竹箭霧阿阿錫綺紈之
美可當於會稽三吳即所稱
任土作貢廑廑若信之赫蹏
饒之陶型而已蓋倚天之匡
廬黏天之彭蠡不為物產效
而盡以融凝鬯泄於人文自
punctuated: 胡此都人士之盛歟？天下中原之地，敝於四爭，而其餘皆以海墺荒陬為徼。獨此地沃壤四包，而衽席其內，自黃、虞以來，不大受兵燹。厥土所出，無丹青、赭堊、瑊玏、南金之屬可當於蜀漢，無珠琲、翠翹、朱提、鞨靺之珍可當於南海、六詔，無竹箭、霧阿、阿錫、綺紈之美可當於會稽、三吳；即所稱「任土作貢」，廑廑若信之赫蹏、饒之陶型而已。蓋倚天之匡廬，黏天之彭蠡，不為物產效，而盡以融凝鬯泄於人文。自
translation_en: … Why is the flourishing of the gentlemen of this metropolis so great? The Central Plains of the realm have been exhausted by contention from all four directions, while the remaining regions all have coastal reaches and desolate corners as their borders. This land alone is encircled on all four sides by fertile soil and rests within as if upon a sleeping mat; since the days of the Yellow Emperor and Shun of Yu, it has not suffered greatly from the ravages of war. As for what its soil produces, there are no pigments of cinnabar and azurite, red ochre and white clay, jade-like stones, or southern metals to match those of Shu and Hanzhong; no treasures of strung pearls, kingfisher feathers, Zhuti silver, or Mohe rubies to match those of the Southern Sea and the Six Zhao; and no fine things such as bamboo arrows, mist-thin silks, fine linens, orpatterned and white silks to match those of Guiji and the Three Wu. Even what is referred to as "presenting tribute according to local products" amounts barely to the thin paper of Xinzhou and the ceramic wares of Raozhou, and nothing more. Indeed, Mount Kuanglu leaning against the heavens and Lake Pengli joining with the sky do not expend their efficacy on material products, but instead fuse, condense, and pour it all forth into human culture. Since…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
高皇帝定洪都有天下而此邦之
士常爲天下選其盛至於正
德己卯之歲而微中於陽九
元二之數維時宗子內訌潢
池弄兵楚之東蓋岌岌然然
而館閣之臣見微而逆拒搢
紳之士毀家而從戎斯亦足
===
明得士之效已
世廟中興南紀敉寧以及
三朝煦覆而齒息之又六十年而
爲今
皇帝之己卯頒白之老目不識兵
革徒見夫穹然高者爲匡山
黝然深者爲彭湖卽求往日
punctuated: 高皇帝定洪都，有天下，而此邦之士常爲天下選。其盛至於正德己卯之歲，而微中於陽九、元二之數。維時宗子內訌，潢池弄兵，楚之東蓋岌岌然。然而館閣之臣見微而逆拒，搢紳之士毀家而從戎，斯亦足明得士之效已。世廟中興，南紀敉寧，以及三朝煦覆而齒息之。又六十年而爲今皇帝之己卯，頒白之老，目不識兵革，徒見夫穹然高者爲匡山，黝然深者爲彭湖，卽求往日
translation_en:
… the Exalted Emperor (Gao Huangdi, i.e., Emperor Taizu) pacified Hongdu (Nanchang) and came to possess the empire, the scholars of this region have regularly been the pick of the realm. Their flourishing reached the jimao year of the Zhengde reign (1519), when it was slightly struck by a cycle of calamity and misfortune. At that time, a royal clansman (i.e., Zhu Chenhao, Prince of Ning) stirred up internal rebellion and played with weapons in the imperial ponds, so that the region east of Chu was in great peril. Yet ministers of the Hanlin Academy and Grand Secretariat perceived the subtle signs and resisted in advance, while gentry scholars ruined their family fortunes to join the military campaign; this too is enough to demonstrate the efficacy of obtaining worthy scholars.

With the dynastic revival under the Shizong Temple (Emperor Shizong), the southern regions were brought to peace, and down through three reigns the court has warmly sheltered and nurtured them to multiply and rest. Another sixty years have passed to reach the jimao year (1579) of the present Emperor. Gray-haired elders do not know the sight of weapons and armor; they merely see that which rises loftily like a vault as Mount Kuang (Mount Lu), and that which lies darkly deep as Lake Peng (Poyang Lake). Even if one looks for the places of past days where…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
嚚奴之所而無能言者士之
戴
上恩良厚矣牢騷仳離之感無迫
乎其中而家絃人誦以求中
於上之所任使上者談性命
稱節義以傳於鄉之先達而
下者亦攻爲一切佔畢之業
===
以覬于升斗自致之路語有
之荆山之下以玉抵鵲彭蠡
之濱以魚食犬夫士有浮於
額而不盡登耳此邦之所患
寧少文哉成孚不佞獲副兹
典與有一日之長則請以而
土之產爲而多士告今夫赫
punctuated: 嚚奴之所，而無能言者。士之戴上恩良厚矣！牢騷仳離之感無迫乎其中，而家絃人誦，以求中於上之所任使。上者談性命、稱節義，以傳於鄉之先達；而下者亦攻爲一切佔畢之業，以覬于升斗自致之路。語有之：「荆山之下，以玉抵鵲；彭蠡之濱，以魚食犬。」夫士有浮於額而不盡登耳，此邦之所患，寧少文哉？成孚不佞，獲副兹典，與有一日之長，則請以而土之產爲而多士告：今夫赫
translation_en: …the lairs of the recalcitrant rebels, there is no one who can even name them. The scholars here truly enjoy the profound grace of the Emperor! Feelings of grievance and the sorrow of separation do not press upon their hearts; instead, every household plays stringed instruments and every person chants the classics, seeking to meet the requirements for imperial service. The superior among them discourse on human nature and destiny and extol moral integrity and righteousness, passing on the traditions of the former worthies of their native place; while the lesser among them also apply themselves to all manner of rote textual study, hoping for a path to advance themselves and earn a modest official stipend. As the saying goes: "At the foot of Mount Jing, people pelt magpies with jade; on the shores of Lake Pengli, people feed dogs with fish." Indeed, the worthy scholars here exceed the quota and cannot all be placed on the list of successful candidates; how could a scarcity of literary talent ever be what troubles this region? Unworthy as I, Chengfu, am, having had the privilege of serving as the associate examiner in this grand ceremony and holding a slight advantage in seniority over you, allow me to address you many scholars by drawing an analogy from the products of your own land. Take, for instance, the fine paper [hehao, a print variant of xihao 赫蹏]…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
號之在信也陶型之在饒也
其質皆任之於天而其力恒
盡之于人木採而楮山採而
土沃以流泉鍛以大火日取
而不稱竭焉足也材堅而完
體質而素然後染以五彩被
以丹青華而不稱靡焉實也
===
大之以供軍國輸尚方下及
乎萌隷以為日用飲食之需
罔不稱利賴焉適也是二者
之用於世則誠切矣夫士國
之所謂南金大寶也其為用
豈直於為紙為陶而已行將
為縣官匠鑄萬有衣被黎庶
punctuated: 號之在信也，陶型之在饒也，其質皆任之於天，而其力恒盡之于人。木採而楮，山採而土，沃以流泉，鍛以大火，日取而不稱竭焉，足也；材堅而完，體質而素，然後染以五彩，被以丹青，華而不稱靡焉，實也；大之以供軍國、輸尚方，下及乎萌隷，以為日用飲食之需，罔不稱利賴焉，適也。是二者之用於世，則誠切矣。夫士，國之所謂南金、大寶也，其為用豈直於為紙、為陶而已？行將為縣官匠鑄萬有，衣被黎庶，
translation_en: … paper [赫蹏, transcribed 赫號] in Xin [Guangxin] and molded pottery in Rao [Raozhou], their raw substance is in both cases entrusted to Heaven, while the effort is invariably exhausted by human hands. From trees they gather mulberry bark, and from the hills they dig clay; they soak them in flowing springs and fire them over great flames. Taken daily, they are never spoken of as exhausted—that is their sufficiency. Their material is firm and intact, their body plain and unadorned, and only afterward are they dyed with the five colors and overlaid with vermilion and azure; they are splendid, yet never spoken of as extravagant—that is their substance. At the highest level, they supply the military and the state and are presented as tribute to the Imperial Manufactories (Shangfang); down to the common folk and menials, they serve the needs of daily use and of food and drink, and none fail to speak of their benefit and reliance upon them—that is their suitability. The utility of these two things in the world is truly immediate and vital! Now scholars are what the state calls its "southern gold" and its "great treasure." How could their utility merely match that of making paper or making pottery? Before long, on behalf of the sovereign, they will mold and cast all things and clothe and shelter the common people…

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
乃其所樹建將無有淺中而
不足於求者乎外澤而不麗
於實者乎一曲一偏而不適
於用者乎有一於茲是寶其
名而其用顧出於赫蹏陶型
之下也玉巵之無當土缶之
弗如而多士其性命之談而
===
務實之以學節義之稱而思
蹈之於道異日效於世而裒
然有稱曰某某某所取士也
則不佞席有榮焉毋寧使人
謂子利器之求而無當於好
用之式猥以𨾏為工師者罪
也而多士其幸勗之
punctuated: 乃其所樹建，將無有淺中而不足於求者乎？外澤而不麗於實者乎？一曲一偏而不適於用者乎？有一於茲，是寶其名而其用顧出於赫蹏、陶型之下也。玉巵之無當，土缶之弗如。而多士其性命之談而務實之以學，節義之稱而思蹈之於道。異日效於世，而裒然有稱曰：「某某，某所取士也。」則不佞席有榮焉。毋寧使人謂子利器之求而無當於好用之式，猥以𨾏為工師者罪也。而多士其幸勗之！
translation_en:
… that constitutes their achievements! Yet might there not be among you some who are shallow within and fall short of what is sought from them? Some who are glossy on the outside yet fail to adhere to substance? Some who are one-sided and partial, unsuited for practical use? If you have even one of these flaws, then although you bear the name of a treasure, your usefulness will actually rank below that of thin paper and molded pottery. A jade goblet without a bottom is not as good as an earthen jar.

Therefore, in your discussions of human nature and destiny, you many scholars should strive to substantiate them through learning; in your praise of integrity and righteousness, you should take thought to tread them in the Way. When in days to come you render service to the world and win outstanding renown, so that people say, "So-and-so was a scholar selected by so-and-so," then I, unworthy as I am, will share in the honor of my post. Rather than let people say that in seeking fine vessels you failed to meet the standard of good utility, thus unjustly bringing blame upon the master artisans, I pray that you many scholars will exert yourselves!

title: 萬曆七年江西鄉試錄
text:
直隸蘇州府嘉定縣儒學敎
諭趙成孚謹序
punctuated: 直隸蘇州府嘉定縣儒學敎諭趙成孚謹序。
translation_en: Respectfully written as a postface by Zhao Chengfu 趙成孚, Instructor of the Confucian School of Jiading County in Suzhou Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area.
